SPECIFIC

T_S: exactly as in scapula-halo-track (iso-motion loop from skin_motion_map_14.json, radius from K3 in RS, running surface at rho_S, underside at rho_S - 5).

T_H, first pass:
- Run the halo-track closure (seed W wdir(115,-18), a2 55, or W wdir(75,54), a2 115). Record the J2 pole in the humerus frame, RH^T p2.
- T_H = the arc of the circle {angle(v, W) = a2} covering the visited range + 15 deg at each end, 2 deg samples.
- Variant: the deltoid oval wdir(95 + 30 cos t, -10 + 60 sin t).

T_H running radius:
- rho_H(t) = max(K3 requirement in RH + 5, max over poses where T_H(t) comes within 8 mm (angularly) of a T_S sample of rho_S + 9 + 5).
- In words: lift the arm track wherever it can pass over the halo. Its underside is at rho_H - 5.

Closure per pose:
- The crossing = min over (az, t) of angle(RS u(az), RH v(t)), required <= 0.5 deg; refine on a finer grid.
- Transversality: the angle between the two track tangents at the crossing must be >= 20 deg, else None.
- p2 = the crossing direction. Branch = the crossing nearest the previous frame (K2).

Swivel block:
- Carriage A at [rho_S - 5, rho_S + 4], carriage B at [rho_H - 5, rho_H + 4], each 20 x 16 mm.
- Passive slide L = rho_H - rho_S - 9 must be in [0, 25] mm, else None.

Metal samples: both track undersides (8 mm wide) and carriage A's underside.

Collisions:
- T_H vs T_S: radial intervals must not overlap where the tracks are angularly within 8 mm.
- T_H vs the body: through B.dist (contact = not taken).
sweep_params:
- Halo contour: thr 13/20, el offset.
- T_H: W and a2 of the arm circle, or oval centre and semi-axes, or a 2-harmonic perturbation.
- Swivel stack: 9-13 mm.
- Quantile q.
prior_art: Crossed circular guides realise orientations in two-arc stereotactic frames (Leksell arc + ring) and gimbal arc positioners. I know of no wearable that uses two skin-fixed tracks crossing at a radial swivel.

name: Rail elbow: J2 is a curved rail on link 1, so link 2 shrinks to a carriage beside the arm-end hub
topology:
- Scapula base (S).
- J1 ACTIVE: O20 hub, axis b on scapula skin a hub can sit on (radial ray within 30 deg of the skin normal).
- Link 1: a strap from J1 plus a circular rail arc fixed on link 1, concentric with the J2 axis p2 through GH. The rail lies on the circle at angular radius a2 + d_off about p2: the locus of the J3 pole relative to link 1, offset sideways by d_off so it runs beside the J3 hub. There is no hub at p2's pole.
- J2 ACTIVE: a rolling carriage on the rail; the rotation about p2 is the joint value.
- Link 2 = the carriage + a 15 mm bridge to J3's upper plate.
- J3 ACTIVE: O20 hub at W, fixed to the arm on a deltoid-cap spot a hub can sit on (delta 75-115, e.g. the low-motion spot (112, -15)).
- Arm-end plate + neck to BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning: Same kinematics as a spherical 3R (b, a1, a2, W): q1, q2 (carriage angle about p2) and q3 all follow from the two-circle closure, with no spare coordinate. Only the physical form of J2 changes. A revolute joint needs no metal on its axis: the rotation about p2 is carried by a rail on a circle about p2.
description:
Rest:
- The J1 hub sits on the lateral or posterior acromion. Link 1 is a short strap to a curved rail: 140-190 deg of a circle of radius about 45-55 mm about the J2 axis, section 8 x 5 mm.
- The rail lies over the deltoid cap and posterior shoulder, about 60-65 mm from GH.
- The carriage sits next to the J3 hub on the top-lateral deltoid. There is no metal at J2's pole.

Overhead: the rail on link 1 swings with q1 over the shoulder top while the carriage runs along it; the arm-end hub stays on the deltoid cap. Across-body and behind-back: the carriage reaches the rail's ends (the extremes of the J2 angle).
why_better:
It deletes the baseline's two worst members at once:
- The J2 hub zone: 18.4 pts of R1 lost, 0.7 % in band, and unfixable by shape.
- Link 2's ribbon: 16.1 pts.

Link 2 becomes a 20 mm carriage next to the arm-end hub, which sits on the best arm spot. The rail is a thin band at constant radius. Where it lies over the round deltoid cap (radius spread about 4.7 mm), it stays in band at any rotation. The arcs and axes stay those of a proven 3R, so the comparison with the baseline isolates the J2 realisation.
main_risk:
- J2 travel: the J2 angle spans 94 deg on the clips but 159 deg over the functional workspace for the r18 chain (17-176 deg). For the layouts with the best singularity margin it spans 119-133 deg (computed).
- The rail is therefore a 140-190 deg arc plus carriage on link 1: long intermediate metal that swings with q1 and must clear the arm and the acromion in every pose.
- At constant radius it stands off where the skin under it is not the deltoid cap.
- Its free ends are cantilevers (stiffness).
unpowered_and_mvp2:
Unpowered: a rolling carriage (4 MR63 V-rollers on a V-edged Ti rail, or a caged wire-race segment). J2 has no hub friction and nothing is free.

MVP2: a cable groove along the rail (a pull along the arc) drives the carriage, with a magnetic strip for q2. J1 and J3 are hubs with drums.

Kinematics: K1 with (b, a1, a2, W, sigma).
- Seed A: r18 s1392 #1: b=bvec(32.55,80.56), W=wdir(71.38,4.78), a=(77.41,81.45), sigma=-1.
- Seed B: the same with W=wdir(112,-15).

Link 1 frame: L1 = [b, e1, b x e1], e1 = norm(p2 - (p2.b) b).

Rail:
- The circle C2 = {x : angle(x, p2) = a2 + d_off}.
- Carriage azimuth psi = azimuth of w about p2, measured from norm(b - (b.p2) p2).
- Rail extent = [psi_min - 15, psi_max + 15] over the fit poses (first pass), sampled every 2 mm.
- Running radius rho_T: one constant = max over rail samples and fit poses of the K3 requirement + 5. The underside is at rho_T - 5, 8 mm wide.
- The rail must clear the J3 hub. Either the angular distance of the rail to w is >= (10+4+4)/rho_T rad, which needs |d_off| >= about 16 deg; or, with d_off = 0, the rail passes over the J3 cap: rho_T - 5 >= F3 + 12.25 + 0.5.

Carriage: a 20 x 16 mm block at [rho_T - 5, rho_T + 4] at psi, plus a bridge strap (K5) to the J3 upper plate.

J3: K4 hub with axis w. The lower member is the arm-end plate (RH, K3); the bridge sits at F3 + 3.15. Neck to BOTTOM per K7.

J1: K4 hub with axis b. The base plate (RS) is the lower member and link 1 the upper. The link 1 strap runs from J1 to the rail's mid-point (great circle), K3 in L1.

sweep_params:
- b: scapula skin within 30 deg of normal, az 0-180, el 20-75.
- W: delta 75-115, az -40..55.
- a1, a2: 55-100 deg.
- d_off: -20 / 0 / +20 deg.
- Branch sigma.
- Quantile q.
prior_art: Circular-guide joints for exo DOFs whose axis cannot carry a hub: the humeral-rotation C-rails of ARMin III and ANYexo, and the arc guides of RCM surgical robots. Here the idea is applied to the middle joint of a spherical 3R.

name: Rolling-cone elbow: J2 is a pair of strap-bound cones rolling about GH, with no hub
topology:
- Scapula base (S).
- J1 ACTIVE: O20 hub, axis b.
- Link 1 ends in a 'sun' conical rim: axis s fixed in link 1, half-angle alpha1, apex at GH.
- J2 ACTIVE: no-slip rolling contact with link 2's 'planet' conical rim (axis c, half-angle alpha2, external contact angle(s, c) = alpha1 + alpha2). Two or three crossed 0.1 mm steel straps hold the pair together, Jacob's-ladder style. It is a 1-DOF spherical joint whose instantaneous axis is the contact generator through GH.
- Link 2.
- J3 ACTIVE: O20 hub at W (deltoid cap, delta 75-115).
- Arm-end plate + neck to BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning:
There are three coordinates (q1, rolling angle psi, q3).
- The rolling pair has exactly one DOF (no slip + contact + straps); the straps add no DOF.
- Its relative motion is M(psi) = R(s, psi) R(c0, k psi) with k = sin(alpha1)/sin(alpha2): a rotation about the moving contact line through GH. The chain therefore stays spherical about GH.
- The arm's three orientation DOF fix (q1, psi, q3) through a 1-D root in psi. No spare coordinate.
description:
Rest: the J1 hub sits on the acromion. Link 1 runs to a standing curved rim (an 8 mm tall, 2 mm thick conical band, radially oriented, 60-90 mm long) over the posterior-lateral shoulder. Link 2's rim rolls on it and link 2 continues to the J3 hub on the deltoid cap. The chain's 'elbow' is two thin rims touching along a radial line: no hub, no cap.

Overhead and across-body: the planet rim rolls along the sun rim. Each rim needs only about half the arc that a rail of the same J2 travel would, because both surfaces move.
why_better:
- It removes the 12.25 mm J2 hub stack and its 20 mm disc, the baseline's worst zone (18 pts of R1, 0.7 % in band). In their place stand two 2 mm rims on edge: almost no skin-facing area at the elbow, and nothing tall for link 2 or the arm to hit. FINDINGS: joint size is worth about 20 points of workspace.
- Rolling contact has near-zero friction (R17) and no bearing play.
- Because the elbow's axis migrates, the chain's singularity set is not the 3R's coplanarity set. This is a new place to put the singularity.
main_risk:
- Novel and fiddly. The cones must stay in contact under every load direction: straps take tension one way and contact the other, so it needs crossed straps on both sides plus preload.
- The rims stand 8 mm radially and still need skin clearance.
- Slip under load would corrupt the angle reading.
- Fatigue of 0.1 mm straps over 10^6 cycles.
- The singularity map has to be built from scratch.
- Sensing psi needs an encoder on the rolling pair.
unpowered_and_mvp2:
Unpowered: pure rolling plus strap bending (a few mN.m), no lubricant, no play, nothing free.

MVP2: a cable wrapped on the sun rim (a capstan on a cone) drives psi. psi is read by a magnetic strip on the planet rim. J1 and J3 are hubs with drums.

K4 O20 hub (docs/HARDWARE.md v5).
- A flat disc of radius 10 mm perpendicular to its axis k, lower face at distance h_F along k.
- h_F = max over the disc samples (2 mm grid) and fit poses of the K3 requirement projected on k.
- The skin-facing samples are the disc.
- Lower member [F, F+3]; upper member underside at F+3.15; crown at F+12.25.

- Each member is its samples with radial intervals [rho, rho+t].
- Two members that do not share a joint collide if two samples are within (half-widths+1 mm)/rho rad and their intervals overlap (+0.5 mm).
- Joint partners are exempt within hub radius+2 mm of their joint.

- Neck: a 14 x 6 mm strap from the arm-end plate to BOTTOM's bar. In the humerus frame the bar normal is Wb=(0,-0.0713,0.9975), its underside is 67.5 mm out along Wb, and it runs along Db=(0,-0.9975,-0.0713) from about 40 mm down. Fit with K3 in RH.

SPECIFIC

Parameters:
- b (scapula frame).
- Link 1 reference frame L1_0, containing b and the sun axis s0, with beta1 = angle(b, s0).
- alpha1, alpha2.
- The planet axis at psi = 0: c0 = R(s0, gamma) applied to the direction at angle alpha1 + alpha2 from s0 in the (b, s0) plane.
- W's direction in link 2 coordinates: w2, at angle beta2 from c0 and azimuth gamma2.

Relative motion (link 1 coordinates):
- M(psi) = R(s0, psi) @ R(c0, k psi), k = sin(alpha1)/sin(alpha2).
- Check numerically that the contact generator g(psi) = R(s0, psi) g0, with g0 = (sin(alpha2) s0 + sin(alpha1) c0)/sin(alpha1+alpha2), has zero relative velocity.

IK per pose:
- w = RH W, theta = angle(RS b_S, w).
- v(psi) = RS L1_0 M(psi) w2 (that is, q1 = 0).
- Solve angle(b, v(psi)) = theta on a 1 deg psi grid within [psi_min, psi_max], then bisect. Take the root on the design's branch, or the one nearest the previous clip frame (K2).
- q1 = the signed angle about b that takes v(psi) to w.
- q3 = the remaining twist at the arm end.
- Link 1 = R(b, q1) L1_0; link 2 = link1 M(psi) L2_0.

Members:
- Link 1 = a strap from J1 (K4 hub, base plate lower) to the sun rim, plus the sun rim itself: a cone band with apex GH, axis s, half-angle alpha1, radial extent [rho_c, rho_c+8], over the contact angles visited +-10 deg. Sample its foot line at rho_c every 2 mm, 2 mm wide.
- Link 2 = the planet rim (same radial band, over k x the visited range) plus a strap to the J3 hub (K4, arm-end plate lower), plus the neck (K7).
- rho_c = the K3 requirement over the rims' directions.
- Collisions per K6, except between the two rims along the contact generator. The straps holding the rims together are not modelled.

- alpha1, alpha2: 20-60 deg.
- beta1, beta2, gamma, gamma2.
- b; W: delta 75-115.
- rho_c lift.
- Branch.
- Quantile q.
prior_art:
Rolling-contact joints:
- Cross-strap / Jacob's-ladder hinges.
- CORE rolling-contact joints (Cannon and Howell 2005).
- The Rolamite.
- Rolling-contact knee and finger orthoses.

A spherical cone-on-cone pair is the gearless analogue of bevel gears. I know of no shoulder exo that uses one as the middle joint of a spherical chain.

name: 2R pointing gimbal with its singularity in a home + humeral rotation on a C-rail on the deltoid sphere (the user's split)
topology:
- Scapula base (S).
- J1 ACTIVE: O20 hub, axis u on the 'singular home' line: in the scapula frame, the line the humerus never comes near.
- Link 1 (arc 90).
- J2 ACTIVE: O20 hub, axis v = norm(u x d), perpendicular to J1 and to the humerus axis d.
- Link 2: a yoke that points along the humerus but does not twist with it. It carries a C-rail: a latitude circle about d on the sphere centred at GH, at angular radius phi of about 50-70 deg from the distal humerus axis and radius about 60-64 mm, open on the medial (axilla) side.
- J3 ACTIVE: humeral rotation, as an arm-fixed carriage on the cuff / BOTTOM top block (lateral deltoid) running on the C-rail.
dof_reasoning:
- J1 and J2 point link 2 along the humerus: two DOF in closed form, q1 = azimuth of d about u, q2 = angle(u, d).
- J3 is the arm's twist about d relative to link 2: atan2((v x p).d, v.p), with p an arm-fixed perpendicular such as the epicondyle axis.
- All three are set by the arm; none is spare.

This is the user's own suggestion: 'put upper arm rotation in its own DOF farther down from the shoulder and just have to handle 2 at the shoulder joint'.
description:
Rest:
- The J1 hub sits on the anterior-superior-lateral acromion: u_S = (0.37, 0.74, 0.56), the line the humerus stays at least 32 deg from over the whole bench workspace.
- The J2 hub is posterior-lateral (v = u x d).
- Link 2 is a yoke from J2 over the deltoid cap. It carries a 180-210 deg C-rail around the deltoid about 30 mm below GH, covering lateral, anterior and posterior, and open toward the axilla.
- The arm's carriage sits at the lateral deltoid.

Overhead: link 2 rotates up with the humerus; the rail stays on the deltoid cap with its opening facing the neck. Across-body and behind-back: the carriage runs to the front or back end of the rail (internal or external rotation).
why_better:
It puts the singularity where the arm never goes.
- The 2R singularity is humerus || u. The best u keeps a 32 deg margin over the full functional workspace (46 deg on the clips).
- The baseline 3R's band is [4, 159] deg and its own workspace crosses it: 3.2 % of workspace poses do not close and the fold margin is 13 deg (computed on the bench poses).

It also moves humeral rotation onto a separate rail.
- Humeral rotation is the largest and most twisting part of the workspace.
- The rail rides the one region of the arm that is round about GH, the deltoid cap (radius spread about 4.7 mm). J1, J2 and their links never chase axial rotation.
main_risk:
Twist travel. Relative to the gimbal, the arm twists over a huge range in the functional workspace (computed):
- |q3| <= 75 deg covers 77-82 %, <= 90 deg covers 87-91 %, <= 120 deg covers 95 %. On the clips, 100 % is within 90 deg.
- A rail longer than about 200 deg must pass the axilla and chest. Expect at most about 85-90 % reach kinematically, and less once contact counts.

Other risks:
- The C-rail plus carriage stack is about 10 mm on the deltoid.
- The rail turns with link 2 over arm skin that twists under it. The arm is non-round below the cap: 13.5-25 mm spread (FINDINGS).
- The J1 hub's home (anterior-superior acromion) has 22-39 mm of skin motion in the scapula frame.
- Asking for better twist coverage moves u to (0.04, 0.25, 0.97), which is lateral and on arm skin at rest, with only a 21 deg margin.
unpowered_and_mvp2:
Unpowered: J1 and J2 are preloaded O20 hubs. The C-rail uses a caged wire-race carriage (ring_and_shell_hardware.md options A/B, about 10 mm stack). All three joints are set by the arm. The gimbal's near-singular speed factor 1/sin(margin) is at most 1.9 at 32 deg.

MVP2: J1 and J2 have hub drums. J3 is driven by a cable in the rail groove, as in ARMin and ANYexo humeral rotation, and read by a magnetic strip.

SPECIFIC

Arm directions:
- d = RH @ e_h, with e_h = the normalised L['elbow'] from pipeline/avg/body_mesh.json landmarks (the GH -> elbow direction in the humerus frame).
- p = RH @ (L['elbow_axis'] made perpendicular to e_h, normalised).

J1 axis: u = RS @ u_S. Search u_S over a 4000-point Fibonacci sphere.
- Either maximise min over all bench poses of angle(+-u_S, RS^T d). Seed: (0.368, 0.743, 0.56), 32.2 deg.
- Or maximise twist coverage subject to margin >= 20/25/30 deg. Seeds: (0.04, 0.25, 0.97), (0.28, 0.53, 0.80), (0.38, 0.70, 0.61).
- Put the J1 hub (K4) at whichever of +-u exits the body clear of other skin.

J2: v = norm(u x d). Pick the sign whose pole is outside the body and keep it continuous along each clip. J2 hub (K4) at v's pole.

Link 1: a strap J1 -> J2 along the great circle (90 deg), K3 in the frame [u, v, u x v].

Link 2: frame [d, v, d x v]. A strap from J2 to the rail's mid-point.

C-rail:
- The circle {x : angle(x, d) = phi} at radius rho_r. Azimuth about d is measured from v.
- Range [c - T/2 - 15, c + T/2 + 15], with travel T = 150-210 deg and rail centre c.
- Section 8 mm wide x 5 mm radial.
- rho_r: one constant = max over rail samples and fit poses of the K3 requirement + 5.

J3: q3 = atan2((v x p).d, v.p). The pose is not taken if |wrap(q3 - c)| > T/2.

Arm end:
- The carriage is fixed to the arm: a 30 deg x 16 mm x 9 mm block at a fixed lateral azimuth in RH, on the rail.
- The carriage plus a short neck to BOTTOM (K7) is the arm-end metal (K3 in RH).

Collisions (K6): rail vs J2 hub, rail vs base, link 2 vs neck, rail vs body (B.dist).
sweep_params:
- u: margin 20-32 deg against twist coverage.
- Rail latitude phi: 45-75 deg; rail radius.
- Rail travel T: 150-210 deg; rail centre c.
- Carriage azimuth.
- Quantile q.
prior_art:
- ARMin III, ANYexo, Harmony and the MGA exoskeleton handle humeral rotation as a separate joint on a curved bearing around the upper arm.
- The 2R pointing + axial decomposition is the ISB Y-X-Y convention.
- FINDINGS 'Humeral-rotation ring' studied a ring fixed to the arm 64 mm down the humerus, with only a 124-130 deg window free of the body.

This version puts the rail on the non-twisting link 2 at the deltoid-cap latitude and places u by the singular-home search.

name: Open-centre ring joints: all three joints as thin-section rings around their poles, so bumps rise into the hole
topology:
A spherical 3R with every axis through GH; only the joints change.
- Scapula base (S).
- J1 ACTIVE: a thin-section ring bearing (wire-race or Kaydon KAA-type, mean radius r_m 14-24 mm, 5 x 5 mm section), concentric with axis b and lying on the sphere around b's pole with an open centre. The inner race is the lower member and the outer race the upper member, at the same height.
- Link 1: a strap between the ring rims.
- J2 ACTIVE: a ring about p2.
- Link 2.
- J3 ACTIVE: a ring about W (arm-fixed).
- Arm-end + neck to BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning: Exactly a spherical 3R: q1, q2, q3 from the two-circle closure, with no spare coordinate. A ring bearing is a revolute joint whose rolling elements run on a circle around the axis instead of on a pin at the axis.
description:
Rest:
- Three rings of 30-50 mm, each a 5 mm-tall annulus around its pole.
- J1's ring circles the acromion summit, so the bony peak sits inside the open centre.
- J3's ring circles the most bulging point of the deltoid cap, so the bulge rises into the centre when the deltoid fires.
- The links are short straps between ring rims. There is no pin and no dome cap anywhere.

Overhead and other poses: as the baseline 3R family (same kinematics, r18/r20 seeds). But every joint is about 9 mm tall instead of 12.25 mm, and has a hole where a flat hub disc would sit on a bump.
why_better:
It attacks the hub directly.
- The O20 stack is 12.25 mm from the lower face to the crown, and its flat face must clear the highest skin under it.
- A ring's skin-facing metal is an annulus with an axisymmetric underside that follows the skin, and the local bump (acromion summit, deltoid belly) can rise into its open centre. Its crown is about 9 mm.
- The lower crown reduces the link-over-hub and link-vs-hub collisions that cost the stacked designs range.
- It tests a claim directly: 'joints on bumps should be rings, not discs'.
main_risk:
- Larger footprint: OD 35-48 mm against 20 mm. The evaluator found that a larger hub radius costs about 20 points of workspace (O17 vs O23), because flat discs ride high on curved skin. The ring must win that back with its axisymmetric open annulus, or it loses.
- Mass: 6-18 g per ring. A preloaded thin-section ring needs a stiff housing, and the housing sets the real stack.
- A cable drum on a 48 mm ring is large. Torque is not the problem: for MVP2's ~10 N.m, a KAA15 ring has a 40 N.m static moment rating.
unpowered_and_mvp2:
Unpowered: four-point-contact thin-section rings, friction about 0.1 N.m (ring_and_shell_hardware.md); nothing is free.

MVP2: the outer race carries the cable groove. At a pitch radius of about 24 mm the cable sees about 420 N at 10 N.m, less than the O20's 950 N. Sensing is a thin magnetic ring encoder in the race.

name: Posterior max-margin Cardan: the orthogonal 3R with the largest possible singularity margin, wrapped behind the shoulder
topology:
- Scapula base (S), low on the infraspinatus.
- J1 ACTIVE: O20 hub with a wedge or skin-normal seat, axis b = bvec(-28, -19) (posterior-inferior-medial).
- Link 1: a 90 deg strap up the back of the scapula.
- J2 ACTIVE: O20 hub at the common perpendicular, p2 = +(b x w)/|b x w|. On this branch it rides the posterior-superior shoulder: scapula-frame az 45-60, el 30-40, about 50 mm from GH.
- Link 2: a 90 deg strap down the posterior deltoid.
- J3 ACTIVE: O20 hub with a wedge seat, W = wdir(42, -64) on the posterior upper arm.
- Arm-end + neck to BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning:
A spherical 3R with a1 = a2 = 90 (a Cardan). p2 = sigma (b x w)/|b x w| in closed form, q2 = theta = angle(b, w), and q1, q3 follow; there is no spare coordinate.

For any spherical 3R the best possible singularity margin over the arcs is reached at 90/90, and then it equals the distance of w from the line b. This placement maximises it over the whole functional workspace: 32.6-34.6 deg (computed over the bench poses, Fibonacci search over b and W). The baseline has a 13 deg fold margin and 3.2 % of the workspace beyond its extended singularity.
description:
Everything sits behind the frontal plane:
- J1 is low on the back of the scapula, 119-135 mm from GH.
- Link 1 runs up the infraspinatus to J2 on the posterior acromion and scapular spine. Under J2 the scapula-frame skin moves a median of 10 mm (p90 38-49 mm), against 29 mm (p90 71 mm) for the baseline's J2.
- Link 2 runs down the posterior deltoid to J3 on the posterior upper arm, 109-125 mm from GH.

The front and top of the shoulder are empty: overhead and across-body, nothing is in front of or above the acromion. Reaching behind the back, the arm swings toward the chain (the main risk).
why_better:
It is range-first by construction:
- It is the global optimum of the singularity margin for any spherical 3R over the bench's functional workspace. Kinematic closure is 100 %, with theta 30-149 deg.
- Its J2 pole lives over the low-motion posterior-superior scapula skin.

Those are the two things that limit the baseline (singularity crossing, and J2 over moving skin), addressed at once. It is also the calibration point that tells the bench whether singularity margin or skin matters more.
main_risk:
Hub obliquity:
- At both end poles the radial rays meet the skin about 49 deg off the normal (back of the scapula, posterior arm), 110-135 mm from GH. J1 and J3 therefore need wedge or tilted seats that add stack.
- If hubs are restricted to skin within 30 deg of the normal and moving at most 15-25 mm, the best margin drops to 15-17 deg (computed).

Other risks:
- Long links, about 150 mm each.
- Posterior arm skin moves 26-58 mm in the humerus frame: bad ground for J3.
- Behind-back reaches squeeze link 2 between the arm and the back.
unpowered_and_mvp2:
Unpowered: three O20 hubs, nothing free. A Cardan is well conditioned away from its singular line: the speed factor 1/sin(32 deg) is at most 1.9.

MVP2: cables to three hubs. J1 on the back is the shortest cable route to a motor pack worn on the back.

- These match band_impl.bvec and w_dir.

K1 Two-circle closure.
- c=b.w, n=(b x w)/|b x w|.
- A=(cos a1 - c cos a2)/(1-c^2), Bq=(cos a2 - c cos a1)/(1-c^2).
- p0=A b+Bq w, h2=1-|p0|^2. If h2<=0 there is no closure -> None.
- p2=p0+sigma*sqrt(h2)*n, with sigma=+-1 fixed per design.
- margin=min(theta-|a1-a2|, a1+a2-theta, 360-a1-a2-theta), theta=acos c. margin<5 deg -> None.

K2 Continuity. Walk B.clip_order(). A clip frame whose joint values jump more than 25 deg from the previous taken frame is a branch flip -> None.

K3 Rigid skin-fitted underside.
- A member is a set of unit directions u_j in its own frame, spaced 2 mm at its height and across its width.
- Per pose, the requirement r_i(d) = the first t on a 1 mm march (15-220 mm) along d with B.dist(i, t d) >= 2.0 and >= 0 over [t, t+15]. Vectorise over all samples.
- rho_j = quantile_q over the fit poses of r_i(R_member,i u_j). Fit poses = all poses the chain closes in, clip and ws. q=1.0 by default; q=0.97 or 0.93 lets the worst poses become contact poses.
- Metal = rho_j R_member u_j. B.dist then decides contact.

K4 O20 hub (docs/HARDWARE.md v5).
- A flat disc of radius 10 mm perpendicular to its axis k, lower face at distance h_F along k.
- h_F = max over the disc samples (2 mm grid) and fit poses of the K3 requirement projected on k.
- The skin-facing samples are the disc.
- Lower member [F, F+3]; upper member underside at F+3.15; crown at F+12.25.

K5 Strap. 12 mm wide, 3 mm thick (report mass at 5.5 mm too), K3 underside. It may not climb faster than 60 deg from the plane of the hub it leaves.

K6 Collisions.
- Each member is its samples with radial intervals [rho, rho+t].
- Two members that do not share a joint collide if two samples are within (half-widths+1 mm)/rho rad and their intervals overlap (+0.5 mm).
- Joint partners are exempt within hub radius+2 mm of their joint.
- Collision -> None.

K7 Neck and record.
- Neck: a 14 x 6 mm strap from the arm-end plate to BOTTOM's bar. In the humerus frame the bar normal is Wb=(0,-0.0713,0.9975), its underside is 67.5 mm out along Wb, and it runs along Db=(0,-0.9975,-0.0713) from about 40 mm down. Fit with K3 in RH.
- B.record(i, all custom metal samples). That is everything except the user's cuff and BOTTOM.
- Print B.report(), the in-band share per member (B.dist per member) and the Ti mass (4.43 g/cm3).

SPECIFIC

Kinematics: K1 with a1 = a2 = 90, so p2 = sigma (b x w)/|b x w| with sigma = +1.
- Seed: b_S = bvec(-28,-19), W_H = wdir(42,-64).
- Global-optimum seed (34.6 deg): b_S = (-0.76,-0.42,-0.48), W_H = (-0.50,-0.84,0.19).
- Report the margin per pose: min(theta, 180 - theta).

Hubs: K4 with a WEDGE seat.
- The lower face F is the plane perpendicular to k at h_F.
- The lower member's skin-facing underside under the disc is fitted to the skin (K3, in its own frame).
- Wedge height = max - min of that underside under the disc. Report it and count it as stack: crown = max(F + 12.25, top of wedge + 12.25).

Variant, skin-normal tilt (report both):
- Keep the axis through GH.
- Lay the disc samples on the plane through the pole perpendicular to the skin normal averaged over the fit poses.
- Treat the tilt as part of the lower member.

Links: 90 deg straps (K3, K5) in the frames [b, p2, b x p2] and [w, p2, w x p2].

Arm end: plate + neck to BOTTOM (K7), fitted in RH.

Collisions: K6. Watch the behind-back poses: link 2 against the trunk shows up as contact through B.dist.
sweep_params:
- b and W within the top-k set with margin >= 28 deg.
- Branch sigma.
- Hub seat: wedge or skin-normal tilt.
- J2 stacking order.
- Quantile q.
prior_art: Orthogonal-axis (Cardan / Euler) 3R shoulders are standard in rehab exos (MGA, CADEN-7, ARMin). Moving the singularity outside the workspace by tilting the first axis is classic, e.g. the MGA exoskeleton (Carignan et al.).

name: Coaxial 3-RRR spherical parallel 'turret': nested dome rings, force-only legs to one arm saddle
topology: Scapula S (on the user's handler) -> R1a, R1b, R1c: three ACTIVE revolutes on ONE axis A through GH, built as three nested thin-section ring bearings (polar radii 9 / 15 / 21 deg about A, about O17 / O28 / O40 at r 55) on the posterior-top dome -> crank k: a strap leaving ring k along a meridian, arc alpha1 -> R2k: passive elbow pin (O14 single-bearing pin, axis e_k through GH) -> distal link k: strap, arc alpha2 (a two-force member) -> R3k: passive platform pin (O14, arm-fixed axis v_k through GH; a rod-end ball stud is an option) -> one arm-fixed saddle carrying the three platform pins -> neck to the user's BOTTOM bar. 9 joints, all axes through GH. Cuff slides (outside the count) handle GH translation, as for the baseline.
dof_reasoning: Spherical Gruebler: 8 bodies (S, 3 cranks, 3 distal links, arm) and 9 revolutes give M = 3(8-1-9)+9 = 3, the arm's three rotations. Active = the three coaxial ring angles. They are the only coordinates that must be sensed (MVP1) or driven (MVP2). Their forward kinematics has up to 8 assembly modes, held by continuity. Every passive angle is set by closure. Given the arm pose, v_k is known, and the elbow e_k is the intersection of the cone alpha1 about A with the cone alpha2 about v_k (2 branches, fixed by design). Elbow and platform angles are therefore functions of the arm pose, so nothing can sag. The only place a passive coordinate is not set is a leg singularity (A, e_k, v_k coplanar), where an elbow could flip. It is kept outside the range by a margin and an elbow stop. 6 passive pins: flag this against the user's 'as low a joint count as possible'.
description: A small turret of three concentric rings sits on the stable posterior-top dome of the scapula. Three thin legs fan out from it, each bending once at a small elbow pin, and land on three pins of one compact saddle on the upper-lateral arm. REST: the rings are over the supraspinous fossa and acromion top. There, at scapula-frame latitude 40-70, the skin is 37-64 mm from GH and changes by <= 7 mm per direction in my ray casts over rest, abduction 90, scaption 150, flexion 90, cross-body and extension. The elbows sit about 60 deg from A, on the posterior, lateral and anterior rim. The distal straps lie down the deltoid to the saddle. OVERHEAD: the saddle climbs to the lateral dome. Rotation about A is unlimited, so the cranks just turn round the turret, the elbows swing to the posteromedial side and the straps shorten over the top. ACROSS-BODY: the saddle goes anterior. The posterior leg wraps behind the acromion and the anterior elbow sits over the clavicle. BEHIND-BACK: the saddle goes posterior-down and the anterior leg stretches over the front of the cap. Heights above the fitted underside: rings 4.5 mm, pins 8 mm, straps 3-4 mm.
why_better: (1) All three actuated joints sit on the most stable skin of the shoulder, on one axis: the champion's J1 site has 1.8 mm skin motion and a 100 % ceiling. They are the only moment-carrying bearings, and MVP2's three cables all end on S. (2) The distal links are two-force members (one pin at each end), so elbows and platform joints carry only in-surface forces. They can be single-bearing O14 pins about 8 mm tall instead of O20 preloaded pairs 12.25 mm tall. FINDINGS puts joint size at ~20 points of workspace (O17 vs O23). (3) Rotation about A is unlimited: no stop on that axis. (4) There is no serial wrist: the 3R's in-range singularity (12.5 deg margin held out) is replaced by parallel singularities that can be placed. Versus the catalogue's seed-spm-3rrr (three separate base hubs around the shoulder, 9 O20 hubs): one coaxial base on stable skin and six small pins.
main_risk: Workspace forces long legs, so the elbows do not stay on the dome. My kinematic screen used the bench poses (110 clip + 360 ws), the evaluator's rotation convention, 8 deg leg margins, no skin and no parallel-singularity check. The best coaxial layout closes 0.93 of the poses, and only with alpha1 60 / alpha2 120 (A = bvec(-40,40), platform centre wdir(60,30), gamma 20). With alpha1 45 it closes 0.66, with alpha1 30 only 0.24. So three elbows ride the rim like the champion's J2 (an 18-point R1 loss zone), plus three long straps: in-band may well be worse than the baseline. The three platform pins crowd the arm patch and must stay inside the rigid-cuff window (theta -20..+62 deg about the humerus, FINDINGS); wdir(60,30) is 10 deg outside it. Cranks that cross the outer rings stack +5 mm per ring. A 3-RRR is over-constrained in 6-DOF terms (Gruebler -3): it binds unless all nine axes meet within tolerance (ball studs at the platform fix this). When unpowered, elbows can flip at leg singularities.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: the arm drives the saddle and the legs follow through rolling bearings (rings: thin-section 4-point or caged-ball races; pins: one MR126 each). No joint is left free, and the base rings need no torque. Risks: an elbow snapping through a leg singularity near the range edge (fit elbow stops at the margin), and binding from axis misalignment (use ball studs). Sensing: one magnetic-strip encoder per ring; forward kinematics by Newton iteration from the last pose. MVP2: each ring's outer race is its own cable drum with Bowden stops on the S plate, so all three motors are S-referenced.
model_spec:
COMMON KIT K0-K7, as in the catalogue's crossed-skin-tracks spec:
- Bench(60,160); RS = B.frames(i)['S'][0], RH = B.frames(i)['H'][0]; bvec / wdir as in band_impl.
- K1: two-circle closure (= band_impl circ_int). K2: continuity on B.clip_order().
- K3: skin-fitted underside, marching B.dist along each sample direction (quantile q over the taken poses).
- K4: O20 hub disc, r 10, crown at +12.25. K5: strap 12 x 3. K6: radial-interval collisions. K7: neck to BOTTOM, then record all metal.
- New: P14 pin = disc r 7 normal to its axis, lower face by the K4 rule, crown at +8.

PARAMETERS
- A = bvec(-40,40).
- Platform centre Wc = wdir(60,30). Also try the champion's wdir(71.38,4.78) and wdir(100,-30), which are inside the cuff window.
- v_k = rot(Wc, 120k deg) applied to rot(t, gamma) Wc, with t = unit(Wc x down-arm axis), gamma = 20 deg, k = 0, 1, 2.
- alpha1 = 60, alpha2 = 120 (the only combination that closes >= 0.9); sigma_k = +1.

PER POSE
- A_t = RS A, v_t = RH v_k, e_k = K1(A_t, alpha1, v_t, alpha2, sigma_k). Return None if there is no closure or the margin is < 8 deg.
- Parallel singularity: with n_k = unit(e_k x v_t), return None if |det[n_0; n_1; n_2]| < 0.10.
- Return None if two elbows are < 17 deg apart, or if two distal great arcs e_k->v_t intersect (or stack them +4 mm).
- K2 on the three ring angles (atan2 about A).

METAL
- Rings: three S-fixed latitude circles about A at 9 / 15 / 21 deg, 4 mm wide, t 4.5, sampled every 4 deg, underside by K3 in RS.
- Crank k: K5 strap, 10 wide, from ring k at the crank's azimuth to e_k, lifted +5 mm per outer ring it crosses.
- Elbows: P14. Distal straps: K5, 12 wide, e_k -> v_t. Platform pins: P14 at v_k.
- Arm saddle: arm-fixed patch covering the three v_k + 8 mm, t 4, K3 in RH. K7 neck from the saddle to BOTTOM.

Then K6, record, and report per member. First screen kinematically (no skin, seconds) over A, alpha1, alpha2, gamma and Wc.
sweep_params: A (bvec az -60..150, el 35-85); alpha1 45-70; alpha2 60-130; gamma 15-35; platform centre Wc (wdir delta 60-115, az -60..+20, inside the cuff window); branches (2^3); ring polar radii 6-24 deg; ball stud vs pin at the platform.
prior_art: Agile Eye 3-RRR SPM (Gosselin & Hamel 1994); coaxial SPMs with unlimited rotation about the input axis (Shintemirov group, e.g. Tursynbek et al. ~2019); SPM shoulder-exoskeleton proposals (Niyetkaliyev & Shintemirov 2014); catalogue seed-spm-3rrr (non-coaxial, O20 hubs).

name: Spherical five-bar pointer plus an active arm roll (hybrid serial-parallel)
topology:
Two branches close on one arm hub at the arm-fixed axis W:
- Branch 1: S -> R_A1 (ACTIVE, O20 hub, dome axis u1) -> crank 1 (arc a1) -> R_B1 (passive elbow pin P14, axis e1) -> coupler 1 (arc c1, two-force member) -> R_C (passive, axis W).
- Branch 2: S -> R_A2 (ACTIVE, O20 hub, dome axis u2) -> crank 2 (arc a2) -> R_B2 (passive elbow pin, axis e2) -> coupler 2 (arc c2) -> R_C.
- u1 = u2 is allowed: a coaxial 'rhombus' with one double-row base hub.
- Coupler 1 -> R_D (ACTIVE roll, about the same axis W as R_C) -> arm-end plate on the upper-lateral arm -> neck to BOTTOM.

6 joints: 3 active (A1, A2, D), 3 passive (B1, B2, C). The arm hub at W stacks three bodies (arm / coupler 1 / coupler 2) on two bearing rows. Variant: replace D by a third base-driven leg (see convergent-spm-twistleg).
dof_reasoning: Spherical Gruebler: 6 bodies (S, crank 1, crank 2, coupler 1, coupler 2, arm) and 6 revolutes give M = 3(6-1-6)+6 = 3. The 5R loop S-crank1-coupler1-coupler2-crank2 has 2 DOF, the direction of W; R_D adds the arm's roll about W. A1, A2 and D are exactly the three coordinates to sense (MVP1) and drive (MVP2). Given the arm pose, W is known. Each elbow is a two-cone intersection (a_k about u_k, c_k about W, branch fixed), C is the angle between the couplers at W, and D is the arm's twist. Every passive angle is therefore set by closure, and gravity cannot move the A-frame without moving the arm. Passive coordinates are undetermined only at a leg singularity (u_k, e_k, W coplanar) or at the loop's parallel singularity (e1, W, e2 coplanar). Both are kept out with margins.
description: Two cranks on the scapula dome and two couplers form a closed spherical A-frame. Its apex is one hub on the upper arm, and the arm turns about that hub (roll) relative to the A-frame. REST: the base hubs sit side by side on the posteromedial dome (or the anterolateral dome, see sweep). The elbows are ~60 deg out on the rim, and the couplers converge on the arm hub at the deltoid / acromion edge. OVERHEAD: the arm hub climbs to the lateral dome, the A-frame folds (the cranks swing toward the hub) and the couplers get short over the top. ACROSS-BODY: the hub goes anterior and the A-frame opens forward over the front of the shoulder. BEHIND-BACK: the hub goes posterior-down; one coupler crosses the posterior deltoid, the other the lateral cap. The arm hub is the only moving joint that carries moment; the elbows are small pins about 8 mm tall.
main_risk: The workspace needs long cranks: crank 45 closes 0.87 of the poses, crank 30 only 0.66. At full reach the elbows ride 60 deg from their bases, which is over the rim where the champion's J2 loses its points. Two elbows and two couplers are more metal over the cap than one J2 and link 2. The best base pairs in the screen are only 20 deg apart (near-rhombus), and the parallel singularity (couplers aligned at W) may eat into that reach. The triple stack at W is taller (~16 mm, two bearing rows) unless coupler 2 rides an outer ring around the hub. The posteromedial bases the screen prefers sit where the trapezius bunches overhead. Like the champion's JN, the arm hub is on arm skin: keep W inside the cuff window (theta -20..+62) and near the low-motion patch wdir(112,-15) (disc ceiling 94 % vs 39.5 % at the champion's W).
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: the arm drives W's direction (the five-bar follows) and the roll about W (D turns). All six joints run on rolling bearings: v5-style preloaded pairs at the bases and at W, one MR126 per elbow. Nothing is free. Snap-through can happen only at leg or parallel singularities, so use margins and elbow stops. Sensing: encoders in A1, A2 and D. MVP2: cable drums in the A1 and A2 base hubs (S-referenced). D needs a cable to the arm hub, as the champion's J3 does, or use the convergent twist-leg variant.
model_spec:
COMMON KIT K0-K7, plus P14 = pin disc r 7, crown +8.

PARAMETERS
- Bases: u1 = bvec(-60,40), u2 = bvec(-40,40). Alternatives: anterolateral u1 = bvec(140,40), u2 = bvec(160,40), or coaxial u1 = u2.
- Arcs: a1 = a2 = 60; c1 = c2 = 120 (or 60 with the anterolateral bases).
- Arm axis W: wdir(60,30), the champion's wdir(71.38,4.78), or W* = wdir(112,-15).
- Branches sigma1, sigma2 = +-1.

PER POSE
- u_t = RS u_k; W_t = RH W; e_k = K1(u_t, a_k, W_t, c_k, sigma_k). Return None if there is no closure or the margin is < 8 deg.
- Parallel margin: with n_k = unit(e_k x W_t), return None if |n_1 x n_2| < sin 12 deg.
- Return None if the elbows are < 17 deg apart.
- Roll D = signed angle at W_t between the tangent toward e1 and the arm-fixed tangent toward the down-arm axis (no limit). K2 continuity on A1, A2 and D.

METAL
- K4 base hubs at u1, u2; coaxial case: one disc r 12, crown +16.
- Cranks: K5 strap u_k -> e_k. Elbows: P14. Couplers: K5 strap, 10 wide, e_k -> W.
- Arm hub at W: disc r 12, crown +16 (two rows), plus the arm-end plate (K3 in RH) and the K7 neck.
- K6: couplers vs neck within 25 mm of W are exempt only if stacked (coupler 2 over coupler 1 over the arm plate, +4 mm each).

Record and report.
sweep_params: u1, u2 (bvec az -90..180, el 35-75; coaxial allowed); crank a 40-70; coupler c 50-130; W (wdir delta 60-115, az -60..+20); branches; parallel-singularity margin 8-15 deg.
prior_art: Spherical five-bar (5R) pointing mechanisms (Ouerfelli & Kumar 1994; camera and haptic orienting devices); hybrid serial-parallel shoulder exoskeletons that move actuators to the base. None known with a roll joint on a skin-hugging arm hub.

name: Convergent 2+1 SPM: a five-bar A-frame on the arm plus a third 'twist' leg, all actives on the scapula
topology:
S -> three ACTIVE base revolutes on the dome (O20 hubs, axes u1, u2, u3 through GH).
- Legs 1 and 2: crank (arc a) -> elbow pin P14 -> coupler (arc c) -> passive pin on the arm about the SAME arm-fixed axis W (two coaxial pins in one double-row arm hub).
- Leg 3: crank -> elbow pin -> distal link -> passive pin about a second arm-fixed axis v3 (P14 on the same arm plate, 25-45 deg from W).
- Arm plate -> neck to BOTTOM.

9 joints: 3 active, 6 passive. Every link after the base is a two-force member. It is a 3-RRR SPM with two coincident platform axes, which puts its metal differently from seed-spm-3rrr's ring of three spread platform pins.
dof_reasoning: Spherical Gruebler: 8 bodies (S, 3 cranks, 3 distal links, arm) and 9 revolutes give M = 3. Legs 1 and 2 fix W's direction (2 DOF); leg 3 fixes the twist about W. The three base angles are the only sensed or driven coordinates. Given the arm pose, W and v3 are known, and every elbow is a two-cone intersection with a fixed branch. The two arm pins at W and the pin at v3 then follow, so nothing is free. Parallel singularity: n1 = e1 x W and n2 = e2 x W are both perpendicular to W, so the twist depends on leg 3 alone. n3 = e3 x v3 must keep a component along W (checked through det). 6 passive pins: flag the joint count.
description: As in fivebar-roll, a two-legged A-frame on the dome holds a double pin on the upper-lateral arm. Here the arm's roll is set by a third, light leg from a third base hub to a second pin on the same arm plate, so nothing active rides the arm. REST: three base hubs spread over the posterior, top and anterior dome. The elbows are on the rim, the two converging couplers meet at the arm hub near the acromion edge, and the twist leg reaches a pin 25-45 deg away, posterolateral on the arm plate. OVERHEAD: the arm plate climbs to the lateral dome, the A-frame folds over the top, and the twist leg swings behind the acromion. ACROSS-BODY: as fivebar-roll; the twist leg crosses the posterior deltoid. BEHIND-BACK: the twist leg crosses the anterior deltoid.
why_better: Every joint that moves with the arm is a force-only pin, because all links after the base are two-force members. The arm hub becomes a double-row pin (~O16 x 10 mm) instead of the active, moment-carrying O20 JN hub, whose zone plus neck lose 17 points of R1 on the champion. All three MVP2 cables end on S; none crosses a moving joint. W-pointing reach is the same as fivebar-roll (0.94-0.97 of the bench poses kinematically with 60-deg cranks). There is no serial wrist singularity.
main_risk: Reach is the five-bar's times leg 3's. The twist leg must close in every pose and keep det away from 0, i.e. its distal plane must keep twisting the arm about W. It likely fails somewhere in large axial rotation (the bench poses include axial -180..135). Three legs means three elbows and three straps over the cap: more covered skin out of band if the elbows sit on the rim. Both arm pins must stay inside the rigid-cuff window (theta -20..+62). Six passive pins (joint count). Over-constrained in 6-DOF terms; ball studs at the arm pins fix that.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: arm-driven; all passive pins are set by closure and no actuator torque is needed. Snap-through can happen only at leg or parallel singularities (use margins and stops). Sensing: three base encoders, forward kinematics by Newton iteration with continuity. MVP2: three cable drums in the three base hubs, all S-referenced.
model_spec:
COMMON KIT K0-K7, plus P14.

PARAMETERS
- Legs 1-2 as fivebar-roll: u1 = bvec(-60,40), u2 = bvec(-40,40), a = 60, c = 120, W = the champion's wdir(71.38,4.78) or W* = wdir(112,-15).
- Leg 3: u3 = bvec(150,45) (anterior dome) or bvec(60,75) (top); a3 = 50; c3 = 80; v3 = wdir(delta_W, az_W - 35) (posterolateral, inside the window).

PER POSE
- e1, e2 from K1 with W_t; e3 = K1(RS u3, a3, RH v3, c3, sigma3). Margins 8 deg.
- Return None if det[unit(e1 x W_t), unit(e2 x W_t), unit(e3 x v3_t)] < 0.10, if two elbows are < 17 deg apart, or if two distal great arcs cross (or stack them).

METAL
- Three K4 base hubs; cranks K5; elbows P14; couplers K5, 10 wide (e1, e2 -> W; e3 -> v3).
- Arm double pin at W: disc r 8, crown +10. P14 at v3.
- Arm plate (K3 in RH) covering W and v3 + 8 mm, t 4; K7 neck.

Then K6, record, report. Screen leg 3's placement kinematically first.
sweep_params: u3 (dome az/el); a3 40-70; c3 40-110; v3 offset from W 25-50 deg and its direction around W; legs 1-2 as fivebar-roll; det threshold 0.05-0.15.
prior_art: Degenerate 3-RRR SPMs with coincident platform axes; 'pointing + twist leg' parallel wrists; catalogue seed-spm-3rrr (generic, spread platform pins, O20 hubs).

name: Polycentric 3R: J2 (and optionally J3) replaced by a spherical four-bar 'virtual joint' with force-only pins
dof_reasoning: Spherical Gruebler: 6 bodies (S, L1, rocker 1, rocker 2, L2, arm) and 6 revolutes give M = 3. The four-bar loop has one DOF; sense it at p1, which is the virtual J2 coordinate. Given the arm pose, (theta1, phi) are fixed by aligning L2's J3 axis with the arm's W (2 equations, 2 unknowns, finitely many solutions, kept by continuity), and theta3 is the remaining twist. The passive pins p2, q1, q2 are then set by the four-bar closure. Nothing can sag, except at a four-bar toggle (transmission angle -> 0), where the coupler could snap through. Toggles are kept out of the range by a transmission-angle limit.
description: It looks like the champion 3R, except that the J2 hub on the rim is gone. Two short rockers join a plate on the dome (L1) to the plate that carries the arm hub (L2), with four small pins. REST: the J1 hub is on the dome top. L1 is a small plate with its two pins 15-25 deg down from J2's old spot, still on stable skin. The two rockers cross over the acromion edge, and L2 runs from its pins to the arm hub. OVERHEAD: the four-bar folds, and the crossing point (the virtual J2) slides along the rim, so L2 rolls over the top of the shoulder like a polycentric knee, instead of pivoting about a fixed spot whose skin radius runs 58-93 mm. ACROSS-BODY / BEHIND-BACK: J1 swings the whole assembly forward / backward, and the rockers' crossing tracks the shoulder's front / back edge.
why_better:
It is a strict superset of the champion. Its kinematic reach on the bench poses is 0.96 ws / 1.00 clips at an 8 deg margin, and the degenerate four-bar (pins coincident) is the champion itself. So a sweep can only match or beat it on the same bench. It attacks the champion's two largest R1 losses directly:
- The J2 zone (18.4 points, unfixable by shape: 5 % even when lowered) becomes four O14 force-only pins (rockers are two-force members, ~8 mm stack instead of 12.25) that can sit on the stable dome and the arm side.
- The coupler's moving instant centre lets link 2 roll around the rim, keeping its strap over a narrower band of skin radius (link 2 ribbon: 16.1 points).
The J3 option targets the arm-end hub and neck (17 points). Planar RCM parallelograms do not fit this body: I measured the posterior skin within +-40 mm of GH's projection at 38-87 mm off any plane normal to the scapular-plane axis. Spherical isograms are not exact RCMs either (the coupler turns 13-31 deg for crank changes of 20-40 deg). So the RCM idea enters here as a spherical virtual pivot.
main_risk: The IK is numerical: two unknowns, several roots, and toggle positions that are easy to hit across a workspace this large (the bench includes axial -180..135). The champion's J3 angle wraps through +-180 on the bench poses, so the arm hub must stay a full-turn bearing. Four pins plus two rockers are more metal near the rim than one hub. The gain may be small if the virtual J2 path cannot both roll with the skin and keep the reach. More pins add friction and backlash (minor with MR bearings). Modelling cost is the highest in this set.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: the arm drives everything; the four-bar has one DOF, fully set by closure. The risk is snap-through at a toggle, prevented by the transmission-angle limit plus stops on rocker 1. Sensing: J1, p1 and J3 encoders (p1 is on L1). MVP2: J1 drum on S; p1's cable crosses only J1, as the champion's J2 cable does; J3 as the champion.
model_spec:
COMMON KIT K0-K7, plus P14.

SEED = the champion: a = bvec(32.55,80.56), W = wdir(71.38,4.78), arcs 77.41 (J1-J2) and 81.45 (J2-J3), branch -1. Reference pose r = the first fit-clip frame: J2_r = K1(a_r, 77.41, W_r, 81.45, -1).

FOUR-BAR at r
- m_up = unit tangent at J2_r toward a_r; m_dn = toward W_r; s_hat = J2_r x m_up.
- p1, p2 = J2_r moved d_up (20 deg) along m_up, then +-s (12 deg) along s_hat.
- q1, q2 = J2_r moved d_dn (20 deg) along m_dn, then -+s (crossed) or +-s (open).
- lambda_k = angle(p_k, q_k); L1 carries {a, p1, p2}, L2 carries {q1, q2, W}.

PER POSE (unknowns theta1, phi)
- R_L1 = rot(a_t, theta1) RS_i RS_r^T; p_k = R_L1 p_k,r.
- q1 = rot(p1, phi) R_L1 q1_r; q2 = K1(p2, lambda2, q1, angle(q1_r, q2_r), sigma).
- R_L2 = the rotation taking (q1_r, q2_r) to (q1, q2); W_pred = R_L2 W_r. Residual W_pred - W_t.
- Grid theta1 -180..180 and phi -120..120 (6 deg steps), refine with scipy least_squares, pick by K2 continuity (clips) or the best transmission angle (ws). theta3 = the arm's twist about W relative to L2.
- Return None if there is no root, if a transmission angle (rocker vs coupler great circle at q_k) is outside [25, 155], or if two pins are < 15 deg apart.

METAL
- J1: K4. L1 plate: K3, covering a, p1, p2 + 8 mm, t 4.
- Rockers: K5, 10 wide. Pins: P14.
- L2 plate: covering q1, q2, plus a strap to W. J3: K4. K7 neck.

Then K6, record. CALIBRATE: d_up = d_dn = s = 0 must reproduce the champion's bench numbers.
sweep_params: d_up and d_dn 10-35 deg; spread s 6-20 deg; crossed vs open rockers; rocker arc asymmetry (lambda1/lambda2 0.7-1.4); J1 axis and W within +-15 deg of the champion; option: second four-bar at J3 (ground pins on the arm at wdir(105-115, -20..-10) and on the BOTTOM saddle).
prior_art: Polycentric (four-bar) prosthetic knees and four-bar knee exoskeletons; self-aligning exo joints (Schiele & van der Helm 2006; Cempini et al. 2013, kinetostatic compatibility); planar double-parallelogram shoulder RCM (Christensen & Bai 2018) and catalogue seed-rcm-parallelogram, both planar.

name: Human-closed 3-RUS truss: dome cranks and thin rods to arm studs, with the user's own GH joint as the centre
topology:
S -> three crank hubs on the stable dome (ACTIVE revolutes, O20; spherical cranks whose axes c_k pass through GH, so the crank tips ride a circle on the skin sphere) -> crank tip -> U-joint (passive, 2) -> straight or slightly bowed Ti rod (O5 tube) -> ball stud (passive, 3) on an arm saddle (lateral BOTTOM bar region plus the posterolateral arm, inside the rigid-cuff window).

The exo has NO joint at the GH centre: the user's own glenohumeral joint is the closing spherical joint. 9 joints: 3 active, 6 passive (15 passive coordinates).
dof_reasoning:
With the arm as a free 6-DOF body, each RUS leg (1+2+3 = 6 freedoms) imposes one constraint once its crank is fixed. With all cranks free, the exo constrains nothing, so the arm keeps its 6 DOF: 3 rotations plus the 3 GH translations its own girdle and joint set.

Given the arm's full pose, set by the human, each crank angle solves |T(theta) - Q| = L (2 branches, fixed by design), and the U and S angles follow. Every passive coordinate is set by the arm, and the U-joint kills the rod's spin about its axis, so nothing sags. The 3 cranks are the only sensed or driven coordinates.

Caveat for the user's ruling: the 3 'extra' mobility directions are the arm's GH translation, which is driven by the arm exactly like the passive cuff slides. But the 3 crank angles give the arm orientation only for an assumed GH position. A GH translation delta changes the readout by about delta / lever (10 mm over ~150 mm is ~4 deg). On the bench (GH fixed in S) it is exactly 3 DOF.
description:
Three short cranks turn on the top / posterior / anterior dome. From each crank tip a thin rod runs down over the shoulder to a ball stud on the arm. The arm is held like the platform of a small hexapod, with the user's shoulder joint as the pivot. REST:
- crank hubs on the acromion top (bvec(60,75)), the scapular spine root (bvec(-10,40)) and the lateral clavicle end (bvec(150,40));
- rods down the lateral, posterolateral and anterolateral deltoid to studs on the BOTTOM bar and the posterolateral saddle, 100-160 mm down the arm.
OVERHEAD: the studs come up beside the acromion, the rods shorten their span (rod-endpoint distances on the bench poses: acromion-top to lateral arm at 160 mm runs 142-222 mm), and the cranks swing to take up the distance change. ACROSS-BODY: the posterior rod lies across the back of the shoulder and the anterior rod gets short. BEHIND-BACK: the anterior rod stretches over the front of the cap. Metal is O5 rods, O12 U-joints and O14 studs, plus three O20 hubs on the stable dome.
why_better:
It beats three of the listed difficulties by construction:
- GH translation: the exo imposes no centre, so the base-slip misalignment (R10's 15.2 mm worst frame; 11.8 mm across the arm, which shifts every link of a spherical chain relative to the skin on the body) does not move the metal off its intended path, and the base never fights the arm.
- No hubs off the skin over the cap: the rods are two-force members on small joints (O12-O14, ~6 mm stack); only the three crank hubs (on the most stable skin) carry moments.
- No wrist singularity: the singularities are line-geometry ones (the rods' moments about GH coplanar), placeable by stud layout.
The arm side is three studs on the BOTTOM / saddle region instead of a deltoid hub and neck (17 R1 points on the champion).
main_risk:
Straight rods over a convex cap: the chord between a dome point and an arm point passes INSIDE the deltoid unless the ends are lifted or the rod is bowed. My rest-pose check put a straight acromion-to-lateral-arm rod ~38 mm inside the lateral deltoid at GH height. Bowing helps but makes the rod a curved bending member. Expect poor in-band unless the rods run in the posterior and anterior 'valleys' (axillary folds), which squeeze in adduction.
Crank size: covering a rod-endpoint distance range of ~80 mm needs crank radii ~40 mm (a big circle on the dome) or dropped poses. Dead centres (crank in line with the rod) give bifurcation when unpowered. 15 passive coordinates. The orientation readout depends on GH position (see dof_reasoning). In MVP2 the assist reaction goes through the user's GH joint (about +100 N compression at 10 N.m and a 0.1 m lever).
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: the arm drives every rod and crank. Rolling bearings at the crank hubs, needle-pin U-joints and low-friction rod-end balls. Nothing sags (the U kills rod spin). Keep the crank transmission angle >= 15 deg so the arm never pushes a crank through dead centre. Sensing: three crank encoders, plus (recommended) the user's own GH estimate for the translation correction. MVP2: cable drums in the three crank hubs on S. The exo then controls the arm's rotations through the human joint, like non-anthropomorphic misalignment-free exos.
model_spec:
COMMON KIT K0, K2, K3, K6, K7. The mechanism is NOT spherical, so it is modelled with 3-D points.

CRANKS: spherical. Hub axis c_k = bvec(60,75), bvec(-10,40), bvec(150,40); hub lower face by K4, hub = K4 disc. Crank = a K5 strap from the hub along a great circle, arc beta (25-40 deg). The tip direction t_k(theta) = rot(c_k, theta) of the reference tip direction; tip point T = r_T t_k with r_T = K3 requirement + 10 (the crank rides over the hub plate). In thorax coords: RS applied.

STUDS (arm-fixed points Q_k, thorax = RH q_k), using K7's bar frame Wb = (0,-0.0713,0.9975), Db = (0,-0.9975,-0.0713):
- q1 = (67.5 + 8) Wb + 80 Db (on BOTTOM);
- q2 = posterolateral (theta +45 deg about the humerus axis) at 110 mm down, rest skin + 7;
- q3 = anterolateral (theta -15 deg) at 100 mm down, rest skin + 7.

ROD LENGTH: L_k = |T(theta0) - Q_k| at the rest pose, with theta0 the crank angle pointing at Q_k's projection (mid-stroke).

IK: T(theta) lies on a circle (centre r_T cos beta c, radius r_T sin beta, plane normal to c). So A cos theta + B sin theta = C, with A = 2 rho e1.(O - Q), B = 2 rho e2.(O - Q), C = L^2 - |O - Q|^2 - rho^2 (O = circle centre, rho = radius). Return None if |C| > sqrt(A^2 + B^2); else theta = atan2(B, A) + sigma acos(C / sqrt(A^2 + B^2)).

CHECKS: return None if
- the transmission |sin(angle(dT/dtheta, rod))| < sin 15 deg;
- the conditioning det of the unit vectors Q_k x unit(Q_k - T_k) has magnitude < 0.10;
- rod-rod segment distance < 8 mm.

METAL
- Rods: 8 points around the O5 circumference every 3 mm along the chord. Optional bow: a circular arc with sagitta h in the plane of the chord and c_k, bowing outward.
- U-joints: spheres r 6 at T. Studs: discs r 7, crown +10 at Q. Arm saddle plate t 4 (K3 in RH) joining q2-q3 to BOTTOM.

Record all points. Rods are not K3-fitted: B.dist decides contact.
sweep_params: Crank hub directions (dome, 3 x az/el); crank arc beta 20-45 deg; stud positions (s 80-170 mm, theta -20..+62); rod bow sagitta 0-25 mm; branch signs; stud height 5-12 mm.
prior_art: Parallel shoulder exoskeletons that move the shoulder actuators into a parallel mechanism (BONES, Klein et al. IEEE T-RO 2010); misalignment-free exos that leave the GH centre to the human (Dampace, Stienen et al. 2009; Schiele & van der Helm 2006); RUS / RSS hexapod-lite wrists. Not the catalogue's deltoid-strut-tripod, which is spherical (arcs through guides, centred on GH).

name: Human-closed 3-UPS 'artificial deltoid': straight telescopes from dome brackets to arm studs
topology:
S -> three dome brackets (anterior: lateral clavicle; middle: acromion; posterior: scapular spine) -> U-joint (passive, 2) -> telescopic strut, O10 / O8 Ti tubes on a linear rolling or iglidur bushing (ACTIVE prismatic, its length sensed) -> ball stud (passive, 3) on the arm saddle (deltoid-insertion region, BOTTOM bar, posterolateral arm).

No exo joint at GH: the user's glenohumeral joint closes the loop. No rotary hub at all. 9 joints: 3 active (prismatic), 6 passive (15 passive coordinates).
dof_reasoning: Each UPS leg (2+1+3 freedoms) imposes one distance constraint once its stroke is fixed. Three fixed strokes give 3 constraints on the 6-DOF arm, and the user's GH joint supplies the centre. Given the arm's full pose, each strut length is |B_k - A_k|, and the U and S angles follow. The U-joint and the keyed telescope stop the strut spinning, so nothing sags. The three strokes are the only sensed or driven coordinates. Same caveat as human-closed-crank-rods: the arm's GH translation is an arm-set passive mobility (like the cuff slides), but the orientation readout depends on it (about 4 deg per 10 mm at a 150 mm lever); the user should rule. Exactly 3 on the bench, where GH is fixed.
description: Three straight telescopic struts run like the three heads of the deltoid, from small brackets on the clavicle end, acromion and scapular spine to studs on the arm around the deltoid insertion. They lengthen and shorten as the muscle heads do. REST: the middle strut runs down the lateral deltoid, the anterior strut over the front of the cap, and the posterior strut over the back. Brackets lift each end 6-10 mm so the chord clears the muscle. OVERHEAD: the middle strut shortens (acromion-top to lateral arm at 160 mm: 142-222 mm on the bench poses, ratio 1.56) and the arm studs rise beside the acromion. ACROSS-BODY: the posterior strut lengthens, the anterior one shortens. BEHIND-BACK: the reverse. Metal is three O8-O10 tubes, three O14 U-joints and three O14 studs.
why_better: It is the leanest possible metal: no hubs anywhere, just three thin two-force tubes and six small joints, so the 'hubs sit 12 mm off the skin' difficulty disappears. Like the crank-rod truss, it never imposes a GH centre: no base-slip misalignment and no centre fighting the girdle (R10). There is no wrist singularity, only the line geometry of the three struts. Its distinct physical difference from the catalogue's deltoid-strut-tripod (spherical arc struts through O20 swivel guides, centred on GH) is that these struts are straight, carry no hubs and do not centre the joint. Prismatic actives are natural for MVP2 'tendon' cables pulling along the muscle lines.
main_risk: Straight struts over a convex, bulging cap: the chord from a dome bracket to an arm stud dips into the deltoid (worst when the deltoid bunches overhead and with the biceps bulge). The only levers are bracket and stud lift and placement, which trade directly against in-band. Stroke: several useful anchor pairs need length ratios > 1.8 (e.g. clavicle to lateral arm at 110 mm: 66-169 mm, ratio 2.56). Those need two-stage telescopes (thicker) or drop poses; good pairs stay at 1.5-1.6. Telescopes under side load bind on plain bushings, so they need rolling bushings. Cables pull only, so MVP2 needs two cables or a spring per strut. 15 passive coordinates. The orientation readout depends on GH position.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: the arm pushes and pulls the struts through low-friction linear bearings; every joint is set by the arm; no sag. Sensing: a linear magnetic strip per strut. MVP2: each strut is driven by an antagonistic cable pair (or cable plus spring) from remote motors, Bowden stops on the S brackets: a literal artificial deltoid. The reaction goes through the user's GH joint.
model_spec:
COMMON KIT K0, K2, K6, K7, using 3-D points.

ANCHORS (S-fixed points; thorax = RS x): A1 = r(150,35) bvec(150,35) (clavicle), A2 = r(85,70) bvec(85,70) (acromion), A3 = r(-15,40) bvec(-15,40) (spine). r(.) = K3 requirement along that ray at the rest pose + h_A (8 mm bracket).

ARM STUDS (arm-fixed points, thorax = RH q):
- B2 = lateral, on BOTTOM: (67.5 + 7) Wb + 85 Db;
- B1 = anterolateral (theta -20) at 95 mm down, rest skin + h_B (7);
- B3 = posterolateral (theta +55) at 105 mm down, rest skin + h_B.

PER POSE: L_k = |B_k - A_k|. Stroke limits: L_min = min over the clip frames - 5, L_max <= 1.85 L_min (single stage, 25 mm overlap). Out of stroke -> None (record the ratio needed).

CHECKS: return None if the conditioning det of unit(B_k x (B_k - A_k)) has magnitude < 0.10, or if two struts are < 12 mm apart (segment distance).

GEOMETRY
- Outer tube O10 from A over 0.55 L_min; inner O8 from B over 0.55 L_min.
- U sphere r 7 at A; ball r 7 at B.
- Sample tube surfaces 8 x every 3 mm; bracket plates t 4 (K3 in RS); arm saddle as human-closed-crank-rods.

Record. Quick first table: stroke ratio and the chord's min B.dist per anchor pair over the poses.
sweep_params: Anchor directions (dome rim, 3 x az/el); bracket lift h_A 4-20 mm; stud positions (s 80-160 mm, theta -20..+62); stud lift h_B 4-15 mm; single vs two-stage telescopes (ratio 1.85 / 2.6).
prior_art: BONES parallel shoulder with pneumatic cylinders (Klein et al. 2010); Stewart-platform ankle rehab robots (Rutgers Ankle, Girone et al. 2001); muscle-line cable / strut exos and exosuits. Spherical arc-strut version: catalogue deltoid-strut-tripod.

name: Tongs tripod: spherical 3-RPR whose three 'prismatic' legs are lazy-tongs scissor lattices
topology:
Three legs in parallel from the scapula to an arm plate. Leg k:
- S -> base boss on stable dome skin (axis a_k through GH), carrying two coaxial half-bar pivots. Their relative angle is the leg's ACTIVE extension; the mean is passive.
- Lazy tongs: n = 2 units of 6 x 2 mm Ti bars on two layers, every pivot axis through GH. 1 DOF: the arc length Theta_k = angle(a_k, b_k).
- Two coaxial half-bar pivots on an arm-fixed boss (axis b_k, passive) -> arm plate -> neck to BOTTOM.

No O20 hub anywhere; all bosses ~O16 x 9 mm and pins O7 x 6 mm. 27 joints: 3 active, 24 passive.
dof_reasoning: A lazy tongs between a and b is a spherical 1-DOF 'prismatic' along the great circle a-b, so each leg is an R-P-R spherical chain. Alone it leaves the arm 3 DOF and constrains nothing (spherical Gruebler per leg: 8 bodies incl. S and arm, 9 joints, M = 3). With its extension fixed, a leg becomes R-R at a fixed arc: one constraint, a_k.b_k = const. Three fixed extensions give 3 constraints, so the arm is locked. Whole device: 20 bodies and 27 joints, M = 3(20-1-27)+27 = 3. Active = the three extensions, sensed at each base boss as the opening between the two half-bars, which is monotonic in Theta. Given the arm pose, a_k and b_k are known, so each tongs' geometry (every node at a fixed fraction of the arc) is determined. Every passive pivot is set by closure; a lattice node cannot sag without moving the arm. 24 passive pivots: flag this; the user may want to rule on many-passive-joint designs.
description: Three small scissor lattices stretch from three dome points to three points on an arm plate, like three folding 'tongs'. As the arm moves, each lattice stretches or folds evenly. Each of its nodes always sits at the same fraction of the path between its scapula point and its arm point, so the lattice stretches along with the skin between them. REST: one leg runs from the anterior dome down the anterolateral cap, one from the posterior dome down the posterior deltoid, and one from the top down the lateral cap. All three are ~12 mm wide when stretched, with nodes 6 mm tall. OVERHEAD: the arm plate rises to the lateral dome. The legs whose arcs shorten fold into fans 25-30 mm wide over the top; the posterior leg lengthens behind the acromion. ACROSS-BODY: the posterior leg stretches over the back of the shoulder and the anterior leg folds. BEHIND-BACK: the reverse.
why_better: No rigid link spans the moving cap: every leg is a lattice whose nodes move like the skin, at fixed fractions between a scapula point and an arm point. That is the closest a rigid mechanism gets to 'metal over skin that stretches'. There are no moment-carrying moving hubs: the bars carry in-surface forces at O7 pins, and the only bosses are ~9 mm tall. This is the joint-size lever (~20 points of workspace per FINDINGS) taken to its extreme. The arm is held from three sides, so no single arm hub or neck carries the arm's moment (the champion's arm end loses 17 R1 points). There is no wrist singularity. The one singularity is the three leg constraints m_k = b_k x a_k becoming coplanar, which layout can avoid. It is distinct from the catalogue's skin-stretch-scissor, which is one lattice as J2 of a serial chain with O20 J1 / J3 hubs.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: the arm drives the three extensions; every pivot runs on a miniature ball bearing (MR63 / MR85), and the lattices are set by closure. Avoid the over-stretched and fully folded ends with stops on the base half-bars. Sensing: one encoder per base boss between its two half-bars. MVP2: two cables per leg at the base boss, one per half-bar (pulling them apart or together drives the extension). The swivel about a_k stays passive. All motors are S-referenced.
model_spec:
COMMON KIT K0, K2, K3, K6, K7.

PER LEG k AND POSE i
- a = RS a_k, b = RH b_k, Theta = acos(a.b). Return None unless Theta is in [25, 125] deg.
- n_hat = unit(a x b); g(f) = slerp(a, b, f); theta_u = Theta / n (n = 2); bar half-arc beta = 15 deg.
- Require theta_u/2 <= beta - 2 deg (else over-stretched -> None).
- delta = acos(cos beta / cos(theta_u/2)); require delta >= 3 deg (else fully folded -> None).

NODES
- Centre pivots c_j = g(j/n), j = 0..n (c_0 = a and c_n = b are the end bosses).
- Lateral pivots l_j+- = cos(delta) g((j - 1/2)/n) +- sin(delta) n_hat, j = 1..n.

BARS (exact by the half-turn symmetry about each c_j)
- Half-bars c_0-l_1+ and c_0-l_1-, and l_n+-c_n and l_n--c_n: arcs of length beta.
- Full bars l_j+ - c_j - l_(j+1)- and l_j- - c_j - l_(j+1)+, j = 1..n-1: one great arc of length 2 beta, crossing at c_j.
- Each bar is a rigid member, its frame built from its two end pins. Samples along its arc, 6 wide, underside by K3. One diagonal family on layer 1 (t 2), the other on layer 2 (+2.5 mm). Pins: disc r 3.5, crown +6.

BOSSES: base disc r 8, crown +9 at a_k (K3 in RS); arm disc r 8, crown +9 at b_k on one arm plate (K3 in RH, covering the three b_k + 8 mm, t 4); K7 neck.

DEVICE CHECKS
- m_k = unit(b x a); return None if |det[m_1; m_2; m_3]| < 0.15.
- The three centre great arcs a_k-b_k must not intersect (or stack +5 mm).
- K2: continuity of the three extensions.

Record. First job: a kinematic re-screen of the leg layout with arm axes restricted to wdir az in [-62, +20] and bases off the medial side.
sweep_params: Three leg pairs (a_k: dome az/el; b_k: wdir delta 60-115, az -62..+20); units per leg n 2-3; bar half-arc beta 12-18 deg; extension window (20-30 to 115-130 deg); det threshold.
prior_art: Spherical scissor / deployable linkages (Hoberman; Kiper & Soylemez); the spherical analogue of planar 3-RPR / Gough-Stewart parallel manipulators; catalogue skin-stretch-scissor (a single lattice as a serial J2). No exoskeleton known.

name: Hubless five-bar: Jacob's-ladder rolling-contact elbows where the loop makes them force-only
dof_reasoning: Each rolling elbow (equal edge radii) is kinematically a spherical 2R with coupled equal angles, rot(c1, psi) then rot(c2, psi), i.e. one DOF, the same as a pin. So the device has fivebar-roll's mobility: M = 3 (the 5R loop's 2 DOF for W's direction plus the roll D). Active: A1, A2 and D. Given the arm pose, each leg's (theta_k, psi_k) is fixed by putting the coupler's W axis on the arm's W (2 equations per leg, branch by continuity), and C follows. Every passive coordinate is set by closure. The straps are constraints, not coordinates: no sag. Why the loop matters: in a serial chain (catalogue rolling-fin-j2, rolling-cone-elbow) J2 must carry a 2-D moment, i.e. tilt that prises the rolling faces apart. Here the couplers are two-force members, so each elbow sees only an in-surface force. That is what a rolling contact plus straps carries natively.
description: The same closed A-frame as fivebar-roll, but each elbow is two flat link ends lying side by side on the skin and rolling on each other's curved edges, held by thin crossed straps like a Jacob's-ladder toy. There is no hub, cap or stack at the elbows. REST: base hubs on the dome; each crank ends in a rounded edge (O17-25 at r 60) touching the coupler's rounded edge at the rim, couplers converging on the arm hub. OVERHEAD: as the A-frame folds, the contact point rolls along both edges, so each elbow's pivot itself moves along the rim. ACROSS-BODY / BEHIND-BACK: as fivebar-roll, with the rolling contacts on the front / back rim. Elbow height = link thickness (4 mm), against 8 mm for a P14 pin and 12.25 mm for an O20 hub.
why_better: It removes the elbow stacks, the one remaining cost of fivebar-roll on the rim (where the champion's J2 zone loses 18.4 R1 points): over the rim the metal is only 4 mm plates. The rolling contact also gives a moving pivot that 'rolls' with the skin (half the travel on each edge). It puts rolling contacts where the loop's statics make them structurally sound (force-only), unlike the serial rolling-J2 entries. Keeps fivebar-roll's reach (kinematic screen 0.94-0.97 with 60-deg cranks; the rolling pair changes the leg geometry, so re-screen).
main_risk: It is outside the user's MVP1 scope phrase 'basic rolling bearings': flexure straps are new hardware (strap fatigue, preload, wear of the rolling faces). Ask before building. Radial retention: a rolling pair has no capacity along the sphere's radius, so it needs a small V-lip on the edges or the straps' width. The kinematics change (coupled 2R elbows), so the elbow paths differ from fivebar-roll and the IK is numerical. Strap wrap limits each elbow to about +-120 deg of psi. Sensing a rolling elbow is not needed (passive), but a rolling elbow cannot later become an active joint.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: the arm drives everything; the elbows roll with near-zero resistance (rolling contact, no sliding) and are fully set by closure. Base and W joints are bearings with encoders (A1, A2, D). MVP2: identical to fivebar-roll: A1 and A2 cable drums on S, D cable to the arm hub. The rolling elbows stay passive, so they never need a drive.
model_spec:
COMMON KIT K0-K7. Parameters as fivebar-roll (u1 = bvec(-60,40), u2 = bvec(-40,40), a = 60, c = 120, W = the champion's wdir(71.38,4.78) or W* = wdir(112,-15)), plus rho = 10 deg.

LEG k
- Crank: rigid axes {u_k, c1k}, angle(u_k, c1k) = a - rho.
- Coupler: rigid axes {c2k, W}, angle(c2k, W) = c - rho.
- At the reference contact, angle(c1k, c2k) = 2 rho.

FORWARD (theta, psi)
- R_c = rot(u_t, theta) R_c0; c1 = R_c c1_0; c2' = rot(c1, psi) R_c c2_0.
- R_d = rot(c2', psi) rot(c1, psi) R_c (times the coupler's reference offset); W_pred = R_d W_0.

IK per leg: grid theta (5 deg) x psi (-120..120, 5 deg), then scipy least_squares on W_pred = W_t. Branch by K2 continuity. Both legs must close.

CHECKS: return None if
- the parallel margin fails (n_k = unit(c2k' x W_t); |n_1 x n_2| < sin 12 deg);
- |psi_k| > 120;
- the two contact regions are < 17 deg apart.
D and C as in fivebar-roll.

METAL
- Crank: K5 strap u_k -> c1k, ending in an edge disc (angular radius rho about c1k, t 4, K3).
- Coupler: edge disc (rho about c2k, t 4) plus a K5 strap to W.
- The two discs share one layer and are K6-exempt from each other. Straps are ignored (0.1 mm).
- Base hubs K4; W hub disc r 12, crown +16; arm plate; K7 neck.

Record and report the elbow-region in-band separately.
sweep_params: rho 6-15 deg; crank and coupler arcs as fivebar-roll (a 40-70, c 50-130); base axes; W; unequal edge radii (ratio 0.7-1.4, which changes the angle coupling to sin(rho1)/sin(rho2)).
prior_art: Rolling-contact joints with crossed flexures: Jacob's ladder, CORE (Cannon & Howell 2005, Halverson et al. 2010), rolling-contact knee exoskeletons and robot fingers. Catalogue rolling-fin-j2 / rolling-cone-elbow put the rolling pair at a serial J2; here it is at the force-only elbows of a closed loop.

name: Spherical lazy-tongs polar positioner (multi-rhombus scissor from a scapula pole hub to a deltoid hub)
topology: Scapula base -> base hub at pole p1 (axis radial through GH) carrying TWO coaxial R joints, both ACTIVE: theta_a (root a-bar vs base) and theta_b (root b-bar vs base); J1 = (theta_a+theta_b)/2 is the scissor's azimuth about p1, J2 = theta_b-theta_a its opening -> spherical lazy-tongs of n = 3 rhombi along the great circle p1 -> e: 3n = 9 passive pivots, all with radial axes through GH (n-1 centre crossings C_1..C_(n-1), 2n side pivots S_k+/-, 1 pivot between the two end half-bars at C_n) -> arm hub at e (arm-fixed direction on the posterior deltoid): J3 R ACTIVE (arm member vs the end a-half-bar, radial axis) -> rigid arm member on the user's upper-arm cuff through the user's passive self-aligning slides (outside the count, GH translation).
dof_reasoning: Spherical mobility: 2n+2 bars + the arm = 2n+3 moving bodies at 3 DOF each, 3n+3 one-DOF joints -> M = 3(2n+3) - 2(3n+3) = 3 for any n, i.e. exactly the arm's 3 rotations. Exactly three coordinates must be driven or sensed: the two coaxial base angles and J3. Every scissor pivot is fixed by the lazy-tongs closure (all rhombi share one angle because each crossing bar is continuous through its centre pivot), and the opening is fixed by the hub distance Theta = angle(p1, e), which the arm sets. So there is no undriven spare coordinate and nothing can sag. The cuff slides are the user's passive closure-set slides, outside the count.
description: A thin titanium lazy-tongs band lies on the shoulder: two layers of 7 x 2.5 mm bars on O8 rolling pivots, about 6.5 mm in total. It runs between a base hub over the medial scapular spine / supraspinatus and an arm hub on the posterior deltoid, always along the shortest path between them. Its length follows the hub distance and its width shrinks as it stretches. Rest: the hubs are about 58 deg apart and the scissor fans across the back of the shoulder (about +/-26 deg, +/-33 mm wide). Overhead: the posterior deltoid rises and comes forward, Theta grows toward about 150 deg, and the band stretches into a narrow (+/-12 deg) strip over the top of the shoulder from the spine to the raised deltoid. Across-body: the deltoid swings forward and lateral, and the band stretches over the posterior-lateral cap. Behind-back: the posterior deltoid comes back toward the spine, the band collapses into wide rhombi on the back of the shoulder, and the hubs approach each other (the Theta_min stop). The only hubs sit on skin that moves with them (scapula and arm). No intermediate hub travels over moving skin.
why_better: It attacks the two largest R1 losses of the baseline. The J2 hub zone costs 18 pts at 0.7 % in band, because J2 sweeps skin whose GH radius runs 58-93 mm; link 2's ribbon costs 16 pts. Here there is no intermediate hub, the moving metal stays in the geodesic band between the two hubs, and it is half as thick (6.5 mm pivot stack vs a 12.25 mm hub plus 5.5 mm straps), so more of it can sit at 2-10 mm. The span is a variable-length link, so no fixed arc overhangs and the 35 deg minimum-arc problem disappears. Two of the three drives sit on the base (MVP2). It is also the armourer's lobster-tail principle: the relative motion is split into equal small steps.
main_risk: Kinematic margin. A frames-only check over the 470 bench poses found no (base pole, arm hub) pair better than Theta in 25-153 deg, with both ends near the polar singularity e = +/-p1 where J1 is undefined.
