The scissor must therefore stretch about 6:1 (n >= 3) and is wide (+/-27 deg, about 35 mm) when collapsed; the bench workspace includes axial -180..135 deg. The 3n+3 = 12 pivots accumulate backlash, and slender bars may not carry MVP2's ~10 N.m (the force ratio rises near collapse). Prior evidence is mixed: this repo's re-optimised 2-rhombus scissor reached ~50 % coverage (arm-rom stage, different body and metric) against 65-76 % for a free 4R. It has never been measured for in-band share.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the arm drives the arm hub, and the opening and all pivots follow by closure. 12 rolling pivots (MR63 in the bars, MR117 pairs in the two hubs) keep friction far under R17, except near collapse, where a small hub motion needs a large opening change (check the stall margin with judge/dynamics.py). MVP2: theta_a and theta_b are two coaxial base joints, i.e. two stacked cable drums in the base hub, sensed by two magnet/PCB encoders in the base stack; neither cable crosses a moving joint. J3 at the arm hub needs one Bowden cable routed along the a-bars (the sheath bends at the pivots) and an encoder in the arm hub.
model_spec: COMMON: B = CB.Bench(); r = BP._rig(); H0 = BP.segs(r.L, r.s, dict(plane=0, elev=0, axial=0, flex=12.5, pron=0))[0][2][0]. Per pose: f = B.frames(i); S = f['S'][0]; Q = S.T @ f['H'][0] @ H0.T (the arm rotation from rest, in the scapula frame). Solve everything in the scapula frame (rest-thorax axes: x anterior, y up, z lateral; GH = origin): base points stay put, an arm point q (rest coords) becomes Q q, and samples X go to the bench as (S @ X.T).T. Sample only skin-facing faces, on a ~2 mm grid (O20 hub = disc r 10 at its lower face). Height fit in 2 passes: each member sample has a radius rho along its fit direction (radial from GH). Pass 1 at rho0 = 100 mm, over every pose where the chain closes, records d_min per sample; then set rho -= d_min - 2.5 (one value per disc; bars smoothed); pass 2 = B.record / B.report. Return None when the chain does not close, a joint leaves its travel, or same-layer parts overlap. PARAMETERS (defaults from a frames-only check): base pole p1 = unit(-0.87, 0.29, -0.41) (S frame, medial scapular spine / supraspinatus); arm hub direction e0 = unit(-0.88, -0.34, 0.33) (rest frame, posterior deltoid). This pair keeps Theta in 25-153 deg over the bench poses. n = 3 rhombi; half-bar angular length l = 28 deg; t0 = any unit vector perpendicular to e0. IK PER POSE: e = Q e0; Theta = arccos(p1.e). Take the pose only if 20 <= Theta <= 0.96*2*n*l. m = unit(e - (p1.e) p1) (tangent at p1 toward e); bpole = cross(p1, m); centreline c(s) = cos(s) p1 + sin(s) m; side point X(s, w) = cos(w) c(s) + sin(w) bpole. Half-width w = arccos(cos(l)/cos(Theta/(2n))). Nodes: C_j = c(j*Theta/n) for j = 0..n (C_0 = p1, C_n = e); S_k+/- = X((k-0.5)*Theta/n, +/-w) for k = 1..n. Bars are great-circle arcs (slerp). a-family on layer 1: C_0-S_1-, S_k+ -> C_k -> S_(k+1)- for k = 1..n-1, and S_n+ - C_n. b-family on layer 2: C_0-S_1+, S_k- -> C_k -> S_(k+1)+, and S_n- - C_n. Coordinates: J1 = azimuth of m about p1 in a fixed tangent frame at p1; J2 = 2*atan(tan(w)/sin(Theta/(2n))); J3 = signed angle about e from the end a-bar's tangent at e to Q t0 (|J3 - median| <= 160 deg, sweep). METAL: bars 7 mm wide; layer 1 skin face at the fitted node radius (linear between a bar's two end nodes); layer 2 at +3.0 mm. Pivot discs O8 at every C and S node (MR63, O3 pin, 6.3 mm stack). Base hub = O20 disc at p1 (base plate + root a-bar + root b-bar, 12.25 mm stack). Arm hub = O20 disc at e (arm member under the end half-bars). Fit one radius per node index (C_j, S_k+, S_k-), taken as the worst case over poses. EXTRA None CHECKS: hub rims closer than 4 mm (Theta*R < 24 mm); any side node within 9 mm of a hub rim. GH translation is not on the bench (passive cuff slides).
sweep_params: p1 (2 angles) inside the S-fixed patch (acromion top / scapular spine / supraspinatus: skin motion vs S < 5 mm at elevation 150); e0 (2 angles) on the deltoid band 60-120 deg from the humerus axis; n in {2, 3, 4}; half-bar l from Theta_max/(2n)+2 to +8 deg; bar width 6-9 mm; layer gap 2.8-3.5 mm; J3 travel cap 120-180 deg.
prior_art: Castro, Rasmussen, Andersen & Bai 2019, 'A compact 3-DOF shoulder mechanism constructed with scissors linkages for exoskeleton applications' (Mech. Mach. Theory 132): spherical scissors with a remote centre. MEDARM (Ball, Brown & Scott 2007): curved tracks as remote-centre joints. Armour lobster-tail lames. In this repo: the user's original scissor CAD topology ('A current CAD scissor', 15 %) and its re-optimised 2-rhombus version (~50 % coverage), pipeline/arm-rom/RESEARCH_NOTES.md and design_search_scissor_pivots.py, whose open directions list 'a scissor with more rhombi (thinner band)'. Never measured for in-band share or on concept_bench.

name: Dome tripod: three curved telescopes between scapula and deltoid (CAREX made rigid, spherical 3-RPR)
topology: Three legs in parallel between the scapula base and an arm plate on the deltoid. Each leg: base pivot (passive R, radial axis through GH, on the acromion / scapular spine) -> curved telescope = spherical prismatic along the great circle b_i -> a_i (ACTIVE: an outer Ti channel arc fixed to the base pivot and an inner bar arc fixed to the arm pivot, sliding on caged balls) -> arm pivot (passive R, radial axis through GH) on a rigid arm plate -> the user's passive cuff slides absorb GH translation (outside the count).
dof_reasoning: Spherical mobility: 6 leg segments + the arm plate = 7 moving bodies and 9 one-DOF joints, so M = 3*7 - 2*9 = 3. Each RPR leg fixes one angular distance, angle(b_i, a_i), which is its active telescope length; three distances fix the plate's rotation (locally, away from parallel singularities). Both pivots of each leg are set by closure, because the leg must lie on the great circle through b_i and a_i. A 2-segment telescope has no free middle segment; a 3-segment one gets a one-rhombus centring scissor so its middle segment cannot flop. All pivot axes meet at one point, so the exo has its own spherical centre, and the cuff slides close the small GH offset.
description: Three slender telescoping arcs (12 x 6.5 mm channels) fan out from the acromion and spine over the shoulder cap to the anterior, lateral and posterior deltoid, like tent poles. The arm plate on the deltoid is the only arm-side metal and a strap joining the three base pivots is the only base metal. Rest: legs are about 60-100 deg long; the front leg runs over the anterior acromion, the middle one over the top, the back one over the posterior shoulder. Overhead: the deltoid rises under the acromion, the lateral and posterior legs shorten and swing up, and the anterior leg rolls over the front. Across-body: the posterior leg stretches over the back of the shoulder and the anterior one shortens. Behind-back: the anterior leg stretches across the front of the shoulder and the posterior one shortens. Each leg is an arc of constant radius about GH.
why_better: No rigid link with an elbow hub crosses moving skin. As in CAREX, the human GH is the spherical constraint, so the metal is three thin strips on near-shortest paths plus a base strap and an arm plate. The 12.25 mm joint stacks shrink to six small leg-end pivots, all on skin that moves with them. Parallel load sharing lets each strip be thin. The singularity is of the parallel kind (leg planes coplanar), not the 3R's J1 || J3, so the overhead pose can be kept far from it.
main_risk: Range. A frames-only check found that even the best single leg (base on the posterior scapula, arm point on the antero-lateral deltoid) spans 85-177 deg over the bench poses. A 2-segment telescope covers only about L - 15 deg of range, and the great circle degenerates near 180 deg, so reach may stay well under the baseline's ~78 %. Constant-radius arcs cannot follow skin whose GH radius runs 47 mm (top) to 73 mm (back), so in-band share is uncertain. Legs may cross, and layering one of them costs 6.5 mm. Near a parallel singularity the unpowered plate goes loose.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the arm pulls the plate, the telescopes slide on caged balls (rolling) and the pivots follow. Near |det| ~ 0 the plate is under-constrained; those poses are excluded and need checking in judge/dynamics.py. MVP2: each telescope gets a pull-pull cable along its channel (sheath stops on the outer arc, cable anchored on the inner bar) and a magnetic linear tape plus reader for sensing. The drive is a curved prismatic whose moment arm is the leg radius (~65 mm), so about 150 N per leg at 10 N.m.
model_spec: COMMON: B = CB.Bench(); r = BP._rig(); H0 = BP.segs(r.L, r.s, dict(plane=0, elev=0, axial=0, flex=12.5, pron=0))[0][2][0]. Per pose: f = B.frames(i); S = f['S'][0]; Q = S.T @ f['H'][0] @ H0.T. Work in the scapula frame (x anterior, y up, z lateral, GH = origin): arm points q become Q q; send samples to the bench as (S @ X.T).T. Skin-facing faces only, ~2 mm grid. 2-pass radial height fit as in lazy-tongs-polar: pass 1 records d_min per sample over the poses where the chain closes, then rho -= d_min - 2.5. Return None on no closure, travel exceeded, or overlap. LEGS: base directions b_i (S frame) and arm directions a_i0 (rest frame). Defaults: b = [unit(0.30, 0.90, 0.30) anterior acromion, unit(-0.36, 0.93, 0.09) acromion top, unit(-0.75, 0.55, -0.37) scapular spine]; a0 = [unit(0.85, -0.2, 0.49) anterior deltoid, unit(0, -0.2, 0.98) lateral deltoid, unit(-0.85, -0.2, 0.49) posterior deltoid]. Each leg has ONE constant radius R_i (telescoping needs it), fitted as the minimum over all of that leg's samples and poses. IK: a_i = Q a_i0; theta_i = arccos(b_i.a_i); the active coordinate is R_i*theta_i. Two-segment telescope (outer arc of angular length L fixed at b_i and pointing toward a_i; inner arc of length L fixed at a_i and pointing back toward b_i): legal if L+3 <= theta_i <= 2L-12 and theta_i <= 165 deg. Option: 3 segments (middle segment centred by a mini scissor), legal if L+3 <= theta_i <= 3L-24. Default L = 80 deg. PARALLEL SINGULARITY: n_i = unit(cross(b_i, a_i)); take the pose only if |det[n_1, n_2, n_3]| >= 0.1. COLLISION: two legs on the same layer whose arcs intersect on the sphere -> None. Layers: default all 0; option: the middle leg +6.5 mm. METAL: outer channel 12 mm wide, skin face at R_i, along s in [0, L] from b_i (titanium U channel with a 1 mm wall, 1 mm caged balls inside, 6.5 mm tall); inner bar only where it lies outside the channel (s in [L, theta_i - 0] measured from b_i; 8 mm wide; skin face at R_i + 1.5); pivot discs O16 at b_i and at a_i, skin face at R_i - 2 (MR85 pair, 9 mm stack under the channel); base strap 14 mm wide along b_1-b_2-b_3 (S-fixed, radius fitted); arm plate strap along a_1-a_2-a_3 (arm-fixed, radius fitted). Report also the median |det| over taken poses.
sweep_params: b_i (3 x 2 angles, inside the S-fixed patch); a_i0 (3 x 2 angles on the deltoid band 60-120 deg from the humerus axis); segment length L (60-110 deg) and segment count {2, 3}; leg radius offset over the fitted minimum (0-4 mm); layer assignment {all 0, middle +6.5 mm}; singularity threshold 0.05-0.15.
prior_art: CAREX (Mao & Agrawal 2012, IEEE TRO): cuffs plus cables, with the human joint carrying compression; made rigid here with curved telescopes on a sphere, which gives a 3-RPR spherical parallel manipulator. Hunt, Lee & Artemiadis 2017 (J. Med. Devices): parallel linear actuation through a passive slip interface. BONES (Klein, Spencer, Allington & Reinkensmeyer 2008): parallel shoulder actuation. Not known on a shoulder in this form.

name: Base-rail tripod: three carriages on scapula rails pushing fixed-length leg arcs (spherical 3-PRR, Hexaglide-like)
topology: Three legs in parallel. Each leg: a curved rail fixed on the scapula base (a great-circle arc on the acromion / scapular spine / supraspinatus) -> carriage on the rail (ACTIVE curved P) -> carriage pivot (passive R, radial axis through GH) -> rigid fixed-length leg arc -> arm pivot (passive R, radial) on an arm plate on the deltoid -> the user's passive cuff slides (outside the count).
dof_reasoning: Spherical mobility: 3 carriages + 3 legs + the arm plate = 7 bodies and 9 one-DOF joints, so M = 3. Each leg fixes angle(c_i, a_i) = L_i. The carriage position t_i is the active coordinate; both leg pivots follow by closure, because the leg is the great-circle arc c_i -> a_i. No coordinate is left free, so nothing sags.
description: All of the variable-length motion happens on the scapula. Three short curved rails (10 x 4 mm) on the acromion, spine and supraspinatus carry carriages that slide as the arm moves. From each carriage a rigid titanium leg arc of fixed length, shaped to its own skin profile, runs over the shoulder cap to an arm plate on the deltoid. Rest: carriages sit mid-rail and the legs go to the anterior, lateral and posterior deltoid. Overhead: the deltoid rises under the acromion and the carriages run toward the lateral ends of their rails. Across-body: the carriage feeding the posterior leg runs medially along the spine. Behind-back: the anterior leg's carriage runs forward on the acromion. Legs swing over the cap but never change length.
why_better: It moves the variable-length part onto S-fixed skin; the baseline's base region is its best-scoring area (82 % in band). The legs stay rigid, so unlike telescopes each leg can follow its own non-spherical height profile (fitted per sample). There are no elbow hubs over moving skin, and all three drives sit on the base (MVP2). The singularity set is different from the 3R's: serial (rail tangent perpendicular to the leg) and parallel (leg planes coplanar).
main_risk: Rail length. A frames-only check found that the angular distance from any S-fixed point to an arm-fixed point varies by about 100 deg over the bench poses, while the S-fixed patch is only about 50 deg across. A leg may run off its rail (reach loss) unless the rails extend onto skin that moves: medially along the spine is fine, the lateral acromion rim is not. Other risks: serial singularities where a rail runs perpendicular to its leg (pushing the carriage does nothing), legs crossing, and curved rails at r 50-80 mm being custom parts (no catalogue part fits, per docs/research/ring_and_shell_hardware.md).
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the carriages roll (V-wheels or a caged-ball curved guide) and the legs follow; poses near a serial or parallel singularity are excluded and need a dynamics check. MVP2: three pull-pull cables run along S-fixed rails, so no cable crosses a moving joint, and magnetic tapes on the rails give sensing.
model_spec: COMMON as in lazy-tongs-polar: H0 from BP.segs at rest; Q = S.T @ H @ H0.T; scapula frame (x anterior, y up, z lateral, GH = origin); bench samples = (S @ X.T).T; skin-facing faces on a ~2 mm grid; 2-pass radial height fit (rho -= d_min - 2.5 after pass 1); None on no closure, travel exceeded, or overlap. RAILS: rail i is c_i(t) = cos(t) r1_i + sin(t) r2_i for t in [0, T_i] (r1_i, r2_i orthonormal, S frame). Defaults: rail 1 from unit(-0.36, 0.93, 0.09) (acromion top) toward unit(-0.85, 0.35, -0.40) (medial spine), T = 55 deg; rail 2 from unit(0.40, 0.88, 0.25) (anterior acromion) toward unit(-0.20, 0.85, -0.48) (supraspinatus), T = 50 deg; rail 3 from unit(0.30, 0.80, 0.52) toward unit(-0.55, 0.72, 0.42) (along the lateral acromion rim), T = 50 deg. Set r2_i = unit(end - (end.r1) r1). Arm points a_i0 as in dome-telescope-tripod (anterior, lateral, posterior deltoid). Leg length L_i = angle(c_i(T_i/2), Q_med a_i0) at the median clip pose. IK per leg: a = Q a_i0; alpha = r1.a; beta = r2.a; rho = hypot(alpha, beta). Need |cos L_i| <= rho. Then t = atan2(beta, alpha) +/- arccos(cos(L_i)/rho); fix the branch per leg to the one inside [0, T_i] at the median pose, and keep continuity on clips. Take the pose only if t is in [0, T_i]. SINGULARITIES: serial: tau = dc/dt, m = unit tangent of the leg arc at c toward a; need |tau.m| >= 0.25. Parallel: |det[unit(cross(c_i, a_i))]| >= 0.1. COLLISIONS: two leg arcs on the same layer that intersect -> None; a leg arc passing within 8 mm of another leg's carriage -> None. METAL: rails 10 mm wide (skin face fitted, base metal); carriages as 16 mm discs at c_i (rail 4 + carriage 5 = 9 mm stack); leg arcs 12 mm wide x 4 mm, parametrised by u in [0, 1] from c_i to a_i, with a fitted radius per u (rigid legs may follow any height profile); arm pivots O16 at a_i; arm plate strap along a_1-a_2-a_3.
sweep_params: rail endpoints (3 x 4 angles, inside the S-fixed patch, rail length 30-70 deg); a_i0 (3 x 2 angles on the deltoid band); leg lengths L_i (median-pose value +/- 15 deg); branch per leg; serial threshold 0.15-0.35.
prior_art: Hexaglide (Honegger, Codourey & Burdet 1997) and Linapod: base-mounted linear guides driving fixed-length struts, transposed here to a sphere as a spherical 3-PRR. The actuators-on-the-base principle of Harmony (Kim & Deshpande 2017) and ANYexo (Zimmermann et al. 2019). No shoulder exoskeleton of this form is known.

name: Co-axial spherical parallel manipulator on a scapula pole (Agile-Eye legs, all drives in one base hub)
topology: Base pole u on the scapula: three concentric thin-section ring bearings about u, each ACTIVE (phi_1..3) -> three proximal 90 deg arcs (nested on three layers) -> elbow R (passive, axis v_i through GH) -> three distal 90 deg arcs -> platform R (passive, axis w_i through GH) on an arm plate across the anterior / top-lateral / posterior deltoid -> the user's passive cuff slides (outside the count).
dof_reasoning: Spherical mobility: 6 arcs + the platform = 7 bodies and 9 R joints, so M = 3. Once phi_i is set, each leg's elbow is fixed by its assembly branch (a two-cone intersection), so every passive joint is set by closure. Parallel-singular poses (|det| small) are excluded, so no free coordinate remains.
description: One flat stack of three concentric rings (radii 9/15/21 mm, 6 mm tall) sits over the supraspinatus / scapular-spine pole. Three nested quarter-circle arcs leave it like clock hands, three elbow hubs ride 90 deg away, and three quarter-circle distal arcs land on three hubs on the deltoid. A rotation of the arm about u, close to elevation in the scapular plane, turns all three legs together with no singularity (unlimited, co-axial). Plane of elevation and twist come from tilting the platform. Rest: the legs lie over the posterior and lateral cap. Overhead: the leg set rotates up about u, and the legs lie over the top of the shoulder toward the neck side. Across-body and behind-back need large tilts: the elbows swing out over the anterior or posterior arm.
why_better: It is the only concept with all three drives in one base hub over S-fixed skin, which gives the cleanest MVP2 routing: three cable grooves on the rings and nothing crossing a moving joint. It has no 3R singularity, since elevation about u is unlimited. Parallel stiffness lets each arc be thin.
main_risk: It carries the most metal of any concept: 6 arcs on up to 3 nested layers (the outermost at +9 mm), 6 hubs and 3 rings, so its in-band share is probably below the baseline's. A frames-only check found that the best arm-fixed platform axis stays within 65 deg (p90) / 89 deg (max) of the best base axis over the bench poses. Tilts therefore approach 90 deg, which needs Agile-Eye 90/90 arcs (about 100 mm each); the legs may cross or hit the neck. Modelling effort is high.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: closure sets all elbows; near parallel singularities the platform loosens (exclude those poses and check dynamics). MVP2: three cable grooves on the three concentric rings at the base pole, with magnetic ring encoders for sensing; the platform carries no drive.
model_spec: COMMON as in lazy-tongs-polar: Q = S.T @ H @ H0.T; scapula frame; bench samples = (S @ X.T).T; skin-facing faces on a ~2 mm grid; 2-pass height fit; None on no closure, travel exceeded, or overlap. GEOMETRY: base axis u = unit(-0.67, 0.56, -0.49) (S frame). Virtual platform axis e_p0 = unit(-0.3, 0.75, -0.59) (rest frame; it points from GH into the scapula). A frames-only check found Q e_p0 stays within 65 deg (p90) / 89 deg (max) of u. Platform joint axes w_i0: three arm-fixed directions on the great circle perpendicular to e_p0, at the anterior, top-lateral and posterior deltoid (drop the axillary or medial part; the spacing need not be 120 deg). Defaults alpha1 = alpha2 = 90 deg (Agile Eye). Pick a reference v_ref with angle(u, v_ref) = alpha1; v1 = v_ref - (u.v_ref) u; v2 = cross(u, v_ref); then v(phi) = cos(phi) v1 + sin(phi) v2 + (u.v_ref) u. IK per leg i: w = Q w_i0. Solve v(phi).w = cos(alpha2): A = v1.w, B = v2.w, C = cos(alpha2) - (u.v_ref)(u.w); phi = atan2(B, A) +/- arccos(C/hypot(A, B)). Fix the branch per leg to the median-pose one and keep continuity on clips; no real root -> None. v_i = v(phi_i). PARALLEL SINGULARITY: n_i = unit(cross(v_i, w_i)); take the pose only if |det[n_1, n_2, n_3]| >= 0.1. LAYERS: proximal arcs on layers 0 / +4.5 / +9 mm (they rotate about the same axis and overlap); distal arcs on 0 / +4.5 / +9 mm in the same order. Two arcs on the same layer intersecting -> None. METAL: base rings as an annulus r 7-23 mm at u (6 mm stack); proximal straps 12 mm x 4 from the ring rim to v_i; elbow hubs O20 at v_i; distal straps v_i -> w_i; platform hubs O20 at w_i; arm plate along w_1-w_2-w_3. Radii are fitted per member with the 2-pass rule, and the layer offsets are added on top.
sweep_params: u (2 angles); e_p0 (2 angles) and the azimuths of w_i0 (3 angles); alpha1, alpha2 (75-100 deg); per-leg branch (8 combinations); layer order; ring radii.
prior_art: Co-axial spherical parallel manipulator for a shoulder exoskeleton (Tursynbek, Niyetkaliyev & Shintemirov 2019, IEEE CASE; Niyetkaliyev & Shintemirov 2014, Nazarbayev University); Agile Eye (Gosselin & Hamel 1994); review: Niyetkaliyev, Hussain, Ghayesh & Alici 2017 (IEEE THMS).

name: Offset-centre 2R pointer with a sliding twist sleeve at the cuff (decoupled, self-aligning)
topology: Scapula base -> J1 R hub (ACTIVE, axis a1 through a centre O placed 0-30 mm from GH) -> link 1 -> J2 R hub (ACTIVE, axis through O, perpendicular to a1) -> bar (link 2) ending in a straight O6 rod on the line O -> C -> linear-rotary sleeve on the rod: J3 R (ACTIVE, spin about the rod) + slide P (passive) -> Hooke U at the cuff (2 passive R, axes perpendicular to the rod) -> the user's upper-arm cuff.
dof_reasoning: Spatial mobility with the human GH as a ball joint: link 1, bar, sleeve, U-cross and arm = 5 bodies (30 DOF), minus J1 5, J2 5, sleeve cylindrical 4, U 5+5 and GH 3 = 27, so M = 3. The chain has 6 coordinates (J1, J2, J3, slide, U1, U2) for the cuff's 6 DOF (Jarrassé & Morel: n + p = 6), so every passive coordinate is fixed by closure and none can sag. Only J1, J2 and J3 need driving or sensing. With O = GH the slide is idle and the U angles are constant, and the chain becomes cuff-sleeve-3r.
description: A J1 hub on the anterior-superior acromion; link 1 runs over the top of the shoulder to the J2 hub on the posterior-lateral cap; one bar runs from J2 down the lateral arm and ends in a short rod at about 200 mm down the humerus. There a sleeve on the user's cuff (O12 linear-rotary bushing on a small 2-axis gimbal) both spins about and slides along the rod. No hub on the deltoid, no ring, no arm-end neck. Overhead: the bar lies along the lateral (now medial-facing) side of the raised arm. Across-body: along its outer side. Behind-back: along the posterior-lateral side. The sleeve slides 30-50 mm along the rod and the cuff gimbal tilts up to about 25-34 deg (frames-only check).
why_better: It removes the arm-end parts (BOTTOM's JN hub + neck: 17 pts of R1 lost; the R16 'link 2 vs neck' collisions) and moves the twist bearing to the cuff, where the arm is narrow and its skin calm. Uniquely, it follows ANY cuff pose exactly, so GH translation and the 4-15 mm handler slip (R10) are absorbed by construction without the user's cuff slides. The centre O can be moved off GH to put the hubs where the skin under them moves least.
main_risk: With O off GH, the links rotate about O while the shoulder skin rotates about GH, so they move against the skin by about |o| x angle. With O at GH this reduces to cuff-sleeve-3r. The measured J1-J3 angles mix in GH translation (an orientation error of about delta/lambda, ~3 deg per 10 mm) when used for MVP1 tracking. The cuff gimbal plus sleeve adds about 16-19 mm of bulk at the cuff, and the rod needs 30-50 mm of slide when O is 20-40 mm from GH. The bar is a long cantilever (stiffness and mass).
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the cuff pulls the sleeve; the slide and the U are set by closure; the linear-rotary ball bushing and the U bearings roll (~0.005). MVP2: drums at the J1 and J2 hubs (J2's cable crosses J1) and a drum on the sleeve with a cable along the bar for J3; encoders at the three. Because the slide is free, the assist reaches the arm as a force perpendicular to the rod (lever ~200 mm, ~50 N at 10 N.m).
model_spec: COMMON as in lazy-tongs-polar: Q = S.T @ H @ H0.T; scapula frame (x anterior, y up, z lateral, GH = origin); bench samples = (S @ X.T).T; skin-facing faces on a ~2 mm grid; 2-pass height fit, with the bar fitted radially from the humerus axis for samples more than 100 mm from O; None on no closure, travel exceeded, or overlap. PARAMETERS: O = o with default 20 mm along unit(-0.36, 0.93, 0.09) toward the acromion top (o = 0 gives the cuff-sleeve-3r limit). a1 = unit(0.31, 0.68, 0.67): a frames-only check found the arm direction never within ~31 deg of +/-a1. Cuff point C0 (rest frame) = lateral upper-arm skin at y = -200 plus 10 mm; BP.V0 arm vertices at y = -200 +/- 6 have max z 82.1 at x -16, so C0 = (-16, -200, 92). Cuff U axis u2_0 = unit(cross(dh_rest, h0)) with h0 = unit(-7.4, -320.5, 53.4) (humerus) and dh_rest = unit(C0 - O). IK PER POSE: C = Q C0; d = C - O; lam = |d|; dh = d/lam. Reject if angle(a1, dh) < 12 or > 168 deg. j2 = unit(cross(a1, dh)). J1 = signed angle about a1 from j2_med to j2 (j2_med = j2 at the median clip pose). J2 = 90 - angle(a1, dh). Bar frame columns R_bar = [dh, j2, cross(dh, j2)]. u2 = Q u2_0. J3 = atan2(-(j2.u2), (cross(dh, j2)).u2), with the +pi branch chosen for continuity. U tilt = angle(dh, Q dh_rest); reject if > 40 deg. Slide: a first pass collects the lam range; reject poses that need a rod longer than 70 mm (frames-only: lam 205-258 mm with O 38 mm above GH, 210-243 mm at 23 mm, 220 mm constant at O = GH). METAL: J1 hub O20 at O + R1 a1. Link 1 strap 14 x 4 along the great circle about O from a1 to j2 (90 deg). J2 hub O20 at O + R2 j2. Bar strap from the J2 hub to the rod top P0 = O + (lam_lo - 15) dh, defined in the bar frame as a polyline of directions with a fitted radius per sample. Rod O6 along dh from lam_lo - 15 to lam_hi + 15 (sample its skin-facing generator 3 mm toward the arm axis). Sleeve O12 x 25 centred at C (skin-facing generator 6 mm toward the arm). Gimbal as an O16 disc at C, arm-fixed. No cuff slides.
sweep_params: |o| 0-30 mm and its direction (2 angles); a1 (2 angles); cuff station s 150-250 mm and its azimuth around the arm (lateral +/-60 deg); U tilt limit 30-45 deg; rod length cap 40-80 mm; bar routing side (lateral / posterolateral).
prior_art: Stienen et al. 2009 (IEEE TRO, Dampace / LIMPACT): self-aligning axes by decoupling rotations and translations. Jarrassé & Morel 2012 (IEEE TRO): passive fixations, n + p = 6. Schiele & van der Helm 2006 (IEEE TNSRE, ESA EXARM): kinematic compatibility. The sliding upper-arm interfaces of Ottobock Paexo Shoulder and suitX ShoulderX, and the passive slip interface of Hunt, Lee & Artemiadis 2017.

name: Spherical 3R with the twist joint as a GH-aimed rod-and-sleeve near the cuff (ring-free, cable-free axial joint)
topology: Scapula base -> J1 R hub (ACTIVE, radial axis at the anterior acromion) -> link 1 (64 deg arc) -> J2 R hub (ACTIVE, radial) -> link 2 (over the deltoid cap and down the lateral arm) -> short rod coaxial with the arm-fixed line e3 through GH (about 13-14 deg off the humerus axis, grazing the lateral arm at s ~230 mm) -> J3 = sleeve bearing on the cuff (ACTIVE R about e3) with a 5 mm axial float (passive P) -> the user's cuff, with one passive lateral cuff slide outside the count.
dof_reasoning: A spherical 3R about GH: all three axes pass through GH, giving 3 coordinates for the arm's 3 rotations with no spare. The sleeve's axial float lies along e3, a line through GH. On a fixed GH the sleeve's distance from GH is constant, so the float is determined (idle); under GH translation it takes up the e3 component by closure. The rest of the translation goes to one passive cuff slide (the user's self-aligning slides, outside the count).
description: The J1 hub sits on the anterior acromion. Link 1 reaches the J2 hub, which rides around the shoulder cap. Link 2 runs from J2 over the round deltoid cap and down the lateral arm to a short O5 rod near the lower upper arm (s ~230 mm, close to the user's BOTTOM bar), whose axis points back at GH. A slim sleeve (O11 x 30, two MR85 bearings that also float axially) on a small cuff bracket is the twist joint. There is no hub on the deltoid, no open ring around the arm and no arm-end neck. Overhead: link 2 lies along the raised arm's lateral (now medial-facing) side. Across-body: along the outer arm. Behind-back: down the posterior-lateral arm. Near GH, link 2 rides the deltoid cap, which is roughly a sphere about GH (4.7 mm radius spread), so turning about e3 keeps it at a nearly constant gap there.
why_better: It replaces the baseline's arm-end JN hub + neck (17 pts of R1 lost; all of R16's part collisions are 'link 2 vs neck') and the J3 hub stack on the deltoid with a sleeve at the lower upper arm, where the arm is narrow (lateral radius ~47 mm) and the skin is calm. It is a ring-free, tendon-free realisation of the repo's family V (2 pointing pivots + axial joint, 67-77 % coverage before hardware). J1 is parked so that the singular directions (J1 || J3) stay outside the bench poses: a frames-only check found >= 27 deg of margin with p1 = unit(0.46, 0.84, 0.30). Cheapest concept to model.
main_risk: The sweep principle (pipeline/arm-rom/RESEARCH_NOTES.md): between the cap and the sleeve (s ~70-150 mm), e3 runs inside the arm, so as the arm turns about e3 relative to link 2 (|J3| up to ~90 deg in the bench workspace, axial -180..135), link 2's mid part sweeps an annulus over the arm. A rough estimate gives a 3-5 mm gap at +/-45 deg and skin contact near +/-90 deg, so J3 travel may need capping and large-twist reach is lost. Link 2 is a ~170 mm cantilever (stiffness, mass). The sleeve's top sits about 14 mm off the skin.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: it behaves like the moving-freely 3R (rolling bearings, cf. band_r14_3r_s1351_1 at 0.05 N.m in judge/dynamics.py); the float is set by closure. MVP2: drums at the J1 and J2 hubs; a drum on the sleeve, with a cable along link 2 to the cuff, for J3; encoders in the two hubs and on the sleeve.
model_spec: COMMON as in lazy-tongs-polar: Q = S.T @ H @ H0.T; scapula frame (x anterior, y up, z lateral, GH = origin); bench samples = (S @ X.T).T; skin-facing faces on a ~2 mm grid; 2-pass height fit, radial from GH near the shoulder and radial from the humerus axis for samples more than 100 mm from GH; None on no closure, travel exceeded, or overlap. PARAMETERS: p1 = unit(0.46, 0.84, 0.30) (S frame); alpha12 = 64 deg; alpha23 = 90 deg. The reach window [|a12 - a23|, a12 + a23] must cover angle(p1, e3) = 28.8-153.1 deg from the frames-only check, so alpha12 >= 63.1. J3 axis: h0 = unit(-7.4, -320.5, 53.4) (the rest humerus); s3 = 230 mm; r_lat = the lateral skin radius from the humerus axis at s3 (from BP.V0 arm vertices: ~47 mm); gamma = atan((r_lat + 8.5)/s3) ~ 13.6 deg; e3_0 = h0 rotated by gamma toward the lateral skin direction at s3 (azimuth psi3 = lateral, swept). t3_0 = any unit vector perpendicular to e3_0. IK PER POSE: e3 = Q e3_0; g = p1.e3; x = (cos(a12) - cos(a23) g)/(1 - g^2); y = (cos(a23) - cos(a12) g)/(1 - g^2); b = x p1 + y e3; p2 = b + sb*sqrt(1 - |b|^2) unit(cross(p1, e3)), with branch sb fixed (median pose); no real root -> None. Reject if angle(p1, +/-e3) < 15 deg. J1 = azimuth of p2 about p1; J2 = angle about p2 between p1 and e3. J3 = atan2(cross(p2, Q t3_0).e3, p2.(Q t3_0)); reject if |J3 - J3_median| > 100 deg (swept). METAL: J1 hub O20 at rho1 p1. Link 1 strap 14 x 4 along the great circle p1 -> p2. J2 hub O20 at rho2 p2. Link 2 is defined in its frame (p2, e3, cross(p2, e3)) as a polyline: along the great circle from p2 toward the point where e3's direction leaves the deltoid cap, then down the lateral arm parallel to e3 to the rod top; fitted radius per sample. Rod O5 along e3 from s3 - 30 to s3 + 30 (skin-facing generator 2.5 mm toward the arm axis). Sleeve O11 x 30 around it (skin-facing generator 5.5 mm toward the arm axis) on an arm-fixed bracket.
sweep_params: p1 (2 angles); alpha12 (63-90 deg); alpha23 (80-100 deg); sleeve station s3 (180-260 mm) and tilt azimuth psi3 (-60..+60 deg around the arm); J3 travel cap (+/-80 to +/-120 deg); link 2 path (lateral / posterolateral, nested over link 1 near J2 per the user's 'fully overlap' hint); branch sb.
prior_art: Humeral-rotation joints: CADEN-7 / EXO-UL7 (Perry, Rosen & Burns 2007), ARMin III / ArmeoPower (Nef, Guidali & Riener 2009) and L-EXOS all use open semicircular guides around the arm; here they are replaced by a GH-aimed rod near the cuff. The J1 pole is placed, like Harmony (Kim & Deshpande 2017) and ANYexo (Zimmermann et al. 2019), so that the singular direction falls outside the workspace. In this repo: family V and the tendon-driven 'Orbit Joint' in pipeline/arm-rom/RESEARCH_NOTES.md, and the arm-fixed ring travel limits in docs/FINDINGS.md.

name: Cam-scheduled 4R: the 4R's skin-hugging fold without a sagging spare (pin-in-slot coupling on the base)
topology: Scapula base -> J1 R (ACTIVE) -> link 1 -> J2 R (passive, scheduled) -> link 2, whose tail carries a roller pin -> J3 R (ACTIVE) -> link 3 -> J4 R (ACTIVE, arm hub) -> arm member -> the user's passive cuff slides (outside the count). Closure: the roller pin on link 2 runs in a circular slot cut in the base plate (a curved P plus the pin's R).
dof_reasoning: Spherical mobility: links 1-3 + the arm = 4 bodies (12 DOF), minus 2 x 4 for J1-J4 and 1 for the pin-in-slot (a point held on a curve), gives M = 3. The 4R's spare coordinate is no longer free: the slot ties q2 to q1 through the pin's position. J2, the pin's slide and the pin's roll are all set by closure, and only J1, J3 and J4 need driving or sensing. This fixes the documented R17 failure of the free 4R, whose spare falls within 0.1 s unpowered.
description: It looks like the r13 4R: a J1 hub on the base, then J2, J3, J4, with links that fold over the shoulder to hug it. Link 2 has a short tail that reaches back over the base plate, where a roller pin rides a circular slot in the plate on the acromion or spine (S-fixed). As the arm moves, the slot steers J2 along the fold the free 4R would have chosen to keep its links low (a fixed schedule instead of a per-pose choice). Rest, overhead, across-body and behind-back follow the seed 4R's metal placement as closely as one schedule allows; the slot and the tail add a small amount of base metal on S-fixed skin.
why_better: The 4R family hugs the shoulder better than 3R: the r13 4R's first build reached 58.9 % in band vs 34.8 % for the r13 3R, and the arm-rom stage measured 65-76 % coverage for 4 pivots vs 50-61 % for 3. The cam keeps much of that freedom while meeting the user's exactly-3-active rule and R17. A cam is not limited to the linear coupling that reached only ~50 %.
main_risk: A single schedule cannot be optimal for both overhead and behind-back (the arm-rom linear law lost 15-25 pts vs the free spare). The pin can lock where the slot is nearly parallel to the pin's J2 motion (pressure angle), causing a stall (R17). The extra tail and slot add metal and a fourth hub stack; links must keep >= 35 deg arcs (the short-link rule). The IK is a 1-D root search.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: q2 is held by the roller in the slot, so no joint sags; the roller is an MR63 bearing (rolling). Poses with a poor pressure angle are rejected by the IK and must be confirmed in judge/dynamics.py. MVP2: drums at J1, J3 and J4 (J2 is driven through the slot); encoders at those three, plus J2 optionally for diagnostics.
model_spec: COMMON as in lazy-tongs-polar: Q = S.T @ H @ H0.T; scapula frame; bench samples = (S @ X.T).T; skin-facing faces on a ~2 mm grid; 2-pass height fit; None on no closure, travel exceeded, or overlap. CHAIN: spherical 4R about GH with home = the chain's configuration at the rest pose, so R(q) = Q. Unit axes w1 (base), w2, w3, w4 (arm hub axis at rest) in the S frame. Seed from the r13 4R in pipeline/full-exo/designs/cad_r13_n4_s1343_1/design.json ('kinematics': az 61.0, el 57.8, arcs a = [23.9, 56.1, 29.6], w = [84.1, -10.8], branch -1; decode with bvec / w_dir / chain() in pipeline/conformal/gpu/band_impl.py), but enforce every link arc >= 35 deg. E(w, q) = Rodrigues rotation; R(q) = E(w1,q1) E(w2,q2) E(w3,q3) E(w4,q4). Coupling: pin direction pi0 (link 2 at home, on its tail) held on the base slot {x : x.n_s = cos(beta_s)}. IK PER POSE: scan q1 over [-180, 180) in 1 deg steps. For each q1: P1 = E(w1, q1); the slot gives q2 from (P1 E(w2, q2) pi0).n_s = cos(beta_s), i.e. A cos(q2) + B sin(q2) = C with v = P1^T n_s, A = (pi0 - (w2.pi0) w2).v, B = (cross(w2, pi0)).v, C = cos(beta_s) - (w2.pi0)(w2.v); two roots. For each root, M = E(w2, -q2) P1^T Q and g = w3.(M w4) - w3.w4. Find sign changes of g along q1 on each root branch and refine by bisection. Then q3 = the angle about w3 taking w4 to M w4 (Paden-Kahan subproblem 1), and q4 = the angle about w4 taking v to E(w3, -q3) M v for any v perpendicular to w4. Pick the root closest to the previous clip frame (workspace poses: closest to the median clip configuration). REJECT (None): no root; pressure-angle check |d(pi.n_s)/dq2| / |cross(pi, n_s)| < 0.25 at the solution, with pi = P1 E(w2, q2) pi0; or the remainder within 10 deg of its singularity (w3 parallel to M w4). METAL: hubs O20 at the current axis poles (axis k = E(w1,q1)...E(w_(k-1), q_(k-1)) w_k), radii fitted; straps 14 x 4 between consecutive poles; link 2's tail strap from the J2-J3 arc to the pin; pin as an O6 disc; slot track = an S-fixed band 14 mm wide along the small circle over the pin's travel (base metal).
sweep_params: 4R axes (az, el, arcs >= 35 deg, w); slot normal n_s (2 angles) and beta_s; pin direction pi0 on link 2's tail (2 angles); branch; pressure-angle threshold 0.15-0.35; optionally a 2-arc slot (two small circles joined tangentially) for a non-circular schedule.
prior_art: Polycentric 4-bar and cam knee orthoses. The coupled GH-elevation mechanisms of ARMin III / ChARMin (Nef 2009, Keller 2013). Harmony's parallelogram-coupled shoulder joint (Kim & Deshpande 2017). In this repo: the r13 4R (best first-build in-band share, R17 fail because the spare falls) and arm-rom's 'tendon-coupling the spare of D: ~50 % (single linear law)', which lists 'a cam (not linear) coupling of D's spare joint' as an open direction.

name: Floating-centre 3R: the spherical chain on a closure-set 3-axis float under J1, rigid cuff (no cuff slides)
topology: Scapula base plate on the user's handler -> passive 3-axis float (two crossed miniature roller slides in the base tangent plane, +/-12 mm, plus a +/-4 mm normal slide, about 5 mm under J1's hub) -> J1 R (ACTIVE) -> link 1 -> J2 R (ACTIVE) -> link 2 -> J3 R (ACTIVE, arm hub) -> arm member rigid on the user's cuff (no cuff slides).
dof_reasoning: A spherical 3R with concurrent axes, rigidly attached to the arm through the cuff, is mobile only if its centre coincides with the bone's GH. The float's 3 translations are exactly the 3 equations c = GH, so they are fixed by closure (no free coordinate). The arm keeps its 3 rotations, and only J1-J3 are driven or sensed. The float replaces the user's cuff slides as the passive self-aligning element (same counting rule), but at the base.
description: It is the champion 3R, except that J1's hub sits on a small float plate in the base and the arm member is rigid. As the handler slips over the bone (up to ~15 mm overhead, judge/base_slip.py) and the GH translates, the float lets the whole chain stay centred on the real GH. The links over the deltoid and arm keep their designed gap to the arm skin; only the base plate rides the slipping skin. At rest the float is centred; overhead (largest slip) it is displaced up to its travel; across-body and behind-back, by the slip law's few mm. The metal placement is the parent 3R's, plus about 5 mm under J1.
why_better: For a spherical chain on the handler, R10 is design-independent ('only the handler, the motions or a passive slider move it'). This puts the slider where it removes the misalignment for the whole chain rather than at the cuff, so R10 drops to about 0 within the float's travel. The arm-side metal (the arm-end hub zone holds ~60 % of the baseline's in-band skin) stays aligned with the arm under real GH motion, and the cuff becomes simple (no slides).
main_risk: Today's bench has no GH-vs-scapula translation, so on the plain bench this concept equals its parent; it needs the slip extension below to show anything. It is a topology modifier applicable to any spherical chain more than a new linkage. The float adds ~5 mm under J1 and ±12 mm of base travel. When the slipping skin carries the base and the bone carries the arm, it is unclear which side should stay aligned (the scapula-skin metal now gets -delta). The chain's weight moves onto the cuff (R11, small). In MVP2 only moments pass the float, so assist forces go through the human GH, as in all self-aligning exos.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the float is set by closure; crossed roller slides (~0.003 friction) and the parent chain's rolling joints keep it far under R17. MVP2: as the parent 3R (drums and encoders at J1-J3). The float passes the joint moments but not forces, so the assist reaches the arm as a pure moment about the real GH.
model_spec: COMMON as in lazy-tongs-polar (Q, scapula frame, bench samples = (S @ X.T).T, skin-facing faces on a ~2 mm grid, 2-pass height fit). PARENT: any spherical 3R pick, by default the champion chain in pipeline/full-exo/designs/cad_r18_n3_s1392_1_f300/design.json ('kinematics': az 32.6, el 80.6, a = [77.4, 81.4], w = [71.4, 4.8], branch -1; decode with bvec / w_dir / chain() in pipeline/conformal/gpu/band_impl.py), or r20 s1414 #4. Pure 3R closure, O20 hubs at the axis poles, 14 x 5.5 straps, J1 raised by 5 mm for the float. SLIP EXTENSION (the rig has none): per pose, from judge/base_slip.py, th, d = angles(np.c_[plane, elev], 'central') (error angles about the ISB scapula axes Xs, Ys, Zs, and the translation magnitude) and r = lever()[0]. Map ISB to the bench scapula frame with Zs ~ unit(0.5, 0, 0.87) (lateral along the spine, scapular plane 30 deg anterior), Ys ~ y, Xs = cross(Ys, Zs). R_err = rot(Xs, th0) rot(Ys, th1) rot(Zs, th2), with + signs, or the 'high' law's worst sign pattern as an option. delta = (R_err - I) r + d * t_hat, with t_hat = superior (swept). Classify each sample by the skin it rides: 'arm skin' if its nearest posed skin vertex is in BP.ARMV, else scapula/trunk skin (that skin slips with the handler). Evaluate the SAME chain twice and add the offsets before B.record. (a) parent, rigid base + cuff slides: chain samples over arm skin +delta, over scapula/trunk skin 0. (b) float: base-plate samples 0; chain samples (J1 onward) over scapula/trunk skin -delta, over arm skin 0. Return None in (b) if |delta tangent| > 12 or |delta normal| > 4 mm. Report reach / follow / in-band for (a) and (b), and the R10 number (max |delta| for (a); 0 within travel for (b)).
sweep_params: parent 3R (the top 5 band / CAD picks); float travel (8-15 mm tangent, 2-6 mm normal); float plane orientation; slip law (central / high) and the translation direction t_hat; J1 raise (3-6 mm).
prior_art: IntelliArm (Ren, Park & Zhang 2009): a passive GH-translation stage. NESM (Crea et al. 2016): passive self-alignment of the shoulder. AssistOn-SE (Ergin & Patoglu 2012): a self-aligning shoulder-elbow exoskeleton. Stienen et al. 2009 (IEEE TRO): only moments transmitted through decoupled translations. Here the self-aligning translation sits under J1 instead of at the cuff.

name: Back-anchored ring-ended 3R (top of the shoulder left bare)
topology: Scapula handler plate on the infraspinous fossa -> J1: ACTIVE R, a thin-section ring bearing (Kaydon Reali-Slim KAA type, 4.76 mm square section, pitch O45-60, open centre). Its axis u1 passes through GH and points posterior-medial-down (S-local lat -25..+5, lon -130..-100; nominal lat -10 / lon -120). The ring is seated where that ray meets the back, 85-150 mm from GH -> link 1 (shaped Ti strap 14 x 5.5, axis angle a12 70-110 deg) -> J2: ACTIVE R, O20 v5 hub (12.25 mm stack), axis through GH, placed by closure (nominally at the posterolateral corner of the acromion at rest, S lat ~25 / lon ~-40) -> link 2 (strap, a23 70-110) -> J3: ACTIVE R, a second thin-section ring (pitch O50-65) on the user's upper-arm cuff saddle. Its arm-fixed axis j3 passes through GH and pierces the lateral/posterolateral arm strip at s 110-150 mm, th 0..60 deg posterior of lateral -> upper-arm cuff / BOTTOM. There is no neck and no JN hub. All axes meet at GH.
dof_reasoning: A serial spherical 3R with no redundancy. For each arm orientation the three angles follow from closure in closed form (a two-cone solve for J2, then two azimuths), so the arm drives every joint and no coordinate is left to sag (R17). All three are rotary joints that can carry an encoder and, in MVP2, a cable drum. The user's passive cuff slides (outside the count) only absorb GH slip (R10); on the bench (GH fixed in S) they stay idle. Measured on the bench poses (u1 = S lat -22 / lon -119, j3 at s120 / th60): the J1-J3 angle stays 48-138 deg over 90 % of the workspace, 32-151 over all of it, and 50-138 on the fit clips. With a12 = a23 = 90 the singular boundaries are 0 and 180 deg, so the chain stays >= 42 deg from them on 90 % of poses and 29 deg in the worst pose. For comparison, FINDINGS reports 12.5-20 deg for earlier 3Rs, and a J1 at the dome pole reaches only 11-14 deg over the full workspace whatever arm-fixed J3 axis is chosen (measured). The cause: any arm-fixed axis's angle to a dome axis spans >= ~89-96 deg, reaching ~176 deg at rest.
description: Overhead-first placement. The skin that bunches overhead is the top of the shoulder (acromion and deltoid cap, 25-50 mm of radial change over the poses). That is exactly where a dome-rooted 3R puts its J1 hub and link-1 ribbon: the baseline's J1 is at S lat 80 / lon -57, 14 deg from the dome pole p*. This design leaves the top bare. J1 is a low ring (open centre, ~8 mm stack) lying on the infraspinous fossa; the S-fixed ray at lat 0 / lon -110 meets skin at 84-100 mm from GH in every bench pose. J3 is a second low ring on the user's cuff saddle on the lateral/posterolateral arm strip, where skin sits 55-65 mm from the humerus axis laterally and moves only 3-6 mm over all poses at s 120-210. Only J2 and the two straps cross the moving transition, and they do it over the back of the shoulder. REST: J1 is on the back of the scapula; link 1 rises laterally over the posterior deltoid to J2 at the posterolateral acromion corner (skin ~50-60 mm from GH); link 2 runs down the posterolateral arm to the J3 ring. OVERHEAD: the scapula's ~50 deg of upward rotation carries J1 up and lateral while the arm points up. The chain folds along the back of the shoulder and the back of the raised arm (stretched, smooth skin); the acromion and the subacromial bunch stay bare. ACROSS THE BODY: J3 on the posterolateral arm faces outward and the chain spans the posterior shoulder, which is stretched and smooth in that pose. BEHIND THE BACK: the arm extends and rotates internally, the posterolateral strip turns toward the back, and J2 / link 2 can be squeezed between the arm and the scapula. This is the case to watch.
why_better: (1) Singularity: about 42 deg of margin on 90 % of the workspace (29 deg in the worst pose), against 11-20 deg for dome-rooted 3Rs. (2) Nothing sits on the acromion. FINDINGS: Raise overhead at 142-150 deg is held up by link 1's J2 hub and ribbon on exactly that skin. (3) The arm end is a ring on stable skin instead of BOTTOM + neck + a JN hub 86-119 mm from GH. That removes the 'link 2 - neck' collisions that made up the whole R16 part-collision loss (14.2 % of workspace poses on r20 s1414 #0). (4) Two of the three 12.25 mm hub stacks become ~8 mm open rings; joint size is the lever FINDINGS values at ~20 points of workspace.
main_risk: Behind the back and Reach back pocket: a posterior route puts link 2 between the arm and the back. That is the same squeeze that holds 28 of 49 back-pocket frames on the baseline. Both straps are long (~90 deg arcs at 60-140 mm radius, ~150-200 mm each) and cross the posterior deltoid, which moves. The J1 site is sensitive. The ray at lat -22 / lon -119 sees skin at 123-198 mm (the back rolls away), so the base needs lat >= ~-15. That costs margin: lat -10 / lon -125 with j3 at s120 / th60 gives 60-147 deg (~33 deg margin, skin 141-153 mm, far but stable); lat 0 / lon -110 with j3 at s140 / th40 gives 63-156 deg (~24 deg). Thin-section rings of O45-65 are catalogue parts (KAA20-KAA25). Their tilt stiffness under MVP2 loads and their encoder integration are unproven here.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: three rolling R joints, driven by the arm through the cuff. The chain is non-redundant, so nothing can fall. A light-preload 4-point thin-section ring has ~0.01-0.03 N.m of friction, against the 1 N.m R17 limit; verify in judge/dynamics.py. MVP2: each ring's rotating race gets a cable groove on its OD (pitch radius 25-32 mm, 2.5-3x the O20 hub's lever, so less cable tension per N.m) and an encoder ring (multipole magnetic ring + Hall/AMR head, or an optical strip on the OD). J2 is a v5 O20 hub with its magnet + PCB and a drum groove on the hub rim.
model_spec: COMMON (repeated in every spec): B = CB.Bench(); for each pose i, f = B.frames(i), Rs = f['S'][0], Rh = f['H'][0]. Both translations are 0, so GH is the origin (thorax mm, x anterior, y up, z right) and spherical chains close exactly; the bench has no GH translation relative to the scapula, and R10 is judged elsewhere. An S-fixed vector v maps to Rs @ v; an arm-fixed one maps to Rh @ v. Arm-local frame (L = body_pose._rig().L): a = L['elbow']/|L['elbow']| is the humerus axis (elbow 325 mm from GH); z_L = rest_humerus @ [0,0,1] orthogonalised to a (lateral); y_L = a x z_L (posterior). Arm point (s, th, rho) = s a + rho (cos th z_L + sin th y_L): th 0 lateral, +90 posterior, -90 anterior. S-local direction (lat, lon) = (cos lat sin lon, sin lat, cos lat cos lon): lon 0 lateral, +90 anterior, -90 posterior, 180 medial. Dome pole p* = (lat 66, lon -68) = (-0.377, 0.914, 0.152). Two-cone solve TC(u, w, al, ga, br): k = u.w, D = 1 - k^2, x = (cos al - k cos ga)/D, y = (cos ga - k cos al)/D, z2 = (1 - x^2 - y^2 - 2xyk)/D. If D < 1e-6 or z2 < 0, the pose cannot be taken (record None); otherwise v = x u + y w + br sqrt(z2) (u x w). Serial singular margin = asin(|u.(v x w)| / sin ga); below 5 deg record None (an unpowered chain can flip branch there, R17). r_skin(i, d) is the outermost radius in [20, 170] mm where the ray rho d crosses the posed skin from inside to outside. Compute it with B.dist on a 5 mm ladder plus 4 bisection steps; do not use nearest-vertex cones, because the render skin is sparser than 2.5 deg over the acromion. Envelope fit EF(part, q): a rigid part is a set of part-local unit directions d_j with underside radii rho_j. Rp(i) is the part frame in pose i (Gram-Schmidt of the part's two joint-axis directions). rho_j = quantile_q over the fit poses of r_skin(i, Rp(i) d_j) + 2 mm, with q 0.85-1.0; poses above the quantile then show up as contact (not taken). For speed, fit on a coarse grid (4 mm along x 3 across) over every 3rd pose, then interpolate to the record grid. Joint keep-outs: an O20 v5 hub is a disc of radius 10 mm with the lower member's skin face at F, the upper member from F + 3.15 mm and the cap crown at F + 12.25 mm. A thin-section ring is an annulus ~8 mm wide (bearing + housings), ~8 mm stack, open centre, with the rotating member at +4.8 mm. Straps are 14 mm wide x 5.5 mm Ti. A ribbon leaves a joint plane at <= 60 deg. Pass only skin-facing samples (undersides, about 1 per 4 mm2) to B.record. Check everything else (hub walls, caps, upper members) with B.dist and record None if any point is < 0. Report B.report() plus the concept's diagnostics. SPECIFIC: Parameters: u1 (S-local lat/lon); r1 = r_skin along u1 in the rest pose + 3 (S-fixed ring seat radius); ring pitch radius p1 22-30 mm; a12, a23; j3 = unit(arm point (s3, th3, 60)); r3 = median over poses of r_skin along Rh j3 + 3 (arm-fixed seat); ring pitch p3; branch br; EF quantile q. Per pose: u = Rs u1, w = Rh j3, v = TC(u, w, a12, a23, br); record None if there is no closure or the margin is < 5 deg. Metal: (a) J1 ring: annulus of directions at cap angles (p1 - 4)/r1 .. (p1 + 4)/r1 rad around u, at radius r1. It is S-fixed; its rotating race and the link-1 root sit 4.8 mm higher. (b) J3 ring: the same around w at r3 (arm-fixed). (c) J2: an O20 disc around v, with underside radius r2 from EF over its footprint in the link-1 frame (Gram-Schmidt of u, v). (d) Link 1: a 14 mm ribbon from the J1 ring rim point nearest v to the J2 hub along slerp(u, v, t), with directions offset +-7 mm across and underside radii from EF in the link-1 frame; ramp <= 60 deg at the hub. (e) Link 2: the same from J2 to the J3 ring rim, in the frame (v, w). Extra outputs: a histogram of the singular margin, and a squeeze flag = share of poses where J2 or link 2 has body both below it (skin < 4 mm) and above it (B.dist < 0 at points 4 mm above its top surface).
sweep_params: u1 lat -25..+5, lon -130..-100 (and its skin seat radius); a12, a23 70-110 (90/90 nominal); j3 at s 100-160, th -20..+60; branch +-1; EF q 0.85-1.0; ring pitch radii 22-30 mm. Track reach, inband14, the 5th percentile of the singular margin, and the squeeze share.
prior_art: Spherical shoulder exoskeletons with a posterior base: Harmony (Kim & Deshpande 2017), ANYexo (Zimmermann et al. 2019), MGA (Carignan et al. 2005). Thin-section ring bearings as exoskeleton joints: the humeral-rotation rings of ARMin III (Nef et al. 2009) and CADEN-7 (Perry et al. 2007). A ring as the scapula-side joint on the infraspinous fossa, with the acromion deliberately left bare: none known.

name: Spherical lazy-tongs J2 (a scissor arc instead of a folding knee)
topology: S -> J1: ACTIVE R (O20 hub or ring), axis u1 through GH -> link 1 = a short end block (~12 deg of arc) -> J2: ACTIVE R about the remote axis u2 = unit(u1 x w), realised as a 1-DOF spherical scissor (lazy-tongs) of n = 4-8 cells. The scissor lies on the minor great-circle arc G from the J1 end block to the J3 end block. Every scissor pivot axis is radial through GH (MR63/MR85 miniature bearing pairs, ~5 mm stack). Each end block holds one fixed pivot and one pivot in a short passive arc slot, so the tongs leaves the two blocks only rotation about u2. J2 is measured at the first pivot (cell angle phi) -> link 2 = end block -> J3: ACTIVE R (O20 hub or ring), arm-fixed axis j3 through GH -> cuff. a12 = a23 = 90 deg, so the J1 and J3 piercing points both lie on G. There is no metal at the piercing point of u2.
dof_reasoning: Active joints are J1, J2 and J3. J2 is a remote rotation about u2; with a12 = a23 = 90 its angle equals the J1-J3 angle theta, so measuring the tongs measures J2 exactly. The tongs is a closed linkage of mobility 1: every scissor pivot and both end slots are functions of the measured cell angle phi (theta = n c(phi), with c the cell length). Because all pivot axes pass through GH, the two end blocks can only rotate about GH; the fixed-plus-slotted end pivots remove the cross-arc and spin rotations, leaving rotation about u2. The chain is therefore a non-redundant 3-DOF spherical chain with nothing undriven. Passive count for n = 6: 3n + 2 = 20 pivots minus the measured one = 19, plus 2 end slides = 21. All are coupled and set by closure, so none is a spare coordinate.
description: The excess problem: over the everyday workspace, the J1-J3 angle of any spherical 3R swings ~90-120 deg. Measured: >= ~89 deg for any dome J1 axis with any arm-fixed J3 axis, and 32-151 deg for the posterior site of back-anchored-ring-3r. A one-hub knee with both links >= ~60 deg then throws J2 far off the J1-J3 line in the short configuration: with the baseline's 77/81 deg links spanning ~69 deg, J2 sits ~78 deg sideways. That is why the baseline's J2 hub lands on the back over the medial scapula overhead. The lazy-tongs never leaves the J1-J3 great circle; the excess becomes band width, not sideways travel. With n = 6, link length lambda = 24 deg and r 65 mm, the band is ~8 mm wide when long and ~26 mm when short. REST: J1 is on the scapula (dome or posterior site), J3 on the arm, and the tongs lies on the direct arc between them over the deltoid. OVERHEAD: the tongs contracts in place between the J1 site and the raised arm (short for a dome J1, long for a posterior J1; the sweep decides). No knee is thrown over the medial scapula, and nothing has to rise over the bunching acromion except the band itself. ACROSS THE BODY and BEHIND THE BACK: the tongs stays on the J1-J3 arc, so it crosses wherever that arc crosses (the posterior shoulder for the posterior site). The metal near the skin is many slim links (5 x 2 mm Ti) in two layers 2.5 mm apart, with pivots ~5 mm tall.
why_better: It removes the knee excursion that every folding spherical 3R has. There is no J2 hub stack at all, and no metal at the J2 axis. The metal stays on the shortest arc between the two joint sites in every pose, so if J1 and J3 sit on stable skin, the only metal on moving skin is a narrow band on a short path. Cells near the two ends travel very little and can be shaped low.
main_risk: Mechanical complexity: ~20 pivots (miniature bearing pairs) whose backlash and friction add up. Toggle: as the cells straighten in the long configuration the force ratio blows up, so keep the cell angle >= 15 deg. The middle cells slide along the arc over different skin as the tongs extends, so their undersides must clear the highest skin on their whole travel. The crossing link layers create shear and pinch points (left to the cover). The band is ~26 mm wide when short. Stiffness across the sphere depends on the pin stacks. MVP2 loads (~10 N.m) through slender scissor links need FEA.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the arm drives J1, J3 and the 1-DOF tongs, and nothing floats. Rolling friction at ~20 miniature bearings is small. At small cell angles the tongs resists being pulled straight (toggle), so check R17 with the toggle margin. MVP2: J2 is driven by a cable on a drum at the first pivot (angle phi). The transmission ratio dtheta/dphi = n dc/dphi varies with phi; this is the only nonlinear drive in the set and needs calibration. J2 is sensed with a v5-style magnet + PCB at that pivot. J1 and J3 are v5 hubs or rings with drums and encoders.

SPECIFIC: Choose u1 (S-local), j3 (arm-local), n and lambda (deg). Per pose: u = Rs u1, w = Rh j3, theta = angle(u, w). Record None if theta/n > lambda cos 15deg (toggle), theta/n < lambda sin 20deg (fully closed), or theta < 25 or > 165 deg (end blocks collide / J1-J3 margin). Arc frame: g = unit(w - (w.u) u), e = unit(u x g); an arc point (t along G from u, c across, both in rad) maps to the direction d = cos c (cos t u + sin t g) + sin c e. Cell length L = theta/n; half-width h = 0.5 sqrt(lambda^2 - L^2) (planar approximation, good enough for screening). Side pivots at (kL, +-h) for k = 0..n; centre pivots at ((k+0.5)L, 0). Radii: layer A at rho_k and layer B at rho_k + 2.5 mm; rho_k is fitted per cell by EF over all poses on the union of that cell's footprints (it moves with theta). Sample each link as a 5 mm wide strip on a 2 mm grid, pivots as O8 discs, the end blocks as plates, and J1/J3 as O20 hubs (COMMON). prior_art: Spherical scissor linkages from deployable structures: Hoberman's expanding sphere (US 4,942,700, 1990) and Gan & Pellegrino 2006 (closed-loop deployable structures). Lazy-tongs appear in reachers and surgical retractors. None known in exoskeletons.

name: 3R with a rolling-cone J2 (no hub and no stack at the knee)
topology: S -> J1: ACTIVE R (O20 hub or ring), axis u1 through GH -> link 1, ending in a conical rocker C1 (apex at GH, axis c1 fixed in link 1, cap half-angle kappa 10-25 deg) -> J2: ACTIVE 1-DOF rolling-contact joint. Cone C2 at the start of link 2 (same kappa) rolls on C1 without slip, held by crossed thin metal bands (the Jacob's-ladder / CORE arrangement: two outer bands one way, one inner band the other way). Both links lie in the same layer at the knee -> link 2 -> J3: ACTIVE R (O20 hub or ring), arm-fixed axis j3 through GH -> cuff.
dof_reasoning: The banded rolling pair is a 1-DOF joint. The bands forbid slip, and J1 and J3 forbid any translation (each link can only rotate about GH), so the cones can neither separate nor slide along their contact line. The relative motion is R_rel(t) = Rot(c1, t) Rot(c2_0, t): the orbit of c2 about c1 plus the equal spin of equal cones, a 1-parameter spherical motion. With J1 and J3 the chain is non-redundant: 3 active coordinates, and closure fixes t, q1 and q3. The active coordinate t is sensed across the contact (a magnet in one rocker, a Hall sensor in the other) and is drivable in MVP2 by a cable on a rocker. There are no passive coordinates; the bands are part of the joint, not a degree of freedom.
description: Overhead-first: the overhead pose is where the chain's knee is sharpest (the J1-J3 angle is at one extreme). It is also where a 12.25 mm O20 stack plus the 3.15 mm upper-member step lifts the knee furthest off skin that is bunching. A rolling-contact knee puts both links in one layer (5.5 mm, no step, no cap). Its instantaneous axis rolls along the rockers, so the knee is rounded over ~2 kappa of arc instead of a point, and the joint has no bearing at all: pure rolling, the user's 'very high quality bearings' taken literally. REST: like a 3R with J2 over the posterior/lateral shoulder, but flat; the two rockers sit side by side ~5.5 mm above the skin. OVERHEAD: the rockers have rolled toward one end; the knee lies flat wherever the kinematics put it (choose the back-anchored J1 site of back-anchored-ring-3r or the dome). ACROSS THE BODY and BEHIND THE BACK: the metal sits as for the 3R with the same axes, minus the hub stack at J2.
why_better: It removes the tallest feature on the moving transition: J2's 12.25 mm stack and the 3.15 mm step, which FINDINGS show cost both stand-off and part collisions (R6/R16). It rounds the knee, keeping a folding chain's excursion closer to the skin, and it is the lightest possible J2. It can be combined with any J1/J3 placement (dome or posterior) and with ring ends.
main_risk: Scope: the joint is held by crossed thin metal bands (a rolling-contact / CORE joint), not a pin and bearing. The user excluded pulleys and cables as transmissions; bands used as joint retention need the user's OK. The bands carry all tension across the knee and flex on every cycle (fatigue in all-day wear). The cone pair must be accurate to GH, because apex error becomes misalignment. Rolling range per rocker is limited: a J2 range of ~90-120 deg needs ~45-60 deg of rocker travel each. The a12/a23 >= ~60 deg rule still applies, so the knee still swings far sideways (rounded, but not removed).
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: arm-driven; rolling contact has near-zero friction, so R17 is easy as long as the bands keep no-slip. MVP2: a cable wrapped on rocker C2 drives t (the rocker is the drum, radius r sin kappa ~ 11-27 mm); t is sensed by a magnet/Hall pair across the contact or a strip encoder on a band. J1 and J3 are v5 hubs or rings with drums and encoders.

SPECIFIC: Parameters: u1 (S-local) and j3 (arm-local); kappa; b1 = angle(u1, c1) 50-100 deg; b2 = angle(c2, j3) 50-100 deg; the azimuth sigma of c2_0 about c1; the t range [t0, t1]; a root branch. Link-1 coordinates: c1 = z, u1 in the x-z plane at angle b1 from z; c2_0 at angle 2 kappa from c1 at azimuth sigma. Link-2 coordinates coincide with link-1 coordinates at t = 0, with j3_l2 given in them at angle b2 from c2_0. R_rel(t) = Rot(c1, t) Rot(c2_0, t). IK per pose: let u = Rs u1, w = Rh j3. The angle between u and w equals angle(u1, R_rel(t) j3_l2) in link-1 coordinates, which depends only on t. Scan t over [t0, t1] at 1 deg and bisect to the root on the chosen branch; record None if there is no root. Then q1 is the rotation about u1 that maps R_rel(t) j3_l2 (link-1 coordinates) onto Rs^T w, and q3 follows from the remaining frame. L1 = Rs Rot(u1, q1); L2 = L1 R_rel(t). Conditioning: finite-difference the map (q1, t, q3) -> arm rotation and take sigma_min of the 3x3 Jacobian (rad/rad); record None below 0.1. Metal: rocker C1 is the arc of directions at cap angle kappa about c1 covering the contact azimuths used over [t0, t1], 10 mm wide at radius rho_k (EF). Rocker C2 is the same about L2 c2_0, at the same radius and in the same layer (no stack). Link ribbons (14 x 5.5) run from the J1 hub to C1 and from C2 to the J3 hub (EF in the link frames); J1/J3 hubs as in COMMON. Run the same axes with an O20 hub at J2 as the control.
sweep_params: kappa 10-25 deg; b1, b2 50-100 deg; sigma; t range; J1 and j3 sites (posterior anchor from back-anchored-ring-3r, or the dome); branch; EF q 0.85-1.0.
prior_art: Rolling-contact joints: CORE (Cannon & Howell 2005), the Jacob's-ladder hinge, and rolling-contact knees in prosthetics and exoskeletons. Rolling cones with their apex at the joint centre, used in a shoulder exoskeleton: none known.

name: Revolved-lamellae pauldron (every joint a large thin ring, links nest as revolved shells)
topology: S -> J1: ACTIVE R as a large thin-section ring (pitch radius 20-40 mm), axis u1 through GH -> link 1 = a dished Ti lame (1.5-2 mm). Wherever it overlaps a neighbour around a ring, it is a surface of revolution about that ring's axis -> J2: ACTIVE R ring about u2 (pitch radius 20-40) -> link 2 lame -> J3: ACTIVE R ring about the arm-fixed axis j3 (on the lateral arm strip) -> cuff. Spherical 3R kinematics with general a12 and a23. Every joint is an open ring, and every link is a shell segment that nests over its neighbour like the lames of a pauldron.
dof_reasoning: The same as any spherical 3R: three rotary joints, non-redundant, closed-form closure, nothing sags. The lames are rigid links, and their overlap (one shell sliding over the next about the shared axis) adds no DOF. Each ring is a drivable, sensable joint.
description: This takes the user's own hint: 'if they could fully overlap each other, you'd get rid of a lot of collision issues ... within 14mm'. Two members that turn relative to each other about an axis can overlap with a constant gap only if their facing surfaces are surfaces of revolution about that axis. So each joint becomes a large open ring, and the two links overlap around it as revolved dishes (2 mm + 0.5 mm gap + 2 mm). The dish profile follows the skin's radial profile around that axis, and the lames are free-form away from the rings (EF). Overhead-first: the folded overhead chain is a stack of up to three lames (~7.5 mm + liner) instead of hubs standing 12.25 mm proud. J1's ring sits on the dome (skin 39-68 mm from GH, < ~11 mm change). REST: the lames lie like a pauldron over the top and side of the shoulder, with the J3 ring on the stable lateral arm strip. OVERHEAD: the lames slide over each other around the rings and stack on the top/back of the shoulder; the J2 ring still sits wherever the kinematics put it (a >= ~60 deg). ACROSS THE BODY and BEHIND THE BACK: the lames turn about the J3 ring on the arm strip and about J2, and their revolved overlap zones cannot collide in any pose.
why_better: No hub stacks: ~8 mm open rings replace the 12.25 mm O20 hubs, the lever FINDINGS values at ~20 points of workspace. No link-link collisions near joints by construction (coaxial revolved surfaces), which removes the R6/R16 part collisions. A large ring carries tilt moments at low ball load (pitch O60 against O11 for the MR117 pair, about 5x the lever), which matters for MVP2's 10 N.m.
main_risk: The skin under a revolved overlap zone is not a surface of revolution about the joint axis. A ring at a 25 deg cap angle around p* sees skin at 39-68 mm around its circumference (up to 116 mm in the neck sector), so the dish must clear the highest point on its circle and stands off elsewhere. Pick each axis by its revolvedness (a sweep objective). Shells cover more skin and weigh more (~25-40 g per ring plus 1.5-2 mm lames), still well under 500 g. The kinematics are a 3R's, so the J2 knee excursion overhead remains. Large-ring housings are custom.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: three light-preload rings driven by the arm, non-redundant; friction ~0.01-0.03 N.m per ring, well under R17. MVP2: each ring's OD is a cable drum (pitch 20-40 mm, more torque per newton of cable than the O20 hub) and carries a magnetic or optical encoder ring.
model_spec: COMMON (repeated in every spec): B = CB.Bench(); for each pose i, f = B.frames(i), Rs = f['S'][0], Rh = f['H'][0]. Both translations are 0, so GH is the origin (thorax mm, x anterior, y up, z right) and spherical chains close exactly; the bench has no GH translation relative to the scapula, and R10 is judged elsewhere. An S-fixed vector v maps to Rs @ v; an arm-fixed one maps to Rh @ v. Arm-local frame (L = body_pose._rig().L): a = L['elbow']/|L['elbow']| is the humerus axis (elbow 325 mm from GH); z_L = rest_humerus @ [0,0,1] orthogonalised to a (lateral); y_L = a x z_L (posterior). Arm point (s, th, rho) = s a + rho (cos th z_L + sin th y_L): th 0 lateral, +90 posterior, -90 anterior. S-local direction (lat, lon) = (cos lat sin lon, sin lat, cos lat cos lon): lon 0 lateral, +90 anterior, -90 posterior, 180 medial. Dome pole p* = (lat 66, lon -68) = (-0.377, 0.914, 0.152). Two-cone solve TC(u, w, al, ga, br): k = u.w, D = 1 - k^2, x = (cos al - k cos ga)/D, y = (cos ga - k cos al)/D, z2 = (1 - x^2 - y^2 - 2xyk)/D. If D < 1e-6 or z2 < 0, the pose cannot be taken (record None); otherwise v = x u + y w + br sqrt(z2) (u x w). Serial singular margin = asin(|u.(v x w)| / sin ga); below 5 deg record None (an unpowered chain can flip branch there, R17). r_skin(i, d) is the outermost radius in [20, 170] mm where the ray rho d crosses the posed skin from inside to outside. Compute it with B.dist on a 5 mm ladder plus 4 bisection steps; do not use nearest-vertex cones, because the render skin is sparser than 2.5 deg over the acromion. Envelope fit EF(part, q): a rigid part is a set of part-local unit directions d_j with underside radii rho_j. Rp(i) is the part frame in pose i (Gram-Schmidt of the part's two joint-axis directions). rho_j = quantile_q over the fit poses of r_skin(i, Rp(i) d_j) + 2 mm, with q 0.85-1.0; poses above the quantile then show up as contact (not taken). For speed, fit on a coarse grid (4 mm along x 3 across) over every 3rd pose, then interpolate to the record grid. Joint keep-outs: an O20 v5 hub is a disc of radius 10 mm with the lower member's skin face at F, the upper member from F + 3.15 mm and the cap crown at F + 12.25 mm. A thin-section ring is an annulus ~8 mm wide (bearing + housings), ~8 mm stack, open centre, with the rotating member at +4.8 mm. Straps are 14 mm wide x 5.5 mm Ti. A ribbon leaves a joint plane at <= 60 deg. Pass only skin-facing samples (undersides, about 1 per 4 mm2) to B.record. Check everything else (hub walls, caps, upper members) with B.dist and record None if any point is < 0. Report B.report() plus the concept's diagnostics. SPECIFIC: The kinematics are those of back-anchored-ring-3r: parameters u1, a12, a23, j3, br; per pose u = Rs u1, w = Rh j3, v = TC(u, w, a12, a23, br). Ring k (axis a_k = u, v or w; seat radius r_k; pitch p_k) has a footprint annulus of directions at cap angles (p_k - 4)/r_k .. (p_k + 4)/r_k around a_k. Overlap zone k covers cap angles (p_k + 4)/r_k .. (p_k + 4 + o_k)/r_k, with o_k 10-25 mm. In it the lower member sits on a REVOLVED profile R_k(psi) = max over poses, and over all azimuths around a_k that the zone occupies in the frame of the member below, of r_skin + 2. The upper member sits at R_k(psi) + 2.5. Lame bodies between overlap zones are 20 mm wide ribbons along the great circle between ring rims, fitted by EF in the link frame. Sample all undersides. Revolvedness score per ring site: the std of r_skin over 24 azimuths on the circle at cap angle (p_k + 10)/r_k, median over poses (smaller is better); use it as a prefilter for axis sites. Run the same axes with O20 hubs and 14 mm straps as the control, to isolate the realisation effect.
sweep_params: u1 (dome and posterior sites); a12, a23 60-110; j3 at s 100-160, th -45..+60; branch; ring pitch radii 20-40 mm; overlap width 10-25 mm; EF q 0.85-1.0. Objectives: inband14 and reach, with revolvedness as a cheap prefilter.
prior_art: Articulated plate armour (pauldron lames on sliding rivets). Thin-section ring bearings as exoskeleton joints: the humeral-rotation rings of ARMin III (Nef et al. 2009) and CADEN-7 (Perry et al. 2007). An all-ring spherical chain with nested revolved links: none known.

name: 3-RUS tripod that uses the wearer's own GH as the spherical centre
topology: S -> three ACTIVE R crank hubs (O20 v5). Their axes do NOT pass through GH (near skin-normal), and the pivots sit on stable scapula skin: the dome near p*, the posterior scapula (lat -10..+10 / lon -125..-100) and the top-front of the acromion (lat ~50 / lon ~10), 55-130 mm from GH -> crank i (radius rc 20-55 mm) -> passive U joint (miniature needle-bearing cardan, O10) -> rigid curved strut i (Ti tube O6 or a 6 x 4 bar, chord length 90-220 mm, bent to follow the deltoid) -> passive S joint (ball, O8-10) in a socket on an arm-fixed bracket at b_i on the user's cuff / arm strip (s 80-180, th -90..+90). The wearer's GH closes the loop; there is no exo joint at GH. Variant switch: telescoping straight struts with an ACTIVE P (linear encoder) and no crank (3-UPS).
dof_reasoning: Each R-U-S leg has 6 joint DOF, so it imposes exactly one constraint: |c_i(phi_i) - b_i| = L_i. The anatomical GH removes the arm's 3 translations, which leaves exactly 3 DOF, set by the three crank angles. Every U and S angle is fixed by closure. The U joint (not a ball) at the crank end blocks the strut's spin about its chord, so a curved strut cannot swing round; there is no idle or spare coordinate. Count under the user's rule: 3 active (the cranks); 15 passive coordinates (3 x (2 + 3)), all set by the arm.
description: The cranks live only on stable scapula skin: the dome (skin 39-68 mm from GH, < ~11 mm change, never visited by the humerus), the infraspinous fossa and the top-front of the acromion. Nothing rigid has to follow the moving transition except three slim struts, which can be bent to hug it. REST: three 'suspenders' run from the cranks over the deltoid cap to balls on the anterolateral, lateral and posterolateral arm strip. OVERHEAD: the arm balls come within ~70 deg of the dome pivots and the chord lengths shrink. Measured: dome pivot to a lateral ball at s150, 145-222 mm over all poses; to an anterolateral ball at s100, 100-171 mm. The cranks swing to take up the change and the struts fold along the top and back of the raised arm, so the bunching acromion only has to clear O6 rods. ACROSS THE BODY: the posterior strut stretches across the back of the shoulder and the anterior one shortens over the front. BEHIND THE BACK: the arm extends and rotates internally, and the anterior strut must cross the front of the shoulder without entering the pectoral fold (risk).
why_better: No joint stacks on the transition: the 12.25 mm hubs live only on stable scapula skin, and the transition carries only O6 struts. In MVP2 all three motors sit at the base on cables and the arm side is three passive balls (the lowest arm-side mass of any concept). It is self-aligning by construction: with no exo rotation centre, a GH centre that translates or a handler that slips (R10) only changes the crank angles and never forces the arm. There is no serial-wrist singularity.
main_risk: Conditioning, measured. With pivots ~60 mm from GH and balls 52-72 mm off the humerus axis, every pivot-ball pair tried has some pose whose chord line passes within 1-4 mm of GH (that strut then has no lever about GH). The smallest singular value of the 3x3 strut-moment matrix reaches ~0 for both triples tried (5th percentile 0.006-0.009 per 100 mm). So there are Type-II singularities inside the workspace: there the arm can rotate without moving the cranks, and an unpowered tripod loses tracking (R3, R17). Pivots far from GH on the scapula body and balls on brackets away from the humerus axis may fix it, at a cost in stand-off. Chord ranges of 70-110 mm need 35-55 mm cranks, which sweep large areas. MVP1 orientation comes from forward kinematics with an assumed GH, so slip shows up as tracking error. Miniature U-joints with rolling bearings are scarce.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the arm drives the cranks through the struts. At a crank dead centre (crank collinear with its strut, |P_i - b_i| = L_i +- rc) the arm cannot push the crank through; it stalls or flips branch, so keep the crank-strut angle >= 15 deg off collinear. In a Type-II singularity the arm moves freely without tracking. MVP2: the crank hubs take cable drums at the base (all three motors remote on the scapula side), and each crank hub has a v5 magnet + PCB encoder, giving the 3 active coordinates. In the telescoping variant, a linear encoder and a push-pull cable per strut.
