I know of no exo that realises a spherical 3R as a scapula-fixed arch crossed by an arm-fixed collar with a double carriage at the crossing.

name: Skin-following cam rails with a telescoping crossing (profiled-radius version of the crossed rails)
topology: Same chain as crossed-muscle-rails, but the rails are not spheres. Scapula base -> R1 = carriage 1 on a scapula-fixed rail whose directions lie on the cone (a1, a12) and whose radius r1(phi) follows the scapula skin [ACTIVE] -> C2 = cylindrical joint on the radial axis a2 at the crossing: rotation [ACTIVE] + radial slide along a2 [PASSIVE, set by the two rail profiles] (rolling ball spline / linear ball bushing) -> R3 = carriage 2 on an arm-fixed rail on the cone (a3, a23) whose radius r2(psi) follows the arm skin; the rail continues down the lateral arm as the neck to BOTTOM [ACTIVE] -> arm.
dof_reasoning: A translation along an axis that passes through the GH centre does not change the orientation a spherical chain transmits. So each carriage may move radially as it travels without changing the 3R kinematics. Carriage 1 sits at r1(phi), set by rail 1's profile at its position; carriage 2 sits at r2(psi). Both phi and psi are functions of the arm pose (the 3R's two-cone closure), so the J2 slide length r2(psi) - r1(phi) is set by closure. That makes it a passive element driven by the chain, outside the active count (user rule 2026-10-15). It cannot sag because both carriages are captive on rails whose profiles fix it. Active: J1 (rail-1 position), J2 rotation, J3 (rail-2 position), which are the 3R's three coordinates.
description: The same picture as the crossed rails, but each rail is a 3-D curve that hugs its own skin. The exo-acromial arch dips to 2-4 mm over the acromion, where the skin is low (37-45 mm from GH), and rises over the supraspinatus / spine (55-60 mm). The arm collar follows the deltoid cap (45-64 mm across poses in the arm frame), then carries on down the lateral arm as the neck to BOTTOM, following the arm skin. At the crossing, a short ball-spline post on the J2 axis lets the two carriages sit at different heights: one carriage stack plus 0-15 mm of slide. Rest, overhead, across-body and behind-back: as in the crossed rails (the crossing travels along both rails). The difference is that the rails keep a constant clearance from their own skin instead of a constant radius, and the slide post grows where the arm rail's skin is higher than the arch's.
why_better: It removes the crossed rails' first weakness: a constant-radius rail over skin whose radius varies (37-58 mm along an arch over the top; 45-64 mm around the cap) loses band wherever the spread exceeds the 12 mm window. Here each rail's in-band ceiling is set only by the skin motion in its own frame (scapula top 1.8-3.5 mm; arm cap band ~12 mm), not by its shape. The proximity analysis classed 44 of the baseline's lost points as 'motion' that no reshaping on its path can recover. Profiled body-fixed rails turn most of that into slack that the profile can remove. The arm rail also doubles as the neck: the baseline's arm end + neck cover 34 % of the covered skin at 61 / 35 % in band, and here one part replaces three.
main_risk: (1) The slide post: where r2 - r1 at the crossing exceeds the carriage stack by more than 15-20 mm, J2 becomes a tall post. The upper rail's profile must then be raised to keep the slide short, which costs band. (2) The ball spline carries the J2 tilt moment (10 N.m in MVP2), which drives its section size and friction. (3) Non-circular rails need custom carriages that follow a varying radius and curvature (4 wheels on a 3-D curve). They are harder to make and to keep free of play, and need 5-axis machining. (4) All of the crossed rails' other risks remain (rail length, stack, tangency).
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: both carriages are captive and the slide is set by the profiles, so there is no free coordinate. Friction comes from two rail carriages and one ball spline (rolling, mu ~0.005). The slide's axial load is the radial component of the cuff force, which is small in MVP1 (< 5 N). MVP2: J1 and J3 are driven by cables. The cable cannot sit in a plain groove on a 3-D profiled rail, so use a closed channel, or a constant-radius drum sector fixed beside the rail, about the rail's own axis. J2 is driven by a v5 hub drum on the spline's outer sleeve. Sensing: arc scales on both rails and a magnet / IC on J2; the slide needs no sensing.
model_spec: Conventions as in crossed-muscle-rails: scapula dir -> S_R(i) d; arm dir (canonical, w_dir) -> H_R(i) @ RH @ d, with RH = BP._rig().L['rest_humerus']; GH origin; numpy band_impl.circ_int. KINEMATICS, extents, branch and None rules: exactly as crossed-muscle-rails pass 1 / pass 2 (same params a1, a12, a3, a23, sigma, gamma_min, Lmax and the same seeds). PROFILES: sample each rail every 2 deg along its extent x 3 across (b = 0, +-5 mm), giving body-frame directions d_k. Shaping poses = the bench's fit-clip poses + workspace poses (held-out clips are never in it). For each pose i, take the points r * R_i d_k for r = 30, 32, ..., 150 (R_i = S_R for rail 1, H_R RH for rail 2) and make one batched B.dist call per pose. r_exit(i, k) = the largest r with dist < 0 (0 if none). r_need(k) = max_i r_exit + 2.5. Rail directions with r_need > 85 are unusable: trim the extent to avoid them, and return None for poses that need them. r_low(s) = moving max of r_need over +-6 mm along the rail, then a smoothing spline with curvature radius >= 15 mm, + 0.5. Upper rail: r_up(psi) = max(its own smoothed r_need, max over closing poses with psi_i = psi of r_low(phi_i) + Delta_min), with Delta_min = 12, smoothed the same way. Slide stroke s_i = r_up(psi_i) - r_low(phi_i) - Delta_min; return None if s_i > stroke_max (15 mm). METAL per pose (skin faces, 2 mm grid): rail 1 at its profile along its directions, mapped by S_R; rail 2 at its profile, mapped by H_R RH; carriage = a disc of 13 mm arc radius around a2 at the lower rail's profile radius. Arm-rail neck: continue rail 2 beyond its travel end nearest BOTTOM, along the great circle, to BOTTOM's cut end (canonical ~(0, -70, 67.5)), profiled by the same r_need rule in the arm frame. Contact-only points: rail tops (+5), and the slide post as a 12 mm-radius cylinder along a2 from r_low to r_up + 6. Record the skin faces with B.record. REPORT: profile ranges, slide strokes, rail lengths.
sweep_params: The same kinematic params as crossed-muscle-rails; Delta_min (10-14 mm); stroke_max (10-25 mm); clearance (2-4 mm); profile smoothing radius (10-25 mm); arm rail as neck on/off; which rail is lower.
prior_art: Self-aligning exos with passive prismatic joints set by closure (Schiele & van der Helm 2006, kinematic compatibility; Stienen et al. 2009, Dampace); cam-follower guides; ball-spline cylindrical joints. I have not seen body-profiled crossing rails.

name: Pauldron: lobster-tail lames as a remote-centre J2 that shares the elevation like the skin (scapulohumeral rhythm inside the mechanism)
topology: Serial spherical 3R with a12 = a23 = 90 deg and no J2 hub. Scapula base -> J1 = v5 O20 hub on the exo-scapula top (axis a1 through GH) [ACTIVE] -> lame 0 -> N-2 intermediate lames [PASSIVE: each held at a fixed share k/(N-1) of the J2 extension by an equal-share coupling, either pin-in-slot or a small lazy-tongs strip along the lame centreline] -> lame N-1. J2 = the stack's total extension, a remote-centre rotation about a2 (the normal of the great circle through J1 and J3) [ACTIVE] -> J3 = v5 O20 hub at the arm's low-motion spot (axis a3) [ACTIVE] -> arm piece -> BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning: J1, J2 and J3 are the three revolutes of a spherical 3R with 90/90 arcs. a2 = unit(A1 x A3), and the J2 coordinate is the arc angle theta13 = angle(A1, A3), so all three are functions of the arm pose. The intermediate lames (N-2; 2 at N = 4) are extra bodies whose angles are fixed fractions of theta13 through the coupling, a linkage with no gears or cables. So they are set by closure, cannot sag and need no sensing: passive elements outside the active count. Active: the J1 hub, the J2 stack extension and the J3 hub.
description: A row of 3-5 overlapping curved Ti lames, like a plate-armour pauldron or a lobster tail. It runs from a hub on top of the shoulder (exo-acromion) down over the deltoid cap to a hub on the arm just under the acromion edge. Each lame is a spherical band 24-40 mm wide and ~3 mm thick that slides on the one below along circular tracks about a2, with rolling elements at the band edges. The coupling keeps the gaps equal, so each lame turns a fixed share of the elevation: lame k moves like the skin k/(N-1) of the way from the acromion to the arm. The lame radii rise by one lame thickness toward the arm, matching the skin, which rises from the acromion (41-50 mm) to the cap (55-60 mm). Rest: the stack is extended down over the lateral cap. Overhead: the arm hub rises toward the top hub and the lames telescope together under the acromion. Across-body: the stack swings forward about J1 and extends over the front of the cap. Behind-back: it swings back over the posterior cap and extends.
why_better: It deletes the J2 hub, the baseline's worst zone (18.5 % of the covered skin at 0.7 % in band), together with link 2's ribbon. The J2 rotation happens in nested circular tracks about the GH centre instead of in a hub standing on moving skin. J1 and J3 sit on the two best-ground spots measured: the scapula top (1.8-3.5 mm skin motion, ceiling 100 %) and the arm spot w(112,-15) (disc ceiling 94 %; the baseline's JN hub rides at 39.5 %). The lames interpolate the skin motion between the scapula and arm frames, instead of one rigid link riding in one frame over skin that moves with the other.
main_risk: Span ratio: J1-J3 spans 46-128 deg on the bench fit clips (2.8x) and 27-150 deg over the workspace for top / tubercle placements (my check). That needs N >= 4 lames with ~30 % overlap (max/min = 1 + (N-1)(1 - overlap) = 3.1 at N = 4), so the workspace extremes stay out of reach. The stack thickness (N x ~3 mm + rolling elements) lifts the outer lames. There are many track surfaces (friction, and pinch points between lames, which are the cover's job), and the coupling is fiddly. Thin lames must carry MVP2's 10 N.m through ~25 mm-wide bands. The chain is singular when theta13 -> 0 or 180 deg (kept within 25-155).
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the hubs and the stack are driven by the arm, and the intermediate lames are held by the coupling, so there is no free coordinate. Friction comes from two hubs plus (N-1) lame tracks on caged balls or needle rollers, and the coupling's tiny pivots. MVP2: J1 and J3 use cable drums on their v5 hubs. J2 uses a cable pulling the last lame along the stack's circular track about a2; the track is a circle about GH, so it acts as a natural drum of radius ~55 mm. Sensing: v5 magnet / IC on J1 and J3; J2 by an arc scale on the last lame's track (or the coupling's first pivot angle).
model_spec: Conventions: scapula dir -> S_R(i) d; arm dir (canonical, w_dir) -> H_R(i) @ RH @ d, with RH = BP._rig().L['rest_humerus']; GH origin. PARAMS: a1 = bvec(az1, el1) (seed (15, 80)); a3 = w_dir(d3, az3) (seed (112, -15)); N (4); lame span Lam (45 deg); overlap ov (0.3); half-width hw (14 mm); lame thickness tl (3 mm); lame order 'rising' (lame k skin face = rhoL + k*tl) or 'falling'. HEIGHTS: rho0 (J1 base pad face) = lowest legal radius of the pad over the fit-clip frames (smallest radius, 0.5 mm steps, with every sample >= 2 mm from the skin by B.dist). rhoL = max(rho0 + 3.15, the lowest legal radius of lame 0). Raise all lames together if any lame violates its own lowest legal radius. VALIDITY: [th_min, th_max] = the fit-clip range of theta13 +-3 deg. The design is valid iff th_max <= Lam*(1 + (N-1)(1 - ov)) and th_min >= Lam + 2*asin(12/rho) in deg. PER POSE: A1 = S_R a1; A3 = H_R RH a3; theta = angle(A1, A3). Return None if theta is outside [th_min, th_max] or [25, 155]. a2 = unit(A1 x A3); e = unit(a2 x A1), so that A3 = cos(theta) A1 + sin(theta) e. Lame k starts at lam_k = k (theta - Lam)/(N-1) and covers lam in [lam_k, lam_k + Lam]. Its directions are cos(mu)(cos(lam) A1 + sin(lam) e) + sin(mu) a2 for mu in +-hw/rho_k. METAL (skin faces, 2 mm grid): the J1 base pad (disc of 13 mm arc radius at A1, rho0) plus a scapula-fixed tab toward the handler (14 mm wide, 25 mm long, toward bvec(-20, 45), at rho0); the lames at rho_k; the J3 arm pad (disc r 13 at A3, face rho_{N-1} - 3.15); the arm piece (a 14 mm strip from A3 along the great circle to BOTTOM's cut end, canonical ~(0, -70, 67.5), radius ramped to 96). COLLISIONS: the J1 hub cap (rho0 .. rho0 + 12.25, r 10) vs lame k >= 1 when lam_k*rho_k < 12 mm, i.e. lame k has slid over the J1 hub -> None. The same at J3 for lames k <= N-2. Contact-only points: lame tops (+tl) and the hub caps. Record the skin faces. REPORT: theta percentiles, and the lame overlap at the extremes.
sweep_params: a1 (az -20..60, el 60-90); a3 (delta 100-120, az -40..0); N (3-5); Lam (35-60 deg); overlap (0.2-0.4); hw (10-20 mm); tl (2-3.5 mm); rising vs falling lame order.
prior_art: Plate-armour pauldrons and lobster-tail lames on sliding rivets; pangolin / armadillo-scale wearable armour concepts; remote-centre circular guides. I know of none used as the J2 of a 3R shoulder exo with an equal-share coupling.

name: Rotator-cuff pair: supraspinatus and infraspinatus arcs converging on an exo-tubercle hub
topology: Parallel: two legs plus one hub. Leg 1 (supraspinatus line): radial pivot on a scapula pad A1 over the supraspinous fossa / top [PASSIVE] -> telescoping great-circle arc, length theta1 [ACTIVE] -> radial v5 hub at the 'exo-greater-tubercle' B1, the arm's low-motion spot [ACTIVE: the twist angle between leg 1's arc and the arm pad]. Leg 2 (infraspinatus line): radial pivot on a pad A2 over the infraspinous fossa / spine [PASSIVE] -> telescoping arc, length theta2 [ACTIVE] -> radial pivot on a second arm pad B2 on the posterior cap, or coaxial on B1 [PASSIVE] -> arm piece -> BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning: Leg 1 alone is a spherical 3R with 90/90 arcs (pivot A1, telescope, hub B1); leg 2 is an R-P-R leg. Mobility = 6 + 3 (human GH) - 2 loops x 3 = 3. Active: theta1 and theta2 (the two arc lengths) and the hub angle at B1 (leg 1's arc direction relative to the arm pad). Passive: the A1, A2 and B2 pivots, each set by its leg's endpoints (closure). There is no free coordinate unless a leg reaches 0 / 180 deg (rejected) or the three active coordinates stop determining the pose, i.e. the sensing Jacobian is singular (reported).
description: Two curved struts laid out like the supraspinatus and the infraspinatus. One runs from the top of the scapula forward-laterally over the acromion edge. The other runs from the back of the scapula around the posterior cap. Both converge on the arm just under the acromion edge, where the real cuff inserts on the greater tubercle. That is the arm's lowest-motion spot, w(112,-15), 60 mm from GH, with a 94 % disc ceiling. A v5 hub there carries leg 1; the arm piece holds the hub and runs to BOTTOM. Rest: both struts hug the top and back of the cap. Overhead: the tubercle rises under the acromion, leg 1 shortens, and leg 2 wraps further around the back. Across-body: leg 2 lengthens over the back. Behind-back: leg 2 shortens and leg 1 swings back. No metal sits over the front of the shoulder.
why_better: Same skin logic as the trilateration (below) with less metal. The two struts lie over the posterosuperior cap, the scapula's best ground, and the one hub sits on the arm's best spot. There is no metal over the anterior shoulder, the scapula frame's worst ground (az 150-180, ceiling 9-27 %), and no third strut to cross. The arm hub sits exactly where the proximity analysis found the only arm-fixed spot a flat O20/O23 disc can ride (94 % disc ceiling; the baseline's JN hub rides at 39.5 %). Each strut lies on the cap's geodesic between its origin and insertion, the line a wrapping cuff muscle takes, over skin that is round (the deltoid cap's radius spreads only 4.7 mm over 120 deg).
main_risk: Span ratio: ~2.6x on the clips and ~5x over the workspace for these point pairs (my check: 46-128 / 27-150 deg). That forces lazy-tongs or 3-stage telescopes. The B1 hub cap (12.25 mm) must never be crossed by leg 2. The sensing Jacobian of (theta1, theta2, twist) can degenerate where the two legs become coplanar (e.g. arm at the side with the insertion between the two origins). The two legs and the single hub carry all of MVP2's torque.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: everything is closure-set, the telescopes and pivots roll, and poses with theta near 0 / 180 are rejected, so nothing sags. MVP2: two tendon-like cables on the struts (pull to shorten; an internal push-pull band or a second cable to lengthen) and one hub drum at B1, with its cable routed along leg 1 or as a Bowden sheath ending on the arm piece. Sensing: a linear scale in each telescope and the B1 hub's magnet / IC. Forward kinematics by Newton from the last pose.
model_spec: Conventions: scapula dir -> S_R(i) d; arm dir (canonical, w_dir) -> H_R(i) @ RH @ d, with RH = BP._rig().L['rest_humerus']; GH origin. PARAMS: A1 = bvec (seed (20, 75)); A2 = bvec (seed (-10, 25)); B1 = w_dir (seed (112, -15)); B2 = w_dir (seed (95, -55)) or 'coaxial' (B2 = B1, leg 2 one layer up, +6 mm). Realisation: 'telescope3' (width 12, allowed theta_max/theta_min <= 2.6) or 'lazytongs' (n units of bar length Lb; band half-width w(theta) = 0.5*Lb*sqrt(1 - (theta*rho/(n*Lb))^2) + 3; requires 0.35*n*Lb <= theta*rho <= 0.92*n*Lb). HEIGHTS: pads at their lowest legal radius over the fit-clip frames (smallest radius, 0.5 mm steps, with all samples >= 2 mm from the skin by B.dist); rho0 = the max of the pad radii; legs at rho0 + 3.15, or the leg's own lowest legal radius if that is higher. PER POSE: P1 = S_R A1; P2 = S_R A2; Q1 = H_R RH B1; Q2 = H_R RH B2; theta_k = acos(P_k . Q_k). Return None if theta_k is outside its leg's fit-clip range +-3 deg, or outside [20, 160]. Twist tau = signed angle at Q1 between leg 1's tangent toward P1 (unit(P1 - (P1.Q1) Q1)) and an arm-fixed tangent at Q1 (H_R RH t0, where t0 = the canonical distal axis (0,-1,0) projected perpendicular to B1 and normalised). SENSING JACOBIAN: rotate the arm by +-0.3 deg about thorax x, y and z (apply the rotation to Q1, Q2 and the t0 image) and finite-difference (theta1, theta2, tau) to get a 3x3 J. Report |det| with the rows normalised; flag |det| < 0.1 as 'unsensable' (counted as taken, reported separately). COLLISIONS (None): leg 2's centreline within 19 mm of Q1 while its layer overlaps the hub span (rho0 .. rho0 + 12.25); legs crossing on the same layer (minimum distance between centrelines < (w1 + w2)/2 + 1). METAL (skin faces, 2 mm grid): pads as discs of r 12 at P1, P2 and Q2; the hub's arm pad at Q1; legs as great-circle bands P_k -> Q_k at their radius and width; the arm bridge Q1-Q2 at the pad radius; plus a 14 mm strip from Q1 to BOTTOM's cut end (canonical ~(0, -70, 67.5), radius ramped to 96). Contact-only points: the hub cap (disc r 10 at rho0 + 12.25) and the leg tops. Record the skin faces.
sweep_params: A1 (az -10..60, el 55-85); A2 (az -40..30, el 10-45); B1 (delta 100-120, az -40..0); B2 (delta 80-110, az -80..-30) or coaxial; realisation (telescope3 / lazytongs with n 4-8 and Lb 20-35 mm).
prior_art: BONES (Klein et al. 2008, UC Irvine), a shoulder orthosis whose parallel mechanism is driven by linear (pneumatic) actuators; rotator-cuff-inspired cable routing in soft shoulder exosuits; the 2R 'pointing + twist' split studied earlier in this repo. I have not seen two geodesic struts converging on a tubercle hub.

name: Muscle-arc trilateration: three telescoping 'deltoid' arcs whose lengths are the active joints
topology: Parallel. Three legs, each R-P-R along a great circle about GH, from a scapula-fixed pad A_k (origin: anterior, middle and posterior heads) to an arm-fixed pad B_k (insertion on the cap band): radial pivot at A_k [PASSIVE] -> curved telescoping arc whose angular length theta_k = angle(A_k, B_k) is the 'muscle length' [ACTIVE] -> radial pivot at B_k [PASSIVE] -> arm (pads tied by an arm bridge to BOTTOM). Realised as a lazy-tongs scissor or a 3-stage curved telescope.
dof_reasoning: Each R-P-R arc leg is a spherical 3R with 90/90 arcs whose middle joint is realised as the telescope (its axis is the normal of the great circle through A_k and B_k). Mobility = 9 + 3 (human GH) - 3 loops x 3 = 3. The three arc lengths theta_k = acos(A_k . B_k) are the active coordinates: like muscle lengths, three distances on a sphere fix an orientation locally. Each leg's plane and its two end pivots are set by its endpoints, so the 6 pivots are closure-set and cannot sag unless a leg reaches theta = 0 or 180 deg (plane undefined), which the model rejects.
description: Three curved struts lie along the geodesics of the shoulder cap, like the anterior, middle and posterior deltoid wrapping the humeral head. Their origins are pads with radial pivots on the exo-scapula's top / posterior ground. Their insertions are three pads on the arm's cap band, tied by an arm-fixed bridge to BOTTOM. Each strut is a band 10-16 mm wide at a constant radius just over the cap (skin face ~3 mm above the pads). Rest: the struts run down from the acromion region over the front, side and back of the cap. Overhead: the middle strut shortens as the insertion rises under the acromion, and the posterior one lengthens. Across-body: the posterior strut is long and the anterior short. Behind-back: the reverse. Axial twist shows up as a difference between the three lengths.
why_better: The only moving metal is the struts, and they lie exactly on the shortest surface path between an origin and an insertion: the line a wrapping muscle takes over the cap, where the skin is round (deltoid cap: 4.7 mm radius spread over 120 deg). No hub ever travels over moving skin; the six pivots sit on fixed pads on the best scapula and arm ground. The MVP2 drive is biomimetic and simple: a cable shortens or lengthens each strut, like a tendon. All three actuated coordinates are at the struts, so no motor cable has to reach a joint riding on a moving link the way the baseline's J2 and J3 do.
main_risk: Span ratio: for every scapula / arm point pair, the arc angle varies by at least 2.1x (best pairs: 75-165 deg). For good-ground pairs it varies 2.6x on the fit clips and 5.4x over the workspace (top / tubercle: 46-128 deg on the clips, 27-150 deg in the workspace; my check). A 2-stage telescope (< 1.8x) cannot do this. A lazy-tongs leg can (3-5x), but brings 15-25 small pivots, varying width and backlash; a 3-stage telescope is thick. Long struts at 150-170 deg approach the undefined-plane singularity. The struts cross each other under twist (stacking). Sensing singularity: when the three leg normals become coplanar, the lengths stop determining the pose.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the arm drives the pads, and the struts extend and retract freely (rolling telescopes or ball-bearing scissor pivots). The pivots are closure-set, so nothing sags except at theta -> 0 / 180, which is rejected. MVP2: each strut is driven like a muscle by a Bowden cable pair (pull to shorten; a second cable or an internal push-pull band to lengthen) from a remote motor. Sensing: a magnetic linear scale along the inner stage, or the angle of the first scissor pivot (length = n*Lb*cos(beta)). Forward kinematics from three lengths by Newton from the last pose.
model_spec: Conventions: scapula dir -> S_R(i) d; arm dir (canonical, w_dir) -> H_R(i) @ RH @ d, with RH = BP._rig().L['rest_humerus']; GH origin. PARAMS: A_k = bvec(az, el) for k = ant / mid / post (seeds (120, 60), (60, 70), (0, 50)); B_k = w_dir(delta, az) (seeds (95, 15), (112, -15), (100, -55)); realisation 'telescope3' (width 12, ratio <= 2.6) or 'lazytongs' (n, Lb; half-width w(theta) = 0.5*Lb*sqrt(1 - (theta*rho/(n*Lb))^2) + 3, two layers 2.5 mm apart; requires 0.35*n*Lb <= theta*rho <= 0.92*n*Lb). Per-leg range [th_min_k, th_max_k] = the fit-clip range +-3 deg; the design is invalid if the realisation cannot cover that ratio. HEIGHTS: each pad at its lowest legal radius over the fit-clip frames (0.5 mm steps, all samples >= 2 mm from the skin by B.dist); rho0 = the max pad radius; legs at rho0 + 3.15, or at their own lowest legal radius if higher; a leg flagged 'upper' gets +6. PER POSE: theta_k = acos(clip(S_R A_k . H_R RH B_k)). Return None if any theta_k is outside its range or outside [20, 160]. Leg geometry: unit vectors along the great circle from A_k to B_k (slerp), with a band of +-w/2 across at the leg's radius. Crossing test: if two legs on the same layer have centrelines closer than (w1 + w2)/2 + 1 mm -> None. SENSING index: rows n_k = unit(A_k x B_k) in the thorax frame; report |det| percentiles; poses with |det| < 0.1 count as taken but are reported as 'unsensable'. METAL (skin faces, 2 mm grid): base pads (discs r 12 at A_k), arm pads (discs r 12 at B_k), the legs, a base bridge (strips joining the A_k), and an arm bridge (strips joining the B_k, plus a 14 mm strip from the mid pad to BOTTOM's cut end, canonical ~(0, -70, 67.5), radius ramped to 96). Contact-only points: pivot caps (face + 10) and leg tops. Record the skin faces. REPORT: per-leg theta ranges, crossings, and sensing-index percentiles.
sweep_params: A_k on the scapula's top / posterior ground (el 30-80, az -30..130); B_k on the cap band (delta 85-125, az -70..+20, spread 60-90 deg); realisation (telescope3 / lazytongs with n 4-8 and Lb 20-35 mm); which leg is upper.
prior_art: BONES (Klein et al. 2008): a parallel shoulder orthosis with muscle-like linear actuators; Stewart-Gough / 3-UPS-S spherical parallel mechanisms; spherical scissor (lazy-tongs) linkages (Hoberman; You & Chen); soft shoulder exosuits with cable 'tendons'. I have not seen curved telescoping struts on the cap's geodesics as the active coordinates.

name: Three-headed exo-deltoid: a 3-RRR spherical parallel mechanism with every actuator on the scapula
topology: Spherical parallel mechanism, all 9 axes through GH. Three legs run from the exo-scapula to an arm platform made of three small pads on the cap band; each leg follows one head of the deltoid. Base R: a radial hub on the scapula (anterior head over the anterior acromion, middle head on the acromion top, posterior head on the scapular spine) [ACTIVE] -> proximal arc link -> elbow R [PASSIVE] -> distal arc link -> platform R: a radial hub on an arm pad [PASSIVE] -> arm. 3 active (base hubs), 6 passive (elbows + platform joints).
dof_reasoning: Mobility = 9 revolute freedoms + the human GH's 3 - 3 independent spherical loops x 3 = 3: the arm's own three rotations. For a given arm orientation, each leg's elbow axis is the intersection of the cone a_prox around its base axis and the cone a_dist around its platform axis, on a fixed working mode. So every passive joint is set by closure and cannot sag, as long as no leg reaches its stretched / folded configuration (where its elbow could flip), which the model rejects. The 3 base hubs are the active joints, sensed and MVP2-powered. The passive joints need no sensing, because the arm pose follows from the 3 base angles (forward kinematics on the chosen assembly mode).
description: Three thin arc 'heads' fan over the shoulder cap like the deltoid. Their base hubs sit on the exo-scapula, on ground the scapulohumeral rhythm protects: anterior-superior over the front of the acromion, middle on the acromion top, posterior on the spine. Each head is two 12 mm Ti arcs, proximal (base face + 3.15) and distal (+ 6.3), meeting at an elbow hub. The distal arcs end on three small arm pads on the cap band just below the acromion edge (posterolateral to lateral, delta ~95-115: the arm's low-motion band). The pads are tied by an arm-fixed bridge that continues to BOTTOM. Rest: the three elbows sit over the anterior, lateral and posterior deltoid. Overhead: the pads rise under the acromion and the heads fold, with the elbows moving up and out over the top and back; the posterior head stretches. Across-body: the posterior head stretches toward the front and the anterior head folds. Behind-back: the reverse. Axial twist is carried as a difference between the three heads.
why_better: In every serial chain, MVP2's hardest problem is driving J2 and J3, which ride on moving links. Here all three motor cables end on scapula-fixed hubs, like the deltoid's origins, and the moving legs carry no actuator. Each leg is short and stays over its own region (anterior / lateral / posterior), so no single link has to sweep the whole cap the way the baseline's link 1 and link 2 do. The arm attachment is three small pads on the arm's best band, instead of one large hub on the deltoid belly (the baseline's JN hub: 39.5 % disc ceiling, vs ~94 % near w(112,-15)). Sharing the load across three legs allows arcs thinner than 5.5 mm. With 90/90 arcs a leg is singular only at base-to-pad separations of 0 / 180 deg, and top / tubercle spans are 46-128 deg on the fit clips (my check), well inside.
main_risk: More metal over the cap (6 arcs, 9 hubs, 3 layers), all of which must stay in band. Legs collide under axial rotation, because the heads cross each other. The reachable set is the intersection of the three legs' sets, each limited by its own collisions. For MVP2 control there are 8 assembly modes and type-II (platform) singularities. The 9 bearings add friction (R17), though each is lightly loaded. Heavier than a serial 3R.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the arm moves the platform and every leg is closure-set. The only failure mode is a leg passing its stretched / folded configuration, where the elbow is undetermined and could flip; the model rejects poses within 12 deg of it. MVP2: a cable drum on each base hub. These are scapula-fixed, so the cable routes are the shortest and fixed of any concept. Sensing on the three base hubs (v5 magnet / IC), optionally plus one elbow encoder to pick the assembly mode. The MVP2 risk is control near type-II singularities (the platform loses stiffness with the actuators locked); the model reports its index.
model_spec: Conventions: scapula dir -> S_R(i) d; arm dir (canonical, w_dir) -> H_R(i) @ RH @ d, with RH = BP._rig().L['rest_humerus']; GH origin; numpy band_impl.circ_int. PARAMS: base axes u_k = bvec(az, el) for k = A / M / P (seeds (120, 60), (70, 70), (10, 50)); platform axes v_k = w_dir(delta, az) (seeds (95, 15), (112, -15), (100, -55)); arcs a_prox = a_dist = 90 (or per leg); working modes s_k = +-1 (per leg, pick the one whose elbow is farther from the other legs at the bench's first pose); link width 12, thickness 5.5; hub radius 10, cap 12.25 above the lower member's face; margin m = 12 deg. HEIGHTS: rho0 = the max over the base pads of their lowest legal radius over the fit-clip frames (0.5 mm steps, all samples >= 2 mm by B.dist). Layers (skin faces): base pads + base bridge at rho0; proximal arcs + arm pads + arm bridge at rho0 + 3.15; distal arcs at rho0 + 6.3. Raise all layers together if the arm pads violate their own lowest legal radius. IK PER POSE: U_k = S_R u_k; V_k = H_R RH v_k; theta_k = angle(U_k, V_k). Return None if theta_k < |a_prox - a_dist| + m or > a_prox + a_dist - m. Elbow W_k = circ_int(U_k, a_prox, V_k, a_dist, s_k). METAL (2 mm grid): base pads = discs r 12 at U_k; base bridge = great-circle strips U_A-U_M-U_P, 12 wide; proximal = great-circle band U_k -> W_k; elbow discs at W_k; distal = band W_k -> V_k; arm pads = discs r 12 at V_k; arm bridge = strips V_A-V_M-V_P plus a 14 mm strip from V_M to BOTTOM's cut end (canonical ~(0, -70, 67.5), radius ramped to 96). SELF-COLLISION (None): same-layer elements of different legs whose centrelines come within 13 mm (arc length at their radius); or any arc passing within 17 mm of another leg's hub whose radial span [face, face + 12.25] overlaps the arc's [face, face + 5.5]. Contact-only points: tops (+5.5) and caps. Record the skin faces. REPORT: the type-II index min |det[unit(W_k x V_k)]| over the taken poses, and the share of poses lost to each test.
sweep_params: Base axes (az, el) for the three heads within the scapula's top / posterior ground (el 30-80, az -30..130); platform axes on the cap band (delta 85-125, az -70..+20, spread 60-90 deg); a_prox, a_dist (60-100, shared or per leg); working modes; link width (8-14 mm).
prior_art: Gosselin & Angeles' Agile Eye (3-RRR SPM); SPM-based shoulder exoskeleton work by Niyetkaliyev and Shintemirov (Nazarbayev University). I have not seen legs routed along the deltoid heads with the platform on the cap band.

name: Lines-of-non-extension helix: 2R pointing over the top + a helical, skin-profiled humeral-rotation rail
topology: Scapula base -> J1 = hub (axis a1 at the 2R singularity home) [ACTIVE] -> link 1 -> J2 = hub (axis a2, at a12 from a1 and perpendicular to the humerus axis) [ACTIVE] -> link 2 (the pointing link: it holds the humerus axis direction and runs down the lateral arm) -> carriage stage on link 2: an axial slide along the humerus axis [PASSIVE] + a radial slide [PASSIVE] -> J3 = carriage on an arm-fixed HELICAL rail around the upper arm, whose station and radius change with its angle (humeral rotation) [ACTIVE] -> arm.
dof_reasoning: The 2R pointing chain sets the humerus direction (2 DOF, both hubs active). J3 is the arm's rotation about its own axis relative to link 2, i.e. the carriage's angle on the helix (active). Because the rail is a helix with a radius profile, the rail point under the carriage moves along the humerus axis (by the pitch) and radially as the arm rotates; the carriage's two passive slides on link 2 follow it. Their positions are set by the helix profile at the current J3 angle (closure), so they cannot sag and need no sensing. A translation along, or radial to, the humerus axis does not change the rotation the joint transmits about that axis.
description: Over the shoulder: a compact 2R pointing chain, with J1 at the anterior-superior acromion / clavicle-tip region (the singularity home) and J2 on the cap's equator. Down the arm: link 2 lies along the lateral arm. At its end, a small two-slide carriage rides an arm-fixed helical rail, a 10 mm band that winds ~120-180 deg around the upper arm. The helix follows a line of non-extension of the skin (as in the MIT BioSuit), and its radius follows the non-round arm. Rest: the helix runs from the posterolateral arm high up to the anterolateral arm lower down (or the reverse). Overhead, across-body and behind-back: link 2 points with the arm. Internal / external rotation runs the carriage along the helix, moving it up or down the arm by the pitch, so that at each station it stays in that station's body-free window.
why_better: It implements the user's own suggestion ('put upper arm rotation in its own DOF farther down ... and just have to handle 2 at the shoulder'). It addresses the two measured failures of an arm-fixed ring (FINDINGS). (1) The arm is not round (13.5-25 mm skin-radius spread over 120 deg at every station 80-280 mm down), so the cam profile follows the skin. (2) The body-free window at a fixed station is only 124-130 deg, so the helix spreads the travel over several stations, each using its own window. The 2R pointing chain's singularity has a home: J1's axis can sit where the arm axis never comes within 41 deg (bench fit clips) / 31 deg (workspace) (my check: bvec(125, 45)).
main_risk: Link 2 still rides over arm skin that rotates under it (a pointing-only link over the arm's non-round section), so its band may be poor. The body-free windows at successive stations may not chain into a helix, because the trunk sits medial at every station. The two-slide carriage stage is bulky (~25 x 20 x 9 mm). The J1 home (anterior-superior, scapula ceiling ~30 %) is not on good ground, and J2 is still a moving hub over the cap equator.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the hubs and the helix carriage are driven by the arm, and the passive slides are set by the profile; V-wheel carriage on a 3-D curve. MVP2: hub drums on J1 and J2. J3 is driven by a cable laid along the helical rail's groove from a Bowden stop on link 2; a helix is a constant-lead path, so the cable wraps it like a screw thread. Sensing: magnet / IC on the hubs; J3 by a magnetic scale along the helix read by the carriage.
model_spec: Conventions: scapula dir -> S_R(i) d; arm dir (canonical, w_dir; the distal axis is (0,-1,0)) -> H_R(i) @ RH @ d, with RH = BP._rig().L['rest_humerus']; GH origin; numpy band_impl.circ_int. PARAMS: a1 = bvec (seed (125, 45)); a12 (90); sigma; chi = the carriage azimuth in link 2's frame, measured from a2 about u, set at the bench's first pose so that the carriage sits at canonical az = psi_c. Helix: s0 = station at its centre (90 mm down the axis); pitch p (0.3 mm/deg); span Psi (150 deg); centre azimuth psi_c (0 = lateral, + anterior); clearance 2.5. KINEMATICS PER POSE: u = H_R RH (0,-1,0); A1 = S_R a1; a2 = circ_int(A1, a12, u, 90 deg, sigma). Return None within 10 deg of cone tangency (angle(A1, u) outside [|90 - a12| + 10, 90 + a12 - 10]). Link-2 frame: e1 = a2, e2 = u x a2, e3 = u. Humeral rotation gamma = atan2(ref . e2, ref . e1), with ref = H_R RH (0,0,1) (canonical lateral). Carriage arm-frame azimuth psi = wrap(chi - gamma + gamma_0), where gamma_0 makes psi = psi_c at the first pose. Return None if psi is outside [psi_c - Psi/2 + c, psi_c + Psi/2 - c] (c = carriage half-length in deg). HELIX (arm frame): station s(psi) = s0 + p (psi - psi_c). Radius r(psi) = r_need + clearance, where r_need = max over the shaping poses (fit clips + workspace) of the outermost inside radius along the canonical ray from (0, -s, 0) in direction (sin psi, 0, cos psi), sampled r = 20..90 in steps of 1.5 with one batched B.dist call per pose. METAL (skin faces, 2 mm grid): the J1 pad disc at its lowest legal radius rho0; link 1 = great-circle band A1 -> a2 at rho0 + 3.15, width 12; the J2 disc at a2; link 2 = a 14 mm strip at azimuth chi in link 2's frame, i.e. points s*u + R2(s)(cos chi e1 + sin chi e2) for s from 0 to s(psi). R2(s) = 2 + the max over poses of the arm skin radius at station s and that link-2 azimuth (computed in a first pass in link 2's frame), but never below rho0 + 6.3 near s = 0. Carriage box face 24 x 20 mm at r(psi) + 5; helix rail = a 10 mm band along (s(psi'), r(psi')) for psi' over the span, mapped by H_R RH. Contact-only points: tops. Record the skin faces. REPORT: link 2's in-band separately (the expected weak part).
sweep_params: a1 (around bvec(125, 45) +-20 deg); a12 (70-90); s0 (70-130 mm); pitch p (0-0.6 mm/deg, either sign); Psi (100-200 deg); psi_c (-60..60); chi.
prior_art: Lines of non-extension (Iberall 1964; Newman's MIT BioSuit; Bethke 2005 mapping); semicircular humeral-rotation bearings (ARMin II/III, ABLE); the 2R pointing + ring studied in this repo (FINDINGS: ring body-free windows). I have not seen a helical, skin-profiled humeral-rotation rail.

name: Cruciate-ligament knuckles: a spherical 3R whose joints are rolling crossed four-bars instead of stacked hubs
topology: A spherical serial chain where each revolute is replaced by a spherical crossed four-bar 'knuckle': two crossing ligament bars between the ends of adjacent members, like the knee's cruciate ligaments. Scapula base -> knuckle 1 [1 ACTIVE input + 3 PASSIVE pivots] -> link 1 -> knuckle 2 [1 ACTIVE + 3 PASSIVE] -> link 2 -> knuckle 3 [1 ACTIVE + 3 PASSIVE] -> arm piece -> BOTTOM. All pivot axes pass through GH. Each knuckle's relative motion is a rolling of two pitch cones about a moving instantaneous axis.
dof_reasoning: Each crossed four-bar is one closed loop with mobility 1: its other 3 pivots are set by closure from the input pivot. So each knuckle is one joint coordinate (one active pivot, sensed / driven), and three knuckles give three active DOF. The 9 passive pivots are inside the loops and cannot sag while the loops stay away from toggle (ligaments collinear), which the model rejects. The chain is still spherical (all axes through GH), and its three inputs are set by the arm orientation (numerical IK, unique on a branch near the previous pose).
description: It looks like the baseline's straps, but the members butt end to end at small knuckles instead of overlapping at O20 hubs. Each knuckle is two short Ti ligament bars (~20 mm) crossing in an X between the rounded ends of the two members, on 4 tiny bearings (O6-8). All members ride on ONE layer: no 3.15 mm step per joint and no 12.25 mm cap. The ligaments sit 3-6 mm above. The joint 'rolls' like the knee, or like the humeral head on the glenoid: its instantaneous axis travels along the member ends by half the rotation, spreading each joint's footprint. Rest, overhead, across-body and behind-back: the chain follows the path of the 3R it replaces (seeded from the baseline and from the crossed-rails seeds), with every member at the height it needs.
why_better: Joint size is a measured lever: O17 vs O23 hubs is worth ~20 points of workspace (FINDINGS). The hub zones (J2's lower plate, BOTTOM's JN hub) carry most of the baseline's R1 loss, and each joint also steps the next member 3.15 mm up. A knuckle has no disc that must stand on the skin and no overlap between members, so the chain can sit one layer lower everywhere and its joint zones are as thin as the members. The model builds the same seed with v5 hubs in the same script, so the knuckle's effect is measured on its own.
main_risk: Range: a crossed four-bar has ~150-170 deg of total travel before toggle, but well-conditioned travel is ~+-70 deg, and some 3R joints need more (J1 / J3 rotations can exceed 150 deg), so some poses become unreachable. Ligament strength and buckling under MVP2's 10 N.m (~1 kN at a 10 mm lever). 12 small bearings. Numerical IK. An unusual CAD.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the loops are closure-set, and the 12 small rolling bearings each carry a low load. The moving instantaneous axis adds no free coordinate. Near toggle a knuckle loses stiffness, so those poses are rejected. MVP2: a cable drum on the input pivot of each knuckle, or on a member-fixed sector about the knuckle's mean axis. Sensing at the same pivot (small magnet / IC); the knuckle's forward kinematics maps it to the member angle.
model_spec: Conventions: scapula dir -> S_R(i) d; arm dir (canonical, w_dir) -> H_R(i) @ RH @ d, with RH = BP._rig().L['rest_humerus']; GH origin. TARGET per pose: T_i = S_R(i)^T H_R(i) RH, the arm orientation in the scapula frame. SEED 3R in product-of-exponentials form: T(q) = Rot(j1, q1) Rot(j2, q2) Rot(j3, q3) T_0. Take the joint axes j1, j2, j3 (scapula frame) and T_0 from a seed spherical 3R evaluated at the bench's first pose: the baseline r18 s1392 #1 (J1 axis bvec(32.6, 80.6), arcs (77.4, 81.4) deg, JN axis w_dir(71.4, 4.8), branch -1: j1 = a1, j2 = a2 at that pose, j3 = HG a3 at that pose), or a crossed-muscle-rails seed. KNUCKLE (idealised rolling equal pitch cones, which a symmetric crossed four-bar approximates): replace Rot(j_k, q_k) by Rot(c_k, q_k/2) Rot(c'_k, q_k/2), with c_k = Rot(n_k, -beta_k) j_k, c'_k = Rot(n_k, +beta_k) j_k and n_k = unit(j_k x j_(k+1)) (for k = 3 use j2). With beta -> 0 this is the seed 3R exactly. IK: solve q (3 values) to minimise |log(T(q)^T T_i)| by Levenberg-Marquardt, warm-started from the previous pose along each clip sequence and, for workspace poses, from the nearest solved pose in pose space. Return None if the residual > 0.5 deg, any |q_k - median_k| > q_max (70 deg; median over the fit clips), or cond(J) > 50. GEOMETRY: member k's frame P_k(q) = the product of the first k knuckle factors. Knuckle k's contact direction in the scapula frame = P_(k-1)(q) Rot(c_k, q_k/2) j_k. Members are great-circle bands, 14 mm wide, between consecutive contact directions (base pad -> contact 1 -> contact 2 -> contact 3 -> arm piece), ALL at one skin face rho = the max over the members of their lowest legal radius over the fit-clip frames (0.5 mm steps, all samples >= 2 mm by B.dist). Knuckles: two ligament bars (6 mm wide, length 2*rho*sin(beta) + 6) crossing over the contact at rho + 6 and rho + 9, plus pivot discs r 4 (contact-only). Arm piece: from contact 3 to BOTTOM's cut end (canonical ~(0, -70, 67.5), radius ramped to 96). Map everything to the thorax frame by S_R(i). CONTROL: in the same script, build the same seed with v5 hubs (discs r 10 at each j_k direction, members stepping +3.15 per joint, caps contact-only) and report both. REPORT: per-knuckle q range and the residuals.
sweep_params: beta per knuckle (6-15 deg); q_max (55-80 deg); seed 3R (baseline r18 / crossed-rails seeds / free 3R parameters); member width (10-16 mm).
prior_art: Crossed four-bar knee models (O'Connor, Zavatsky) and polycentric prosthetic knees; rolling-contact joints (Jacob's ladder; CORE by Halverson and Howell). I know of no spherical crossed-four-bar knuckles in a shoulder exo.

name: Crown ring 3R: J1 is an open thin-section ring on the crown the arm never approaches; donut J2/J3
topology: S (handler) -> J1 R active: 4-point-contact thin-section ring (RBC/Kaydon Reali-Slim KA025XP0 63.5x76.2x6.35 or KA030XP0 76.2x88.9x6.35, ~60-70 g). It lies flat on the shoulder crown (top-back of the acromion and supraspinatus), axis a1 through GH near c* = [-0.38, 0.91, 0.16] (S-local; S-local = thorax at rest because scap(0) = I). Stator on the handler, rotor = link 1 -> link 1 = rotor flange + 14 mm Ti strap from the ring rim to J2 at alpha12 = 58-80 deg from a1 -> J2 R active: donut hub (RBC KAA15XL0 38.1x47.6x4.76, 18 g, ~40 N.m static moment; or IKO CRBT305A 30x41x5), axis a2 through GH -> link 2 strap over the deltoid -> J3 R active: KAA15XL0 donut on the lateral upper arm, axis a3 humerus-fixed through GH (NOT the humerus axis). Its outer race sits in the arm-side saddle under BOTTOM. All axes meet at GH. Passive (outside the count): the cuff's self-aligning slides, zero travel in the bench.
dof_reasoning: A spherical 3R: the humerus orientation relative to the scapula fixes the 3 joint angles (closed-form IK, 2 branches, branch fixed per design). There is no redundant joint and nothing that can sag. Each joint is one rolling bearing with an open bore for an encoder and an OD for an MVP2 cable drum. A feasibility constraint, measured today on the bench frames (470 poses): every humerus-fixed direction swings over at least ~95 deg of polar angle about c*. The 3R band [|a12-a23|, a12+a23] must contain that range plus a margin, so alpha12 >= spread/2 + 10 ~ 58 deg, with alpha23 at the band centre.
description: At rest the ring frames the acromion and supraspinatus. That skin moves with the base: measured today, the skin along S-fixed superior stays at 47.7-48.6 mm and along superior-posterior-lateral at 49.6-54.8 mm, from rest to 150 deg elevation. The ring sits like an eyelet with the bony crown inside its bore, 2-9 mm above the skin around it. Link 1 leaves the rotor and runs down the front or back of the crown to J2, 58-80 deg from the crown pole (top of the anterior or posterior deltoid). Link 2 runs to J3 on the lateral upper arm, 100-160 mm from GH, inside the -20..+62 deg arm sector. Overhead: the humerus never comes within 82 deg of c* (one-sided, all bench poses; 58 deg for plain superior), so J1 and the ring never meet the deltoid; J2 swings to the back or front of the crown. Across-body and behind-back: J1 turns, J2 travels around its circle, and link 2 is the only metal over the moving deltoid.
why_better: All S-fixed metal and J1 sit on the only skin that moves with the base, at the one pole the arm never approaches. The open bore takes the 12.25 mm O20 dome off the highest bony point: the ring is a 6.35 mm section with ~9 mm of housing stack. KAA15 / CRBT donuts at J2 and J3 (~9 mm, open bore) take ~3 mm off each O20 stack and let the deltoid bulge rise into the bore. FINDINGS puts joint size at ~20 points of workspace. The strap from J1 to J2 starts at the ring rim, so link 1 cannot become the short-link failure (two hubs side by side).
main_risk: alpha12 >= ~58 deg means J2 still travels a circle 58-80 deg off the crown. That is the same circle on which the baseline's J2 hub lands on the back over the medial scapula overhead, so this concept may only move J1's share of the problem. A flat ring on a dome tilts against the skin across its land: on a 55 mm-radius dome, a 76 mm ring's skin side drops ~6-7 mm across its section. The ring needs a stiff round housing (1.5 mm Ti both sides), so J1 alone weighs 60-90 g.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: rolling everywhere (mu ~0.004) and no spare joint, so nothing sags or locks. Use shielded rings, not 2RS seals, to keep drag on the large ring under ~0.05 N.m. MVP2: the J1 drum is a groove on the rotor OD (r 38-44 mm), which roughly halves the cable tension of an O20 drum; J1 sensing is a magnetic ring on the rotor with a Hall sensor on the stator. J2 and J3 have drums on the donut OD (r ~24 mm) and encoders in the open bore.

Arm direction t = Q@u. Arm-fixed vectors: v_H = RH0.T@v_rest (RH0 = RH at the all-zero pose). Map S-local points by RS@p and H-local points by RH@p. Sample skin-facing faces on a 2 mm grid; hubs and rings = underside annulus + outer rim. Solve R(a1,q1) R(a2,q2) a3 = G@a3 with Paden-Kahan subproblem 2 (no solution -> None; along a clip take the branch nearest the previous frame, on workspace poses the design's branch). Get q3 from subproblem 1. Singular if |a1 . (a2c x a3c)| < 0.17 (current axes) -> None. Apply joint travel limits. Its plane is perpendicular to a1 at the smallest height h such that every land point p = h a1 + r e(phi) satisfies |p| >= ENV_S(dir p) + 2, with ENV_S over all clip poses (the base is S-fixed). Metal: the underside annulus + the outer cylinder, 9 mm tall. a2_0 = a1 rotated by alpha12 toward a chosen azimuth. J2 donut: annulus r 19-26 perpendicular to a2 at max(ENV over L1 and L2 under the annulus) + 2, stack 9 (upper member from +3). J3: same donut on a3 with ENV over the arm. Link 1: great-circle strap from the ring rim (at a2's azimuth) to J2, 14 wide, 3 thick (MVP1 loads ~1 N.m; 5.5 for MVP2), underside ENV_L1 + 2. Link 2: J2 -> J3 the same way in L2. Seed: the baseline axes in pipeline/full-exo/designs/cad_r18_n3_s1392_1_f300/design.json (convention in pipeline/conformal/gpu/band_impl.py) with J1 moved to c*; or choose a3 (H-local) to minimise its polar range about c* over the clip and workspace poses and centre the band on that range.
sweep_params: a1 within 20 deg of c*; ring size (KA020/025/030); alpha12 55-80 deg; alpha23 60-100 deg; a3 direction (2 params, H-local); branch; J2/J3 donut type (KAA15 vs CRBT305A); R2, R3 hub distance from GH 55-95 mm.

name: Twin rails, one hub: virtual J1 on an S-fixed crown rail, virtual J3 on an arm-fixed rail
topology: S -> J1 R active with a VIRTUAL axis a1 through GH. An S-fixed open arc rail carries it: either a custom caged-ball wire-race C-slide (docs/research/ring_and_shell_hardware.md option A: 26 mm-wide hollow Ti band, 6 mm radial, 2 hardened race wires per edge, 3 mm balls) or a plain iglidur J band slide (8.5 mm stack). The rail lies on a circle about a1 at cone alpha12, over the crown -> carriage 1 (40-60 mm shoe) = J2's lower member -> J2 R active: the ONLY hub (KAA15XL0 donut, ~9 mm), axis a2 = the carriage's ray through GH, mounted BESIDE the rail at the same level (side outrigger, not stacked on it) -> link 2 = short strap -> carriage 3 -> J3 R active with a VIRTUAL axis a3 (humerus-fixed, through GH): an ARM-fixed arc rail on a circle about a3 at cone alpha32, on the lateral upper arm inside the -20..+62 deg sector, fixed to the cuff saddle under BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning: Kinematically a spherical 3R: the two carriage positions are q1 and q3 and the hub angle is q2, all fixed by the humerus orientation (closed-form IK). No spare coordinate. The caged-ball cages move at half the carriage speed but carry no load-free freedom: their position is set by the carriages, an anti-creep rack keeps them centred, and they are not a DOF. Each coordinate can be sensed (magnetic strip along each band, hall on the carriage; magnet + hall in the donut bore) and, in MVP2, driven (cable laid in a groove along the band to the carriage; drum on the donut).
description: Neither the J1 pole nor the J3 pole has a hub, so those poles may point into the body. The crown rail is a 26 mm band laid like a headband over the acromion and supraspinatus. This base metal is shaped exactly to skin that moves with S (measured today: 47.7-55 mm from GH, rest to 150 deg), so it never moves against that skin. The arm rail runs along the lateral arm 100-200 mm from GH, shaped to the arm skin. Only J2 and the short link 2 between the carriages move over the deforming deltoid. Overhead: carriage 1 sits at the front or back end of the crown rail and J2 at the crown edge. Across-body and behind-back: the carriages move to opposite ends of their rails.
why_better: Metal fixed to S or to the humerus can be shaped exactly to the skin it rides on, because nothing moves between them. Only one hub and one short link cross the deltoid, where the skin bulges and moves with the pose. The rails replace both pole hubs, link 1, and the arm-end neck: today the 'link 2 - neck' collision is all of R16's part interference (FINDINGS). Axis directions that hub chains could never build become available, because the poles no longer need room for a hub.
main_risk: The J1 travel used must fit on the crown patch (roughly +-35 deg around c*), and J3 travel plus the carriage arc must fit in the 82 deg arm sector. Both cap the joint ranges, and the alpha >= ~58 deg constraint from the crown-ring concept still applies, so it is not certain a 3R exists whose q1 and q3 both fit. A long open rail is a curved cantilever (a 26x6 hollow band twists ~2 deg at 25 N.m). Rail plus carriage is ~10 mm, which leaves no margin to 14 mm where the deltoid bulges under the arm rail in flexion.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: caged-ball rolling, or iglidur with friction ~(4/pi) mu M under tilt (~0.06 N.m at MVP1's ~0.5 N.m tilt), so no locking; anti-creep rack on each cage; no spare joint. MVP2: a Bowden cable runs in a groove along each band to its carriage, with sheath stops at the band ends; the J2 drum is on the donut OD; encoders are magnetic strips under the carriages plus the J2 bore encoder.

name: Coaxial spherical parallel manipulator driven from a nested ring stack on the crown (bold)
topology: S -> three ACTIVE R joints, all coaxial with a0 (S-local, near c* = [-0.38, 0.91, 0.16]): three concentric thin-section rings nested in one ~7 mm layer on the crown (RBC KA020XP0 50.8x63.5x6.35, KA025XP0 63.5x76.2, KA030XP0 76.2x88.9), or two nested and one stacked. Each rotor carries a proximal arc link (arc ap) -> passive R micro-hub (2x MR85-2RS 5x8x2.5, or 683ZZ 3x7x3, in an O12 boss, ~7 mm stack) -> distal arc link (arc ad) -> passive R micro-hub on the arm platform, axes v_i humerus-fixed through GH (platform = a C-saddle on the lateral upper arm under BOTTOM). Three RRR legs, every axis through GH.
dof_reasoning: A spherical parallel mechanism: 3 legs x 3 R = 9 joints, mobility 3. The 3 coaxial input angles fix the platform orientation (coaxial-SPM forward/inverse kinematics, Tursynbek et al. 2019). Conversely the humerus orientation fixes every input angle and all 6 passive joints: each leg's middle-joint axis is the intersection of two cones. The passives are set by closure, so there is no spare coordinate and nothing can sag. Near-singular frames are rejected, because there the passives would be force-amplifying, not sagging.
description: At rest a flat ring stack sits on the crown, on skin that moves with S (48-55 mm from GH). Three thin curved legs fan out over the front, top-lateral and back of the deltoid to the arm saddle. Because the inputs are coaxial, rotation about a0 is unlimited, so the arm can sweep any azimuth around the crown pole. Overhead the legs fold toward the crown; across-body the front leg flattens over the anterior deltoid; behind-back the rear leg crosses the posterior deltoid.
why_better: All three actuated joints, and later every MVP2 drum and encoder, sit on the base, on the only skin that moves with S. The moving legs carry only O12 micro-hubs (~7 mm) instead of 12.25 mm O20 hubs, which attacks the hub-stack difficulty directly. Each leg carries about a third of the moment, so the legs can be thinner than a serial strap. Closed loops are stiff for MVP2.
main_risk: Orientation workspace. Each leg needs v_i to stay within [|ap-ad| + m, ap + ad - m] of a0, while any humerus-fixed direction swings at least ~95 deg about the crown. That forces ap ~ ad ~ 80-90 deg: long legs over the deltoid. Parallel singularities inside the range are likely. Legs may collide with each other and with the arm across-body. Nine joints of metal over the shoulder.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: thin-section rings and micro ball bearings, all rolling. The passives are set by closure; near-singular configurations are rejected, not passed through. MVP2: drums on the three ring rotors (r 30-42 mm) with cables to remote motors; encoders are magnetic rings on the stator. No actuator or sensor on the moving legs.

Self-collision under 1 mm -> None. Per pose: v_i' = Q@v_i. (w_i x v_i')| < 0.15; parallel if |det[(w_i x v_i') for i = 1..3]| < 0.05 -> None. Check leg-leg and leg-arm clearance.

name: Hubless spherical rolling-contact joints: conical Rolamite / CORE pairs with apex at GH (bold, weird)
topology: S -> J1 active: a conical rolling-contact pair. Two Ti cone-sector rims (apex at GH, half-angles ga and gb, 2.5 mm wall, radial extent from skin+2 to skin+10 mm) roll on each other along a radial contact line, held by 2-3 crossed flexure straps (0.1 mm spring steel or Ti foil, wound in opposite senses: the Jacob's-ladder / Rolamite principle) -> link 1 -> J2 active: second cone pair -> link 2 -> J3 active: third cone pair on the arm saddle. Every contact line is a ray from GH, so each pair is a 1-DOF spherical motion with a rolling instantaneous axis. No pins, no hubs.
dof_reasoning: Each strap-held rolling pair is exactly 1 DOF (rolling without slip). With equal cones the relative rotation is T(phi) = R(c, phi) R(m0, phi), where c is the fixed-cone axis and m0 the moving-cone axis at phi = 0, 2g apart; that is the spherical analogue of equal rolling circles. Three such joints in series give a generic 3-DOF spherical map, so the humerus orientation fixes phi1-phi3: a 3x3 nonlinear solve, no redundancy, nothing that sags. Each phi is sensable (magnet on one cone, hall on the other) and, in MVP2, drivable (cable wrapped on the cone rim, the rim acting as its own drum).
description: There are no hubs and no pins. Each joint is two thin bevel-wheel-like rims standing on edge, ~8 mm tall, rolling on each other like toothless bevel gears, with the straps wrapped around them. At rest J1's pair stands on the crown, J2's over the deltoid top and J3's on the lateral arm. As the arm moves the rims roll, so each joint's contact point walks along its rims: the joint itself travels over the skin by up to (rim radius x phi), which a hub cannot do.
why_better: It removes the joint stack entirely. A rolling pair is two 2.5 mm walls and 0.1 mm straps, ~8-10 mm tall in total, with no dome, cap, pin or bearing seat. There is no friction torque under tilt (rolling; the straps carry the tension). The wandering contact point gives each joint a cam-like freedom to put its metal where the skin is, beyond the fixed-axis-point limit of every hub chain.
main_risk: Off-plane loads: strap-held rolling joints resist only in their rolling plane, so the cones need side flanges or guides (extra width). Each joint's range is limited by its rim arc (+-90-120 deg needs long rims). The rims stand radially, edge-on to the skin, so their footprint is narrow but the links must sit on top. A precise conical rolling surface on Ti is unusual to make (DFM), and strap fatigue over all-day wear is unproven. Modelling is nonlinear: no closed-form IK.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: rolling with no stiction or self-locking; preloaded straps give zero backlash; no spare joint. MVP2: the cable wraps the cone rim (drum radius = rim radius ~50-60 mm, low tension); sensor = magnet and hall across the contact, or a hall track on the rim.
model_spec: COMMON: fr = B.frames(i); RS, RH = fr['S'][0], fr['H'][0]; GH = origin, so Q = RS.T@RH (S-local = thorax at rest). Humerus axis in H-local: u = normalize(BP._rig().L['elbow']). Arm-fixed vectors: v_H = RH0.T@v_rest. ENV(member, rays): for each member-local ray d and each fit-clip pose taken, the skin radius is the first r >= 30 mm along M(i)@d with B.dist >= 0 (2 mm march, then 0.5 mm bisection); the envelope is the max over poses, and the underside = envelope + 2. 2 mm sampling grid. Self-collision under 1 mm -> None. THIS CONCEPT: joint k has a fixed-cone axis c_k in its lower member frame and a moving-cone axis m_k0 at angle 2g_k from c_k (equal cones; unequal cones: T_k = R(c_k, phi) R(m_k0, phi sin ga / sin gb)). Relative rotation T_k(phi_k) = R(c_k, phi_k) R(m_k0, phi_k). FK: M1 = T_1(phi1), M2 = M1 T_2(phi2), M3 = M2 T_3(phi3), with c_2, m_20 expressed in link 1's frame (so they move with M1) and c_3, m_30 in link 2's frame; Q_pred = M3 @ Q0. IK: Levenberg-Marquardt on phi (3 unknowns), minimising ||log(Q_pred^T Q)||. Warm-start from the previous frame along a clip; use 8 seeds on workspace poses. Fail if the residual > 0.5 deg or any |phi_k| > rim range. Metal per joint: two cone walls, each a strip on the cone surface about its axis spanning the rim arc actually used (+-range) and radially from ENV + 2 to ENV + 10 along each generator, sampled every 2 mm (both rims, in their members' frames). The current contact ray = the fixed cone's generator rotated by phi about c_k. Straps ignored (sub-mm). Links: great-circle straps between consecutive rims, 14 wide, 3 thick, at ENV + 2.
sweep_params: Joint axes (equivalent to the axis set of a 3R: seed with the baseline or crown-ring-3r axes, then split each axis into c_k / m_k0 symmetric about it); cone half-angles g_k 10-40 deg; rim arc ranges; link widths.
prior_art: Rolamite (Wilkes 1967); Jacob's-ladder / XR joints; CORE compliant rolling-contact elements (Cannon & Howell 2005); rolling-contact knee orthoses. No conical (spherical) rolling exo joint known.

name: Off-sphere skin hubs + passive cuff stage: axis directions spherical, axis positions free
topology: S -> J1 R active: O20 v5 hub or KAA15XL0 donut lying flat ON the crown skin, axis direction a1, but its axis line does not pass through GH -> link 1 -> J2 R active: hub on skin, offset axis line -> link 2 -> J3 R active: hub on the arm, offset line -> passive self-aligning cuff stage under the saddle (passive, outside the count): one along-arm miniature linear guide (THK RSR5 / RSR7: 5 / 7 mm rail, block height 6 / 8 mm, travel +-40 mm) + two short transverse guides (THK RSR3: 3 mm rail, 4 mm tall, +-8 mm), or a 2-axis flexure parallelogram (+-5 mm) -> user's cuff.
dof_reasoning: The axis directions are those of a spherical 3R, so the joint angles are fixed by orientation alone (same IK as a spherical 3R) and the chain matches the arm's rotation exactly. The axis offsets only create a translation mismatch at the cuff, which the 3 passive slides take up. Chain 3R + 3P = 6 coordinates; closure with the rigid cuff = 6 equations; so each slide position is a unique function of the pose, set by closure and driven by the arm. That is the user's passive self-aligning cuff slide (2026-10-15 rule: not counted). No spare coordinate, nothing that can sag. In the real body the same slides also absorb GH translation (R10).
description: Hubs are no longer forced onto rays through GH at fixed radii. J1 lies flat on the crown, J2 on the top of the posterior or anterior deltoid wherever the skin is, J3 on the lateral arm; each hub's lower plate rests on its own skin patch at +2 mm. The end of link 2 rides a short rail along the lateral arm under BOTTOM: overhead it slides toward the shoulder, across-body away from it, and the transverse guides shift a few mm.
why_better: Spherical chains pay for 'every axis through GH' by holding hubs at a constant radius over a shoulder that is not a sphere (38-98 mm skin radius about GH; 47-98 mm measured along S-fixed directions today). Freeing axis positions lets each hub sit at skin + 2 at its own centre, which attacks the stand-off that limits in-band to 41-58 % in the built CAD. The minimax LP in pipeline/girdle/girdle.py (for fixed axis directions, the carried GH point is linear in the axis points) gives exact offsets that keep slide travel inside the guides.
main_risk: Travel. An offset e turned by q moves the cuff end ~2e sin(q/2), so with q up to ~150 deg the transverse offsets must stay under ~4-5 mm (+-8 mm guides), or the motion must be steered along the arm; the hubs gain far less freedom than hoped. The passive stage adds ~6-8 mm of stack under the saddle, plus friction and compliance at the cuff (R17 limits: 5 N and 5 deg at the cuff). A slide that moves the chain end against the arm skin is the R10 problem in reverse.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: the slides run on miniature ball guides (mu ~0.003-0.005) and are driven by the arm through the closure; unique closure, so no sag; hubs are rolling. MVP2: the 3 hubs carry drums and encoders as today; the slides stay passive and unsensed (their position is not needed to know the arm pose).

Arm-fixed vectors: v_H = RH0.T@v_rest. ENV(member, rays): for each member-local ray d and each fit-clip pose taken, the skin radius is the first r >= 30 mm along M(i)@d with B.dist >= 0 (2 mm march, then 0.5 mm bisection); the envelope is the max over poses, and the underside = envelope + 2. 2 mm sampling grid. Self-collision under 1 mm -> None. IK3R on directions: G = Q@Q0.T; Paden-Kahan subproblem 2 for q1, q2, subproblem 1 for q3; singular if |a1 . (a2c x a3c)| < 0.17 -> None. THIS CONCEPT: params axis directions (a1, a2_0, a3_0); axis points c_k = GH + offset perpendicular to a_k (2 params each); cuff attach point Pc (H-local, lateral arm, s 150-200); slide frame (along u, plus two transverse). FK with axis lines: rotating about the line (a, c) maps p -> R(a, q)(p - c) + c, composed through the chain in S-local, then RS applied. Per pose: q from the orientation IK; chain-end point E (fixed on link 3 at the cuff interface) from FK; mismatch delta = RH^T (E - RH@Pc) in the slide frame. Take the pose if |delta_along| <= 40 and |delta_x|, |delta_y| <= 8, else None. Metal: hubs at their placed centres (underside at ENV in their member frame + 2, stack 12.25 for O20 or 9 for a donut); straps between hubs at ENV + 2; slide stack at the cuff (saddle-fixed rail 4-6 mm + block 4 mm, in H at Pc); link 3's end at Pc + delta. Optional first step: girdle.fit_minimax over the clip poses to minimise max |delta_transverse| subject to hubs at ENV + 2 (an LP for fixed directions).
sweep_params: Axis directions (seed: baseline or crown-ring-3r); offsets c_k up to 30 mm; transverse / along travel budgets (5-10 / 25-50 mm); cuff attach station; hub type (O20 v5 vs KAA15 donut); whether the J1 axis line is pinned through GH (offsets only at J2/J3).
prior_art: Self-aligning exoskeleton axes with passive translations (Stienen et al. 2009; Schiele & van der Helm 2006); repo P0 offset-axis minimax LP (pipeline/girdle/girdle.py, p0_results.json).

name: The user's split: 2R donut pointer + shoulder-side wire-race C-slide for humeral twist
topology: S -> J1 R active: KAA10XL0 or KAA15XL0 donut (25.4x34.9x4.76 / 38.1x47.6x4.76) on an S-fixed bracket over the anterior acromion, axis a1 = p* ~ [0.36, 0.72, 0.60] (S-local; the best two-sided pointer pole over the 470 bench poses) -> link 1 (~90 deg arc) -> J2 R active: donut, a2 = +-normalize(a1 x t), i.e. 90 deg from both a1 and the arm -> link 2 = pointing link (follows the arm direction, not its twist), carrying an open C-rail (custom caged-ball wire-race band 26x6 mm; 2 + 6 + 2 = 10 mm stack) on a circle about the humerus axis at station s, radius rho -> J3 R active: arm-fixed 50-60 deg shoe on the rail (humeral axial rotation; 67-87 deg of travel per pipeline/girdle/ring_travel.json) -> shoe neck along the arm -> user's cuff / BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning: A spherical 3R with a3 = the humerus axis: q1 and q2 point the arm, q3 is its twist about its own axis, all fixed by the humerus orientation in closed form. Singular when t is parallel to +-a1; such frames are rejected. No spare joint. Each joint is a rolling element with its own sensor (bore encoders on the donuts, magnetic strip on the rail band) and an MVP2 drive (drums on the donuts, a cable along the rail band).
description: J1 sits on the anterior acromion / lateral clavicle edge. J2 always rides beside the arm, 90 deg off its axis: anterolateral at rest, on the shoulder top overhead. The C-rail wraps the lateral half of the arm root, with the shoe on the arm's lateral side. Overhead the arm comes within 32 deg of J1 (its closest approach), so the deltoid passes right under J1. Across-body, the rail's open side faces the chest. Behind-back, J1 turns ~180 deg and J2 moves posterior.
why_better: This is the user's own suggestion (REQUIREMENTS 2026-10-14: 'put upper arm rotation in its own DOF farther down ... just handle 2 at the shoulder'). Humeral twist no longer swings the hub chain around the shoulder (the sweep principle, pipeline/arm-rom/RESEARCH_NOTES.md section 2): link 2's envelope is only the annulus around the arm root, and only two hubs ride over the shoulder. RESEARCH_NOTES reports family V (two pivots + ideal axial joint) at 67-77 % of a workspace before hardware.
main_risk: Measured today on the bench frames: the best two-sided pointer pole has only 32 deg of margin (p*). ring_travel's clip-optimal pole n = [-0.525, -0.253, 0.812] drops to 14.6 deg on the workspace poses, against 45-55 deg on the clips. p* lies where the overhead arm comes, so J1-deltoid contact overhead is likely. A rail at the deltoid cap needs r >= 82-91 mm to be body-free (pipeline/girdle/ring_roundness.json) against ~55-60 mm of skin: 20+ mm of stand-off unless it moves to s 120-160 (17-21 mm skin spread). The rail is a cantilever (~2 deg twist for a hollow 26x6 band at 25 N.m).
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: rolling (thin sections, caged balls), no spare joint. Cage creep is handled by an anti-creep rack or end-stop re-centring. MVP2: J1/J2 drums cut into the donut ODs (r ~17-24 mm); for J3 a cable runs along the band and wraps the shoe (radius rho); encoders in the donut bores and a magnetic strip on the band.
model_spec: COMMON: fr = B.frames(i); RS, RH = fr['S'][0], fr['H'][0]; GH = origin, so Q = RS.T@RH (S-local = thorax at rest). Humerus axis in H-local: u = normalize(BP._rig().L['elbow']); arm direction t = Q@u. Arm-fixed vectors: v_H = RH0.T@v_rest. ENV(member, rays): for each member-local ray d and each fit-clip pose taken, the skin radius is the first r >= 30 mm along M(i)@d with B.dist >= 0 (2 mm march, then 0.5 mm bisection); the envelope is the max over poses, and the underside = envelope + 2. 2 mm sampling grid. Self-collision under 1 mm -> None. POINTER IK: if angle(t, +-a1) < 15 deg -> None. a2 = s * normalize(a1 x t), with s the branch. Pointing frame P = columns [a2 x t, a2, t] (S-local). q1 = azimuth of a2 about a1 (reference e1 perpendicular to a1); q2 = angle(a1, t). Twist: l_H = RH0.T@[0, 0, 1], made perpendicular to u; v = P.T @ Q @ l_H; q3 = atan2(v_y, v_x). Reject if |wrap(q3 - c)| > T/2. Members: L1 = rotation about a1 by q1, P, arm. Metal: J1 donut on a1 at R1 = ENV_S(a1) + 2 (annulus r 13-17.5 for KAA10 or 19-24 for KAA15, stack 9); J2 donut on a2 at R2 = ENV_L1 + 2; link 1 = great-circle strap a1 -> a2 (14 wide, 3 thick) in L1; link 2 = strap in P from a2 to the rail's mid angle. Rail in P: points s_r t + rho (cos th x_P + sin th y_P) + w t, for w in [-13, 13] and th in [c - T/2 - Ls/2, c + T/2 + Ls/2]. rho = 2 + the max skin radius about the humerus axis over the rail arc and the clip poses at stations s +- 13. Shoe in the arm frame: th = q3 +- Ls/2 at rho + 6..+8. Neck: strap from the shoe's distal edge along the arm, at ENV_arm + 2, to s = 180.
sweep_params: a1 within 15 deg of p*; branch s; J1/J2 radii R1, R2; station s 40-160 mm; rho; window centre c; travel T 60-90 deg; shoe arc Ls 40-60 deg.
prior_art: CADEN-7 humeral C-rail (THK HCR, 3x60 deg); Harmony and MGA (3R humeral rotation); repo P0 '2R shoulder + humeral-rotation ring' (kinematic only); pipeline/arm-rom families V/G (virtual axial joint); docs/research/ring_and_shell_hardware.md.

name: Goniometer pointer: J2 is an arc rail running beside the arm's elevation path, no J2 hub
topology: S -> J1 R active: donut at p* (as in pointer-cslide) -> link 1 = arc rail (wire-race or crossed-roller curved slide, 6 mm band), lying on a small circle about a2 at cone alpha_r = 35-55 deg on one side of the plane through a1 and the arm, fixed to the J1 rotor by a short root -> J2 R active with a VIRTUAL axis a2 = normalize(a1 x t): carriage (40-50 mm shoe) on the rail -> link 2 = carriage + short bridge to the arm root -> J3 R active: humeral C-slide as in pointer-cslide -> cuff.
dof_reasoning: Same 3-DOF spherical kinematics as pointer-cslide: q1 = J1 azimuth, q2 = carriage position along the rail (rotation about the virtual axis a2), q3 = humeral twist, all fixed in closed form by the humerus orientation. No spare coordinate. The rail cage is not a DOF (half speed, anti-creep rack). Each coordinate is sensable and drivable: donut drum + encoder; cable in a band groove + magnetic strip for the carriage and the C-slide.
description: There is no J2 hub. The rail runs alongside the arm's elevation path, 35-55 deg to the front or back of the plane holding the arm and the J1 pole, like a goniometer cradle; the carriage stays level with the arm root and moves with it. At rest the rail runs from the front of the shoulder down beside the arm root. Overhead the carriage sits at the rail's upper end near the crown edge. Across-body and behind-back, J1 turns the whole rail about p*.
why_better: J2's metal moves from a hub held 90 deg off the arm, which always sits on the moving deltoid, to a thin band beside the arm path at whatever cone the skin allows. Link 2 shrinks to a carriage plus a bridge. The rail can go on the side of the arm where the body leaves room (in front for most ADL), and a 6 mm band is lower than any hub.
main_risk: The same 32 deg pole problem as pointer-cslide. A long rail (the q2 range, ~90 deg, plus the shoe) fixed to J1's rotor sweeps around p* with q1 (~190 deg) and must clear the body over that whole sweep. Rail plus carriage stack is ~10-12 mm. The rail is a curved cantilever.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: rolling, anti-creep cage, no spare joint. MVP2: a cable along the rail band to the carriage (Bowden stop at the root); J1 drum on the donut; J3 as in pointer-cslide; magnetic-strip encoders.

Humerus axis in H-local: u = normalize(BP._rig().L['elbow']); arm direction t = Q@u. Arm-fixed vectors: v_H = RH0.T@v_rest. ENV(member, rays): for each member-local ray d and each fit-clip pose taken, the skin radius is the first r >= 30 mm along M(i)@d with B.dist >= 0 (2 mm march, then 0.5 mm bisection); the envelope is the max over poses, and the underside = envelope + 2. 2 mm sampling grid. Self-collision under 1 mm -> None. POINTER IK as in pointer-cslide (t, a2 = s * normalize(a1 x t), P = [a2 x t, a2, t], q1, q2 = angle(a1, t), q3 from the arm-fixed lateral; reject within 15 deg of +-a1 or outside the twist window). L1 = rotation about a1 by q1, in which a2 is fixed: a2_L1. Rail in L1: points R(a2_L1, phi) applied to Rr(phi) * (cos alpha_r * (side * a2_L1) + sin alpha_r * e_t0), where e_t0 = the arm direction at q2 = 0 in the meridian plane, for phi in [q2min - Lc/2, q2max + Lc/2], plus a band of +-13 mm along the circle's binormal. Rr(phi) = ENV_L1 along that ray + 2 (circular variant: the max over phi). Carriage: phi = q2 +- Lc/2 at +6..+9 mm. First pass: the q2 range over all poses; then cut the rail to the chosen percentile and reject poses beyond it.
sweep_params: a1 within 15 deg of p*; branch; rail side (+-a2); alpha_r 30-60 deg; Rr; q2 range cut (percentile); carriage arc Lc 30-50 deg; C-slide station, rho, window c, travel T.
prior_art: Goniometer cradle stages (curved crossed-roller guides); circular-guided RCM mechanisms (Yip et al. 2014); MEDARM curved track; CADEN-7 arcs.

name: Closed thin-section armband at the user's cuff + 2R donut pointer with a lateral spar
topology: S -> J1 R active: donut at p* ~ [0.36, 0.72, 0.60] -> link 1 -> J2 R active: donut, a2 = +-normalize(a1 x t) -> link 2 = a long lateral spar from J2 down the outside of the arm (pointing frame: no twist) -> J3 R active: a CLOSED 4-point thin-section ring coaxial with the humerus axis around the distal upper arm, s = 190-240 mm from GH (RBC/Kaydon KA045XP0 114.3x127x6.35 or KA050XP0 127x139.7x6.35; a KA040XP0 is ~86 g with ~310 N.m static moment). Stator on the spar; rotor bolted into the user's upper-arm cuff / BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning: Spherical 3R with a3 = the humerus axis: two pointing angles and the arm twist, all fixed in closed form by the humerus orientation; singular only for t parallel to +-a1 (rejected). No spare joint. The ring is a single closed rolling bearing: a magnetic-ring encoder and an MVP2 cable drum on its rotor OD.
description: The shoulder carries only two donuts and the strap between them. The spar runs down the lateral arm 8-15 mm off the deltoid to a ring around the arm just above the user's cuff, where the arm is slimmer: 40-50 mm skin radius, so 7-17 mm of gap inside a 57 mm bore radius. Overhead the spar lies along the arm's lateral side. Across-body the ring's medial arc meets the chest. Behind-back it sits between the arm and the trunk.
why_better: A closed ring is a full bearing: no open-rail cantilever, no twist and no cage creep, which are the recurring failures of open humeral rings in exos (research note section 3). Its 6.35 mm section is thinner than any C-slide (~10 mm). The twist joint moves to where the arm is a plain cylinder and where the user's own cuff already sits, and the spar does not twist with the arm.
main_risk: The ring's medial arc between arm and trunk: in the rig the arm touches or enters the torso in walking and wash-opposite-shoulder poses, so adducted poses will count as contact (follow and reach losses). The arm must be threaded through the ring (donning). The spar's gap changes with axial twist over a non-round arm (13.5-25 mm skin-radius spread 80-280 mm down the arm, FINDINGS), so the spar is often over 14 mm. The p* pole limit (32 deg) is the same as in pointer-cslide.
unpowered_and_mvp2: MVP1: rolling throughout (4-point thin section, donuts), no spare joint. Use shielded, not sealed, rings to keep drag under ~0.05 N.m. MVP2: J3 drum = a groove on the rotor OD (r ~64-70 mm, low tension), with the cable led along the spar; J1/J2 as in pointer-cslide.

Metal: J1 and J2 donuts and link 1 as in pointer-cslide. Ring in P, centred at s_r * t: inner cylinder at r_in = bore/2 (57.15 for KA045), axial width 10 mm (s_r +- 5); both side annuli from r_in to r_in + 10 (bearing + housings); the rotor housing in the arm frame (same place). Spar in P: strap 16 wide x 4 thick from J2 to the ring stator at angle c (lateral), underside = 2 + the max skin radius about the humerus axis at that angle over the clip poses (ENV in P). Ring points inside the body are the adduction failure mode: let the bench count them, and also report the share of poses lost to the ring alone.
